Initial Decision 2026-05-20
Problem: Emergency habitat bulkhead closure is currently represented by CPU-side BaseAirlock transform motion, while batch requires mathematical CSR/KCC blocking and GPU-only visual closure.
Solution: Add vault-backed explicit-layout bulkhead state lane, Burst jobs for closure/edge sealing/KCC plane blocking, and shader StructuredBuffer reader for visual "Dear Lie."
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping emergencyBulkheadDoorMesh.localPosition movement is cheap per object but still object-state animation and scales badly across many base doors; adding colliders would churn broadphase and violate prompt.
Scalability potential: Low uses 5 Hz authority integration with shader interpolation; Middle keeps 10-20 Hz; High/Ultra can run denser visual distortion in UberNoir without changing gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: Expected low-end i3/MX350 gain is removal of per-door transform writes, Animator risk, and collider toggles; exact microseconds pending static implementation and profiler proof.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Data Authority Lane
Problem: Emergency bulkhead truth had no unmanaged CSR/KCC lane, so any lock state would be trapped in managed MonoBehaviour state.
Solution: Added BulkheadStateDTO as exact 32-byte explicit layout and registered Shinobu220Bulkhead BufferIDs in H8Memory with Construction ownership.
Rejected Alternatives: Local persistent NativeArray ownership was rejected because Global Authority Boundaries require cross-domain state to live in DataVault. Managed dictionaries were rejected because KCC/rollback cannot memcpy them.
Scalability potential: Low uses 256-state fixed lane with 5 Hz authority; Middle raises cadence smoothly; High/Ultra keep same state truth and spend saved CPU on shader distortion only.
Hardware Impact: Low-end i3/MX350 expected gain is 5-20 us per active door cluster by removing Transform/Animator state as gameplay authority and avoiding broadphase churn.
Decision 2026-05-20 - BaseAirlock Publish-Only Boundary
Problem: BaseAirlock moved emergencyBulkheadDoorMesh.localPosition and played clang as if object was emergency door.
Solution: Removed mesh transform door fields and replaced them with edge hash plus mathematical plane dimensions. BaseAirlock now publishes lock intent to BulkheadContainmentRuntime.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping hidden Transform as visual truth was rejected because it keeps physical-door model alive. Adding disabled collider fallback was rejected because it invites broadphase toggles.
Scalability potential: Low has zero per-frame door Transform writes; Middle keeps pressure whistle logic; High/Ultra render closure through UberNoir with continuous quality.
Hardware Impact: Estimated 2-8 us saved per door per frame on weak CPUs from eliminating localPosition writes and hierarchy dirtiness; more if prefabs previously had animated child graphs.
Decision 2026-05-20 - KCC Plane Result Instead Of Direct KCC Patch
Problem: player controller is separate authority domain, and direct edits risk colliding with Agent 113 work.
Solution: EvaluateDoorCollisionsJob runs in PreSimulation and writes BulkheadCollisionResultDTO to Shinobu220BulkheadCollisionResults; PlayerKinematicsRuntime consumes that data-only result and projects position/velocity out of closed plane. Plane math subtracts AUP doubles before float projection.
Rejected Alternatives: Unity colliders were rejected because closure would require broadphase updates. Direct Construction object references in KCC were rejected; bridge is DataVault-only.
Scalability potential: Low tests only active planes at low cadence; Middle/High increase cadence with HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight; Ultra can widen debug/telemetry without changing solver semantics.
Hardware Impact: Expected gain is 10-40 us per moving door avoided versus BoxCollider/MeshCollider broadphase updates; plane query cost is linear over active bulkheads and fixed-capacity.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Dear Lie Shader Closure
Problem: visual door still needs to read as heavy steel without CPU geometry or physical door object.
Solution: Added GlobalBulkheadStates StructuredBuffer and GlobalBulkheadParams to UberNoir. Vertex deformation uses ClosureProgress to slide/split vertices and distort normals.
Rejected Alternatives: CPU mesh deformation, Animator clips, and instantiated door meshes were rejected because they duplicate gameplay truth and dirty transforms.
Scalability potential: Low uses simple vertical displacement; Middle adds center split; High/Ultra increase ripple/normal distortion through continuous quality weight.
Hardware Impact: Moves visual cost to GPU vertex path; expected CPU saving remains 2-20 us per active bulkhead while GPU cost scales with doorway vertex count and quality.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Black Box And Tooling
Problem: system needs crash explainability, tuning, CSV profiles, and architectural scan without allocating in hot paths.
Solution: Added BulkheadTelemetryEntry300, DumpSHINOBU220.bin writer, UI Toolkit tuner, span-based CSV profile parser, and DoorPhysicsInquisition report route.
Rejected Alternatives: Runtime string CSV parsing and log-only telemetry were rejected; both produce GC or fail black-box requirements.
Scalability potential: Low writes compact telemetry and skips expensive visuals; Middle/High expose live tuning; Ultra can use same telemetry to justify visual overkill.
Hardware Impact: Hot-path telemetry is fixed-size native writes. Dump and CSV file allocations are cold/editor or fault-path only; after Loop 20, empty routes write direct telemetry row and active routes schedule small telemetry job every Simulation frame.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Contract Bridge Instead Of Gameplay Construction Import (SUPERSEDED)
Superseded By: BulkheadContainmentIntentBus unmanaged DataVault ingress in later hardening pass below.
Problem: BaseAirlock and KCC bridge had direct Construction namespace coupling. That is compile-wall risk if Gameplay becomes its own assembly and violates mandate's sibling-runtime isolation intent.
Solution: Moved KCC collision payloads into Hecton8.Core.Contracts and added IBulkheadContainmentPublisher/BulkheadContainmentBridge for cold BaseAirlock lockdown publish. BulkheadContainmentRuntime registers publisher on enable and unregisters on disable.
Rejected Alternatives: new SignalBus lane was rejected because direct signal dispatch is generated/hardcoded in GlobalSignals.cs; adding one safely would touch much broader Core surface. Keeping Gameplay using Hecton8.Construction was rejected because it left obvious dependency smell.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged; this is compile-boundary hardening only. Runtime cost is one cold managed interface call when airlock lockdown changes, not frame loop.
Hardware Impact: No measurable frame gain. gain is iteration-time protection and KCC Burst isolation because hot KCC code now reads only Core contract DTO.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Vault Generation Handles
Problem: runtime still resolved owner-local buffers via direct GetBuffer calls across phases, which can pin stale views and contradict Vault generation-handle addendum in binary ledger.
Solution: Store only VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors for SHINOBU220 owner buffers and resolve transient NativeArrayT views inside phase using them. Gizmo also resolves handles instead of owner GetBuffer.
Rejected Alternatives: Persistent NativeArray fields and legacy VaultBufferHandleT were rejected because DataVault is owner and relocation must be possible. Raw pointer caching was rejected because jobs receive pointers only at schedule time.
Scalability potential: Same data route from weak devices to high-end machines; handle layer allows future DataVault defrag without changing bulkhead math.
Hardware Impact: Removes stale-pointer risk. Runtime cost is metadata resolve per phase, not per element; hot Burst loops still operate over raw pointers.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Catastrophic Integrity Lane
Problem: Catastrophic damage originally read conductivity scalar as fake parent integrity. That made room collapse semantics dishonest and could never represent independent structural failure.
Solution: Added Shinobu220BulkheadModuleIntegrity (72013). BaseAirlock publishes normalized CurrentIntegrity / MaxIntegrity; ApplyCatastrophicDoorDamageJob consumes that lane, sets SiblingNodeHash = 0, marks Destroyed | Jammed | CatastrophicDamage, and clamps visual closure to 0.73.
Rejected Alternatives: Spawning broken door debris or rigidbody wreckage was rejected as physics work. Reusing conductivity was rejected as shadow-state corruption.
Scalability potential: Low uses same scalar, middle/high can add richer shader mangling from flags without adding CPU simulation.
Hardware Impact: One extra float lane read in damage job. Saved path remains collider/debris-free; expected gain is avoiding tens of microseconds of physics/object churn during collapse events.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Split KCC And CSR Thresholds
Problem: first pass sealed CSR at ClosureProgress = 0.5, but assignment only gives 0.5 threshold to KCC solidity. CSR isolation must wait until bulkhead is materially sealed.
Solution: KCC collision remains active at ClosureProgress 0.5; ApplyBulkheadLockJob now drops conductivity/fluid flow only at = 0.95. Damage runs before lock so destroyed bulkheads reopen CSR flow in same authority tick.
Rejected Alternatives: Single shared threshold was rejected because it collapses gameplay feel and logistics truth into one scalar boundary.
Scalability potential: Low tier still integrates at 5 Hz but absolute closure time is preserved through accumulated dt; high/ultra get smoother shader perception without changing thresholds.
Hardware Impact: No added allocations or object work. fix prevents false flood/power isolation while preserving cheap mathematical route.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Unmanaged Intent Bus Hardening
Problem: cold IBulkheadContainmentPublisher bridge removed direct Gameplay-Construction imports, but still left managed interface registration path that looked like ordinary OOP service wiring.
Solution: Replaced it with BulkheadContainmentIntentDTO256 and BulkheadContainmentIntentControlDTO1 in GlobalDataVault. BaseAirlock writes one blittable intent packet through BulkheadContainmentIntentBus; BulkheadContainmentRuntime consumes ring in PreSimulation and then mutates its owner-local state, plane, CSR, and integrity lanes.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing GlobalSignals.cs for one-off typed lane was rejected because generated/hardcoded dispatch tables are wider Core compile-wall risk during parallel batch. Keeping interface bridge was rejected because it preserved managed object dispatch where flat unmanaged packet is enough.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all use same single unmanaged route. Quality still changes authority cadence and shader deformation continuously; intent lane does not create hardware tier branch.
Hardware Impact: No measured frame gain claimed. Cold publish removes interface dispatch and runtime object registration; hot frame cost is unchanged except for write == read cursor check before PreSimulation collision work.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Telemetry Timing Honesty
Problem: LastCpuMicroseconds implied measured Burst execution time, but without completing scheduled handle in-frame runtime can only measure enqueue/schedule cost.
Solution: Renamed value to LastScheduleMicroseconds and tags telemetry rows with ScheduleTimeOnly. Actual Burst execution proof remains pending Unity Profiler/SystemDispatcher timing evidence.
Rejected Alternatives: Calling JobHandle.Complete() for timing was rejected because it would stall dispatcher and violate dependency chaining. Leaving CPU label was rejected as fake proof.
Scalability potential: Low tier still sheds schedule frequency through cadence curve; high/ultra still spend saved CPU on shader detail. metric now accurately describes what is measured.
Hardware Impact: No hot-path cost change. This prevents bad performance decisions based on mislabeled timing data.
Decision 2026-05-20 - No Resurrection After Catastrophic Door Crush
Problem: later BaseAirlock publish could clear Destroyed bit while reasserting lock intent, briefly turning crushed bulkhead back into ordinary jammed blocker before damage job ran again.
Solution: Cold intent consumption now only asserts Active and writes current lock/sibling/plane data; it does not clear Destroyed, Jammed, or CatastrophicDamage. Catastrophic state remains authoritative until dedicated repair/rebuild owner exists.
Rejected Alternatives: Auto-clearing damage on any fresh BaseAirlock publish was rejected because it creates shadow repair fact and can let KCC/CSR observe resurrected door for one frame.
Scalability potential: All tiers keep same deterministic damage state; high/ultra can still render richer mangling through flags without CPU debris.
Hardware Impact: No runtime cost change. fix prevents one-frame authority drift after collapse.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Contracts Assembly Purity
Problem: unmanaged intent DTO file lived in Core/Contracts, but first hardening pass also placed DataVault-writing bus in same file. Hecton8.Core.Contracts.asmdef cannot reference Hecton8.Core.Memory because Core.Memory already imports contracts.
Solution: Left only pure flags/DTOs in BulkheadContainmentContracts.cs and moved BulkheadContainmentIntentBus to Assets/Project/Scripts/Core/BulkheadContainmentIntentBus.cs, which is compiled by root Hecton8.Core asmdef. public namespace remains Hecton8.Core.Contracts, so BaseAirlock call sites do not gain Construction coupling.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding Hecton8.Core.Memory reference to Hecton8.Core.Contracts.asmdef was rejected as circular compile wall. Moving DTOs into Construction was rejected because Gameplay/KCC need sibling-neutral data contract.
Scalability potential: No runtime quality change. Low/Middle/High/Ultra still use one unmanaged DataVault intent route and continuous q-driven authority cadence.
Hardware Impact: Frame hot cost remains 0 us. gain is compile isolation: contracts stay memory-agnostic and DataVault write helper sits in assembly that already owns required dependencies.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Startup Intent Retry Without Registration OOP
Problem: BaseAirlock.OnEnable can fire before DataVault is registered. one-shot publish would silently drop initial locked/unlocked bulkhead intent, leaving CSR/KCC lane stale until next manual state change.
Solution: PublishBulkheadContainmentState now returns success and sets bulkheadContainmentPublishPending on failure. Tick retries with 15-tick countdown only while pending; success clears flag and retry path becomes inactive.
Rejected Alternatives: Reintroducing managed runtime registration callback was rejected because it restores object-service path removed by intent bus. Publishing every tick forever was rejected because it turns boot-order problem into persistent traffic.
Scalability potential: Low tier pays only during boot gaps; Middle/High/Ultra behavior is identical after first accepted intent. mathematical closure lane remains q-driven.
Hardware Impact: Post-success frame cost is zero beyond existing false-branch check. During boot gaps cost is one byte decrement per tick and one DataVault write attempt every 16 ticks per airlock.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Explicit AUP Publish Conversion
Problem: cold publish path still called centerAup.ToAbsoluteDouble3() directly from BaseAirlock and static runtime publish helper. method exists today, but bulkhead route already owns exact AUP arithmetic and should not depend on incidental helper surface during compile-wall-sensitive batch.
Solution: BaseAirlock now uses local ToBulkheadAbsoluteDouble3(in AbsoluteUniversePosition) helper with explicit Grid AbsoluteUniversePosition.CellSizeMeters + Local math. BulkheadContainmentRuntime.TryPublishAirlockBulkheadState now calls BulkheadContainmentMath.ToAbsoluteDouble3(in centerAup), same helper used by Burst-side plane/KCC code.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving instance helper call was rejected because it hides AUP conversion dependency behind method outside bulkhead route. Moving helper into Core.Contracts was rejected because it would expand contract surface during parallel integration.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged; this is deterministic coordinate hygiene only. Shader quality and authority cadence remain driven by continuous GlobalQualityWeight.
Hardware Impact: Hot-frame impact is 0 us. Cold publish still performs three double multiplies/adds and writes one unmanaged intent packet; no managed allocation or object route is introduced.
Decision 2026-05-20 - GPU Upload Double Buffer And Dirty Gate
Problem: Dear Lie shader upload path used one GraphicsBuffer and uploaded bulkhead DTO payload every VisualSync even when state hash had not changed. LockBufferForWrite avoided managed staging, but route still risked GPU/driver synchronization and wasted PCIe or unified-memory bandwidth.
Solution: BulkheadContainmentRuntime now owns two persistent shader buffers, shaderStateBufferA and shaderStateBufferB, with byte read/write slots instead of managed array. VisualSync writes only inactive slot, flips it into read slot after successful UnsafeUtility.MemCpy, and binds that read buffer globally. Uploads are gated by telemetry StateHash plus uploadCount; unchanged states skip StructuredBuffer write and only update GlobalBulkheadParams.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping single buffer was rejected because CPU writes can contend with GPU read timeline. Using GraphicsBuffer.SetData was rejected because project bandwidth discipline requires LockBufferForWrite with direct memcpy. GraphicsBuffer wrapper was rejected to avoid introducing private managed array field just to hold two stable slots.
Scalability potential: Low tier benefits most because authority cadence collapses toward 5 Hz, so most visual frames reuse last state buffer while shader params still move continuously. Middle keeps reduced upload frequency proportional to actual state changes. High/Ultra still get full visual deformation when state changes, but do not waste bandwidth on identical DTO payloads.
Hardware Impact: Unchanged VisualSync frames avoid 32 bytes uploadCount payload traffic. At 256 rows this is 8192 bytes per skipped frame, which matters on MX350/Quest unified-memory pressure. Exact frame-time delta remains pending Unity profiler/Frame Debugger proof.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Shader Global Fail-Closed Gate
Problem: After valid upload, GlobalBulkheadParams.y could remain active if shader upload was later disabled, Vault generation-handle resolution failed, read buffer was missing, or EnsureGraphicsBuffers() released buffers before failed recreate. That leaves visual-only stale bulkhead route even though owner Vault truth is unavailable.
Solution: Added shaderGlobalsActive and DisableShaderGlobals(). VisualSync calls it on disabled upload, Vault failures, invalid resolved arrays, or missing read buffer; shutdown and ReleaseGraphicsBuffers() call it before freeing buffers. function writes GlobalBulkheadParams = Vector4.zero, clears valid-read flag, and marks upload dirty for next successful activation.
Rejected Alternatives: Clearing StructuredBuffer binding itself was rejected because Shader.SetGlobalBuffer null semantics are Unity-version-sensitive and unnecessary; shader already guards on GlobalBulkheadParams.y. Leaving stale params until next successful VisualSync was rejected because allocation failure and disabled upload are exactly frames where no later overwrite is guaranteed.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged while valid. Under thermal or editor-driven upload disable, shader collapses to cheapest no-op path through existing enabled = 0 branch with no binary quality tier branch.
Hardware Impact: Enabled hot path adds one bool store after SetGlobalVector; disabled/failure path emits one global vector write only on active-to-inactive transition. It prevents stale GPU vertex deformation and avoids per-frame zero-global spam.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Zero-Active Visual Bypass
Problem: VisualSyncTick still resolved Vault state and created double GraphicsBuffer lanes before discovering there were no active bulkhead owner rows. previous uploadCount = 1 clamp was correct for buffer indexing but wrong for empty scenes because it kept shader route enabled with no mathematical door truth.
Solution: Added activeCount = 0 guard immediately after upload-enabled check. Empty scenes call DisableShaderGlobals() and return before Vault resolution or graphics buffer creation. Valid active scenes keep existing double-buffered upload and state-hash gate.
Rejected Alternatives: Uploading row zero as sentinel was rejected because it wastes GPU branch work and can keep visual proof artifact active without owner fact. Scanning BulkheadStateDTO array in VisualSync to find active rows was rejected because it moves owner truth discovery onto main/render phase; activeCount is already cold owner row bound.
Scalability potential: Low tier gets largest benefit because no active base bulkheads means no shader-buffer allocation or vertex branch at all. Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged once bulkhead owner row exists, and continuous q still drives cadence and deformation.
Hardware Impact: Avoids allocating two GraphicsBuffer objects of 256 32 bytes each in empty scenes and removes per-vertex bulkhead enabled path until real owner row exists. Runtime proof remains pending Unity profiler/Frame Debugger.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Zero-Active KCC Job Bypass
Problem: PreSimulationTick still scheduled EvaluateDoorCollisionsJob with Count = 0 just to clear single KCC collision result row when no bulkhead owner rows existed. That preserved dispatcher job and active-job registration for inactive mathematical route.
Solution: Reset pre-simulation handle/scheduled flag at phase entry, then after unmanaged intent ingestion compute bounded active count once. If it is zero, clear Shinobu220BulkheadCollisionResults0 and return before override or collision jobs are scheduled.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping zero-count Burst job was rejected because it spends scheduler overhead to do one scalar clear. Moving clear into KCC was rejected because bulkhead containment owns collision proof artifact and KCC must only consume it.
Scalability potential: Low tier and empty-start scenes pay no bulkhead PreSimulation schedule until real owner row exists. Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged after activation; continuous quality still controls authority cadence and shader deformation.
Hardware Impact: Saves one IJob schedule and one H8Memory.RegisterActiveJob call per empty PreSimulation tick. Exact microseconds remain profiler-pending, but this removes avoidable main-thread scheduler traffic on weak CPUs.
Decision 2026-05-20 - KCC Stale Frame Fence
Problem: PlayerKinematicsRuntime.TryApplyBulkheadCollisionResult accepted any blocked collision row if depth was finite and positive. If PreSimulation failed to refresh result, KCC could reuse stale closed-door proof beyond frame it was generated for.
Solution: Add one-frame freshness fence using result.Frame. This was immediately hardened in next decision to source current frame from SystemDispatcher.CurrentFrameId, not Time.frameCount. Rows with frame zero, future frames, or age greater than one dispatcher frame are ignored.
Rejected Alternatives: Clearing stale rows from KCC was rejected because containment owns proof artifact; KCC must not mutate bulkhead lane. Leaving row unbounded was rejected because stale collision is worse than one-frame missed block.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged for fresh rows. On weak devices under phase skip or temporary Vault failure, stale data collapses to no-op consumption instead of blocking movement indefinitely.
Hardware Impact: Adds one uint read and three integer comparisons on KCC consumption path. It prevents persistent false-positive KCC correction without allocating memory or touching physics colliders.
Decision 2026-05-20 - KCC Dispatcher Frame Fence
Problem: first stale-row fence used Time.frameCount in new SHINOBU220 critical correction path. Even though surrounding legacy KCC code still uses Unity frame counters, this route must not add more local Unity-time dependency to rollback-sensitive bulkhead blocking.
Solution: Compare BulkheadCollisionResultDTO.Frame against SystemDispatcher.CurrentFrameId and reject dispatcher frame zero, future result rows, or rows older than one dispatcher frame.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Unity frame check was rejected because bulkhead row is produced by dispatcher-phase PreSimulation, so its freshness proof should use same dispatcher frame spine. Reading or mutating collision row from KCC was rejected because containment owns proof artifact.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged for fresh rows; phase-skipped or stale rows collapse to cheap no-op regardless of quality weight.
Hardware Impact: Hot cost remains one static uint read and integer comparisons. No allocations, no collider work, no cross-domain Construction reference.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Static Scan Wording Correction
Problem: verification wording said forbidden-pattern scans had no hits in owned files, but editor-only DoorPhysicsInquisition scanner intentionally contains BoxCollider, MeshCollider, and Animator string literals as signatures to detect illegal door-object code. That wording was imprecise and could be read as hiding scanner hit.
Solution: Re-run scan on runtime/core/shader files separately, record that it has zero hits, and explicitly document editor scanner literals as intentional cold/editor detection signatures.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing scanner string literals was rejected because it would blind Task 19's inquisition report. Calling editor literals runtime dependencies was rejected because they are not executed in gameplay and do not introduce colliders, Animator paths, or Transform door motion.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra runtime behavior is unchanged; this is evidence hygiene only.
Hardware Impact: Hot cost remains 0 us. editor scan remains cold tooling and does not allocate in gameplay.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Vault Hot-Swap Release Discipline
Problem: generation-handle migration removed persistent NativeArray ownership, but runtime still needed explicit cold lifecycle path for DataVault replacement and teardown. Without release calls, hot reload or registry service replacement could leave stale generation descriptors and Vault ref counts alive after owner route is inert. Releasing immediately is also unsafe because scheduled Burst jobs hold raw pointers into old Vault until their handles finish.
Solution: BulkheadContainmentRuntime now registers as GlobalRegistry hot-swap listener, handles DataVault slot through ref-forwarding callback, disables shader globals immediately, releases graphics buffers immediately, stores pending Vault, and refuses to resolve stale Vault while rebind is pending. TryFlushPendingDataVaultRebind() releases all 16 SHINOBU220 Vault generation handles only after preSimulationHandle.IsCompleted and simulationHandle.IsCompleted; it then reacquires from current Vault through normal EnsureVaultState() path. editor gizmo normal conversion was also made explicit from float3 to Vector3 to remove compile-risk dependency on implicit conversion operators.
Rejected Alternatives: Polling GlobalRegistry.DataVault per phase was rejected because registry polling belongs to boot/rebind paths, not hot execution. Clearing handles without IDataVault.ReleaseBuffer was rejected because it hides ownership leaks. Calling JobHandle.Complete() before release was rejected because it would stall dispatcher. Immediate release on registry callback was rejected because it can free memory still referenced by scheduled jobs.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra gameplay behavior is unchanged. Under editor hot reload or Vault replacement, shader route fails closed with GlobalBulkheadParams = 0 and no stale visual proof. Once reacquired, continuous GlobalQualityWeight again controls cadence and deformation.
Hardware Impact: Hot-frame cost remains 0 us outside pending rebind. Cold replacement pays two job-handle completion checks, up to 16 release calls, and two graphics-buffer releases at most, avoiding persistent native memory pressure on weak devices while preventing use-after-free of old Vault memory.
Decision 2026-05-20 - PreSimulation Fence Ownership
Problem: pre-simulation collision job was scheduled from void dispatcher phase. It was only combined into returned Simulation handle when slower authority cadence fired. On cadence-skip frames, job could be active without being returned to central Simulation fence, which weakens KCC freshness and makes deferred Vault release rely on handle dispatcher did not necessarily complete.
Solution: ScheduleSimulation() now creates dependency from preSimulationHandle before cadence checks. Every early exit returns that dependency, so central dispatcher owns pre-simulation job even when no authority closure update is due. Pending DataVault rebind reset preserves scheduled flags until that Simulation phase can collect handle, then clears them only after deferred Vault release is flushed. full closure/CSR/telemetry chain still appends to same dependency when cadence fires.
Rejected Alternatives: Completing pre-simulation handle locally was rejected because it would stall main thread and violate dispatcher-owned fence model. Moving KCC collision into slower authority job was rejected because KCC blocking must be refreshed on PreSimulation cadence, not only on closure authority cadence.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior remains continuous. Low quality still skips expensive authority updates by cadence, but cheap collision proof is fenced correctly; high/ultra still run smoother closure updates without changing KCC semantics.
Hardware Impact: Adds one conditional JobHandle.CombineDependencies only on frames with scheduled pre-simulation job. This buys deterministic ownership and prevents unsafe old-Vault release without adding colliders or blocking waits.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Teardown Drain And Idempotent Shutdown
Problem: After deferred Vault release hardening, OnDisable unregistered dispatcher phases before requesting DataVault rebind. If SHINOBU220 job was still active, TryFlushPendingDataVaultRebind() correctly refused to free raw-pointer memory, but no later phase was guaranteed to run and clear pending Vault release. system was use-after-free safe but could retain Vault references during shutdown.
Solution: Added ShutdownRuntime(forceCompletePendingJobs: true) and routed both OnDisable and Application.quitting through it. Shutdown is idempotent, unregisters callbacks once, drains only scheduled SHINOBU220 handles through DispatcherJobFence.TryComplete(..., forceComplete: true), then calls same pending rebind/release path. Application.quitting no longer calls OnDisable() manually.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping deferred release with no remaining phase pump was rejected as cold native-memory retention risk. Immediate ReleaseBuffer without draining handles was rejected because Burst jobs may still own raw pointers. Manually invoking OnDisable() from quit callback was rejected because lifecycle recursion hides ordering and can double-run partial cleanup.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra gameplay behavior is unchanged. drain is cold teardown only; runtime cadence and shader deformation still scale continuously from 5 Hz authority on weak devices to high-frequency visual overkill on strong machines.
Hardware Impact: Frame-loop cost is 0 us. Teardown may wait on at most active SHINOBU220 pre-simulation and simulation handles; that is explicit shutdown boundary, not gameplay-frame wait.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Every-Frame Black Box Telemetry
Problem: first telemetry implementation wrote 300-frame ring only when authority closure cadence fired. At low GlobalQualityWeight, authority can collapse toward 5 Hz, which means black box could miss multiple dispatcher frames immediately before fatal NaN or shutdown fault.
Solution: ScheduleSimulation() now records telemetry on every Simulation phase. expensive closure, catastrophic damage, and CSR lock jobs remain behind continuous cadence gate. On cadence-skip frames, only states/collision/telemetry/cursor buffers resolve and RecordBulkheadTelemetryJob writes black-box row. If no bulkheads are active, runtime writes direct zero telemetry row and schedules no no-op job.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping telemetry at authority cadence was rejected because it weakens crash autopsy proof. Scheduling whole closure chain every frame was rejected because it violates continuous scalability. Resolving CSR/conductivity/fluid/integrity just to write telemetry was rejected because it increases failure surface and Vault metadata traffic on cadence-skip frames.
Scalability potential: Low tier preserves 5 Hz closure authority while retaining 60 Hz black-box observability; middle/high/ultra keep smoother authority cadence and same every-frame forensic ring. visual Dear Lie remains shader-driven by q.
Hardware Impact: Empty scenes pay one direct NativeArray row write and no scheduled job. Active scenes pay one small IJob schedule per Simulation frame for telemetry; closure/CSR chain still sheds work continuously based on GlobalQualityWeight.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Telemetry Length And Pending-Producer Guards
Problem: Every-frame telemetry introduced more frequent writes to 300-frame ring, but first hardening pass still assumed fixed-size Vault lanes were nonzero and that empty-route direct write could never overlap pending PreSimulation producer. hot-swap, partial Vault failure, or future call-site drift could turn that into modulo-zero fault or data race on collision proof row.
Solution: ScheduleSimulation(), ScheduleTelemetryJob(), and VisualSyncTick() now reject empty state/collision/telemetry/cursor lanes before unsafe pointer extraction or cursor modulo. If active count resolves to zero while preSimulationScheduled is still true, runtime schedules zero-count telemetry job chained behind pre-sim dependency instead of writing ring directly. RecordBulkheadTelemetryJob also exits on invalid pointer/count inputs before reading Cursor0 or CollisionResult0.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting boot-time fixed-capacity requests was rejected because DataVault hot-swap can invalidate assumptions. Forcing all empty routes through no-op telemetry job was rejected because normal inactive scenes should remain scheduler-inert. Completing pre-sim handle before direct write was rejected because it would block frame loop.
Scalability potential: Low tier keeps cheap direct empty-route row and low closure cadence. Middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged; only extra path is rare dependency-correct telemetry job when pending producer must be fenced.
Hardware Impact: Normal active path pays integer length checks before scheduling telemetry. Normal empty path remains one direct row and no job. Rare pending-producer empty path pays one tiny IJob to avoid race; no object, collider, or physics route is introduced.
Decision 2026-05-20 - BaseAirlock Bulkhead Shadow State Purge
Problem: BaseAirlock still kept bulkheadClosureIntent01, local float shadow of closure intent used only to gate pressure whistle. It was not gameplay-authoritative, but name and scalar preserved object-door semantics beside Vault-owned BulkheadStateDTO truth.
Solution: Removed bulkheadClosureIntent01 and SetBulkheadClosureIntent. Audio whistle gating now uses emergencyLockedDown only; closure progress remains owned exclusively by containment Vault lane and shader upload route.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping audio-only float was rejected because shadow state is exactly how standard door objects creep back in. Reading BulkheadStateDTO from Gameplay for audio was rejected because it would add cross-owner polling and DataVault read to cosmetic path.
Scalability potential: Low tier avoids one more local scalar branch and preserves no-object model. Middle/high/ultra still get same shader Dear Lie and continuous q-driven closure cadence from owner runtime.
Hardware Impact: Removes two cold writes and one scalar read in whistle gating. measurable gain is negligible; authority gain is that closure progress exists in one owner route only.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Black-Box Dump Before Shader Fail-Closed Branches
Problem: RecordBulkheadTelemetryJob can mark DumpRequested, but previous dump call lived after successful shader buffer resolution and upload. If shader upload was disabled or failed closed because visual route was inactive, black-box file would not be written even though solver requested forensic output.
Solution: Added DumpBlackBoxIfRequested(IDataVault) and call it at start of VisualSyncTick() after Vault rebind handling, before uploadShaderBuffer, active-count, and graphics-buffer checks. helper resolves only telemetry and cursor lanes, validates nonzero lengths, reads latest ring row, and emits dump when DumpRequested is set.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping dump behind shader upload path was rejected because crash evidence must not depend on visual feature enablement. Completing telemetry job immediately in Simulation was rejected because it would stall frame. Leaving both old and new dump checks was rejected because it could double-write same flagged row.
Scalability potential: Low tier can disable or fail-close shader upload and still preserve fatal telemetry. Middle/high/ultra keep same Dear Lie visual path; forensic output is now orthogonal to visual quality.
Hardware Impact: Adds one telemetry/cursor descriptor resolve and latest-row flag check per VisualSync. Fault-path file I/O remains gated by DumpRequested; no collider, object, or physics route is introduced.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Duplicate Black-Box Dump Fence
Problem: After decoupling dump emission from shader upload, persistent latest telemetry row with DumpRequested could rewrite same dump file every VisualSync until cursor advanced. That keeps evidence correct but creates avoidable fault-path file I/O during already unstable frame sequence.
Solution: Added lastDumpedTelemetryCursor, reset with Vault runtime state, and skip dump emission when latest cursor value was already written. fence is diagnostic-only and does not mutate telemetry ring or gameplay authority.
Rejected Alternatives: Letting same flagged row dump repeatedly was rejected as avoidable I/O churn. Storing "dumped" bit inside telemetry was rejected because forensic rows should remain raw solver evidence.
Scalability potential: Low tier and upload-disabled routes avoid repeated file writes during fault. Middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged; visual quality remains separate from forensic output.
Hardware Impact: Adds one uint comparison before fault-path I/O. In repeated-fault frames it saves full .h8dump rewrite cost.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Hot-Loop DataVault Registry Poll Purge
Problem: BulkheadContainmentRuntime.ResolveVault() still fell back to GlobalRegistry.DataVault when vault was null. That made phase ticks capable of registry polling after Vault loss or boot-order gaps, violating "cache during boot/rebind, no registry in hot execution" rule.
Solution: Removed fallback lookup from ResolveVault(). Runtime phases now use only cached vault reference, and DataVault replacement is handled by existing hot-swap callbacks plus deferred handle release. OnEnable remains cold bootstrap cache point, and static airlock ingress facade remains cold publish helper outside Burst/job math.
Rejected Alternatives: Polling every PreSimulation/Simulation/VisualSync phase until Vault appears was rejected because it hides service-order problems in hot code. Moving Gameplay directly onto BulkheadContainmentRuntime was rejected because it would reintroduce Gameplay-Construction dependency.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged while Vault is present. When Vault is absent or rebinding, containment route fails inert, disables shader globals, and waits for hot-swap rebind instead of escalating work.
Hardware Impact: No normal-frame speed claim. change removes failure-path registry read from phase ticks and closes authority-boundary violation without adding allocations, colliders, or object state.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Airlock Registry Publish Purge
Problem: BaseAirlock.PublishBulkheadContainmentState still read GlobalRegistry.DataVault during cold publish and bounded retry. It was not Burst math, but retry call lives in Tick, so route still had service-locator read in gameplay update path.
Solution: Added cached-Vault overload to BulkheadContainmentIntentBus. BulkheadContainmentRuntime binds that cache during OnEnable and every DataVault hot-swap/rebind. BaseAirlock now publishes through bus cache and no longer references DataVault directly.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding Core.Memory.IDataVault field to BaseAirlock was rejected because Gameplay should not own Vault service references. Reintroducing managed Construction publisher was rejected because it revives OOP service wiring. Editing generated SignalBus tables was rejected as broader Core compile-wall risk.
Scalability potential: Low tier retry remains bounded and now fails fast when no cached Vault exists. Middle/high/ultra use same unmanaged intent route; continuous GlobalQualityWeight still controls authority cadence and shader deformation.
Hardware Impact: Removes service-locator read from airlock retry path. No allocation, collider, Animator, or Transform-door route was introduced.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Intent Bus No-Allocation Resolve
Problem: BulkheadContainmentIntentBus.TryWriteAirlockBulkheadIntent still used GetGenerationHandle for intent ring and control row. Even though bus is cold ingress helper, that allowed Gameplay publish/retry to create or grow Construction-owned Vault lanes before owner runtime bootstrapped them.
Solution: Switched publish path to explicit TryGetGenerationHandleT calls followed by transient TryResolveHandle. If Construction owner has not created descriptors yet, bus returns false and existing bounded airlock retry remains active.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping GetGenerationHandle in bus was rejected because allocation authority belongs to BulkheadContainmentRuntime.EnsureVaultState. Forcing all SHINOBU Vault lanes to allocate in OnEnable was rejected because dispatcher bootstrap/rebind already owns lazy creation path and fail-inert retry is cheaper during boot-order gaps.
Scalability potential: Low tier avoids accidental Vault growth from many airlocks during scene activation. Middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged after owner bootstrap; same unmanaged ring carries intents and continuous GlobalQualityWeight controls solver cadence.
Hardware Impact: Removes allocation/grow/ref-count risk from publish path. In pre-owner window, cost collapses to two descriptor lookup failures and one false return instead of lane creation.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Intent Bus Rebind Inert Window
Problem: DataVault hot-swap could bind airlock intent bus to replacement Vault before old SHINOBU jobs had drained and before old generation handles were released. That left window where Gameplay could publish fresh intent packets into new Vault while owner runtime still held old raw-pointer handles.
Solution: RequestDataVaultRebind() now binds intent bus to null during pending rebind, disables shader globals, releases graphics buffers, resets runtime state without clearing scheduled flags, and waits for tracked handles. TryFlushPendingDataVaultRebind() releases old handles, commits vault = pendingVault, then rebinds bus cache.
Rejected Alternatives: Binding bus to replacement Vault immediately was rejected because publish authority would move before pointer ownership was settled. Dropping same-service callbacks into null bus was rejected because it would create false retry storm during benign registry refresh.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged after rebind. During rebind window, publish fails inert and shader route is disabled rather than doing speculative work.
Hardware Impact: Hot-frame cost is one branch only during rebind. It prevents stale-pointer ownership ambiguity without adding main-thread completion wait.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Dispatched Mock Generation
Problem: GenerateMockBulkheadsJob had required Burst attributes but runtime invoked it through managed for loop calling job.Execute(i) during Vault setup. That bypasses Burst scheduling and weakens fallback mock generator required for isolated CI/profile runs.
Solution: Removed setup-time GenerateMockData loop. ScheduleSimulation() now schedules GenerateMockBulkheadsJob through Schedule(count, 32, dependency) when mock mode is enabled, no mock was generated, and no real bulkhead row exists. returned handle flows into telemetry/closure dependency chaining, so dispatcher owns completion.
Rejected Alternatives: Calling Complete() immediately after mock schedule was rejected because it would add gameplay-frame barrier. Seeding mock rows after real airlock intents was rejected because it could overwrite live edge hashes, AUP planes, and CSR metadata. Keeping direct Execute(i) was rejected because it is not Burst profiled path.
Scalability potential: Low tier pays no mock job once real airlocks publish. Middle/high/ultra test scenes still get deterministic synthetic rows, and continuous GlobalQualityWeight controls closure cadence after mock rows exist.
Hardware Impact: Removes managed setup loop from mock route and moves work into dispatcher job graph. Normal production scenes with real airlock ingress pay 0 us for mock generation.
Decision 2026-05-20 - CSV Scratch File Ingest
Problem: CSV parser was allocation-free once handed ReadOnlySpanbyte, but UI Toolkit facade still called File.ReadAllBytes, allocating managed byte and leaving Vault-owned Shinobu220BulkheadCsvScratch lane unused.
Solution: Added TryLoadProfilesFromCsvFile(string path) on BulkheadContainmentRuntime. It resolves profiles lane and CSV scratch byte lane, reads file directly into native scratch buffer using FileStream.Read(Spanbyte), and parses ReadOnlySpanbyte over native pointer. editor window now calls that file-ingest bridge instead of File.ReadAllBytes.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping editor byte staging was rejected because task explicitly requires zero-GC span parser and route already owns Vault scratch lane. Parsing oversized files partially was rejected; ingest returns false if file exceeds scratch capacity. Managed dictionaries and string.Split remain rejected because hashes and floats are parsed directly from bytes.
Scalability potential: Low tier and editor-on-device workflows avoid temporary managed CSV blobs. Middle/high/ultra designer workflows can hot-load profiles without recompiling C# while preserving same continuous quality/cadence math.
Hardware Impact: Cold/editor file import removes one managed allocation sized to CSV file. Gameplay hot-frame impact is 0 us.
Decision 2026-05-20 - SignalBus Manual Override Route
Problem: BulkheadContainmentRuntime.PreSimulationTick read BufferID.InteractionSignalQueue as NativeArrayInteractionUiSignal, but that Vault lane is owned by GameplayTools as InteractionSignal. That was both type/owner collision and persistence risk: stable queue row could toggle AssociatedLock every frame.
Solution: Removed Vault queue read. PreSimulation now reads current SignalBusInteractionUiSignal frame snapshot, scans bounded 32-row window for ToolHash == BulkheadContainmentConstants.OverrideToolHash, and schedules ProcessDoorOverrideJob only when matching override exists. job itself also filters tool hash and uses read-only NativeArray snapshot.
Rejected Alternatives: Reusing InteractionSignalQueue as bulkhead UI lane was rejected because lane has different owner and DTO type. Always scheduling serial override job was rejected because it creates tiny same-frame job without signal proof. Draining GlobalSignals.TryDequeueInteractionUi was rejected because typed SignalBus snapshot is first-party hot broadcast route.
Scalability potential: Low tier pays zero override job cost on normal frames. Middle/high/ultra keep deterministic manual override while richer visual closure stays in shader.
Hardware Impact: Ordinary frames save one serial IJob schedule and one wrong-lane Vault resolve. Override frames still pay tiny chained IJob to preserve dependency safety without Complete().
Decision 2026-05-20 - Bootstrap Versus Hot Refresh
Problem: EnsureVaultState() could create SHINOBU Vault handles from PreSimulation, Simulation, or VisualSync because hot phases called same method that used GetGenerationHandle.
Solution: Split path into BootstrapVaultState() for cold owner allocation/rebind commit/editor profile loading, and RefreshVaultState() for dispatcher phases. Hot phases now resolve and validate existing generation handles and write tuning proof row; they do not create or grow Vault lanes.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving lazy allocation in phase entry was rejected because it turns DataVault into hot global heap. Duplicating handle fields for preallocated pending Vaults was rejected as unnecessary state expansion for rare rebind path.
Scalability potential: All tiers use same fixed Vault lanes. Weak devices fail inert if bootstrap is absent instead of doing surprise allocation; high/ultra visual overkill remains shader-driven.
Hardware Impact: No measured speed claim. change removes allocation/ref-count risk and DataVault growth from dispatcher phase entry.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Burst Pointer Fail Gates And Provenance
Problem: Several SHINOBU unsafe-pointer jobs trusted caller guards. future direct invocation, partial Vault failure, or hot-swap drift could dereference null or zero-length inputs. Collision no-hit rows also returned Frame = 0, weakening KCC freshness proof.
Solution: Added in-job pointer/count guards to mock generation, closure update, CSR lock, manual override, KCC collision, and catastrophic damage jobs. EvaluateDoorCollisionsJob now stamps current frame even on no-hit rows and uses epsilon for plane crossing rather than exact float-zero checks.
Rejected Alternatives: Caller-only validation was rejected because Burst jobs are reusable kernels and must be self-vaccinating. Exact zero crossing was rejected because deterministic epsilon is cheaper than NaN-adjacent edge case.
Scalability potential: Guard cost is constant across low/middle/high/ultra. actual closure cadence remains controlled by continuous GlobalQualityWeight.
Hardware Impact: Adds small fixed branch block at job entry. Prevents invalid pointer reads without adding main-thread completion or managed allocation.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Native DTO Layout Guard Expansion
Problem: layout guard proved only BulkheadStateDTO, while BulkheadPlaneDTO, BulkheadCsrEdgeDTO, BulkheadTuningDTO, BulkheadProfileDTO, and BulkheadTelemetryEntry also move through Vault/Burst/shader-adjacent routes.
Solution: Expanded BulkheadStateLayoutGuard.ValidateLayout() to check size and offsets for every SHINOBU native DTO. Added explicit constants for max intent age and plane crossing epsilon.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting StructLayout declarations without runtime/editor proof was rejected because ARM64 padding mistakes are silent until they become corrupted math.
Scalability potential: Layout is invariant across hardware tiers; quality changes cadence/visual fidelity, not DTO shape or authority identity.
Hardware Impact: Cold validation only. Hot-frame cost is 0 us after layoutChecked is set.
Decision 2026-05-20 - Shader Index Sanitization And Continuous Normalization
Problem: bulkhead Dear Lie shader cast GlobalBulkheadParams.x and UberNoirInstanceParams.x to uint without finite guards, and normalization helper used by bulkhead deformation still contained compile-time MATHLODLOW branch.
Solution: Guarded and clamped both index-driving floats before uint casts. Replaced binary normalization branch with continuous blend from cheap axis approximation to precise rsqrt based on global/material quality weight.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting C# upload counts was rejected because shader globals can outlive or be corrupted independently. Keeping MATHLODLOW in bulkhead path was rejected because it creates hard binary quality mode in visual algorithm that already has continuous q.
Scalability potential: Low tier leans toward axis approximation; middle tiers blend; high/ultra use precise rsqrt-heavy normals. Visual quality scales smoothly without changing gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: Low quality avoids part of expensive normalization visually through blending. High quality spends ALU on better normals. CPU cost remains 0 us.
Decision 2026-05-20 - UberNoir Compile-Time LOD Purge
Problem: Static scan still found MATHLODLOW forks in shared UberNoir shader after bulkhead-specific normalization fix. SHINOBU's bulkhead Dear Lie runs through this shader, so compile-time low/high variants could keep visual behavior binary even while C# authority path is continuous.
Solution: Removed every MATHLODLOW branch from Hecton8UberNoir.hlsl. Brownout, dither, hull bending, wake deformation, biolum emission, caustics, main lighting, extinction, refraction, and vertex extinction now consume H8UberNoirGlobalQualityWeight, smooth quality ramps, step, and existing runtime feature gates. Gameplay DTOs and Vault ownership were not changed.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving shared shader branches in place was rejected because it preserves compile-time quality dichotomy. Moving change into C# was rejected because these effects are visual fakes and should stay GPU-side. Removing high-end effects outright was rejected because high/ultra tiers must spend saved CPU on visual overkill.
Scalability potential: Low tier uses cheap dither, reduced wake slot budgets, suppressed hull bending/biolum/refraction detail, and cheap extinction/lighting contribution through quality weights. Middle tier blends into richer caustics, shadows, and wake curl. High/ultra enables fuller shader detail without changing bulkhead closure truth, save identity, or KCC collision state.
Hardware Impact: CPU cost remains 0 us. GPU work now scales by continuous uniforms instead of shader variant forks; low tiers suppress expensive contribution through quality gates, while high tiers intentionally spend ALU/texture samples for visual overkill.
Decision 2026-05-21 - UberNoir Runtime Cost Collapse After Macro Purge
Problem: Removing MATHLODLOW eliminated binary variant split, but static review found masked work still executing: global wakes always iterated 16 lanes, main lighting still built shadow coordinates before quality detail opened, extinction always invoked richer world resolver, and cavitation refraction paid sqrt/sin per shockwave once refraction feature was active.
Solution: Converted those masked paths into runtime cost collapse. Wake deformation now loops only to quality-scaled slot count. Main lighting uses no-shadow/no-specular cheap path while detailWeight is zero, then transitions to shadow/specular/caustic path as smooth ramp opens. Extinction returns vertex-resolved cheap color until richer LUT ramp is nonzero. Cavitation refraction uses squared-radius shell and triangle-wave curl below rich band; sine curl and precise shell blend only above detail threshold.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping masked 16-lane work was rejected because zero contribution is not zero cost. Reintroducing MATHLODLOW was rejected because compile-time dichotomies are forbidden. Removing wakes/refraction/caustics outright was rejected because high and ultra tiers must buy visible depth with saved budget.
Scalability potential: Low tier evaluates one wake lane, cheap light, cheap extinction, and squared-shell cavitation. Middle tier increases wake/shockwave slots and blends in precise shells/shadows. High/ultra tiers restore all 16 wake lanes, rich caustic noise, shadow attenuation, and trig curl without changing BulkheadStateDTO, Vault ownership, save identity, or KCC collision proof.
Hardware Impact: CPU cost is 0 us. GPU low-tier vertex/motion/shadow wake work drops from 16 lane iterations to 1 lane before active wake count. Fragment low-tier avoids shadow-coordinate/main-light shadow sampling and extinction rich resolver until quality ramps open. Cavitation low-tier avoids sin and true distance shell math.
Decision 2026-05-21 - KCC Snapshot Fail-Inert Guard
Problem: PreSimulationTick() ignored boolean result from TryResolvePlayerState(). If Kinematics Vault snapshot was absent, collision job still ran against playerAup = double3.zero, which could create false blocked bulkhead rows near world origin and poison collision proof lane.
Solution: When TryResolvePlayerState() fails, PreSimulationTick() now writes no-hit BulkheadCollisionResultDTO stamped with current dispatcher frame and returns before scheduling EvaluateDoorCollisionsJob. active-count-zero path also writes no-hit row with Frame = timing.FrameId instead of default, so fresh absence is explicit.
Rejected Alternatives: Continuing from zero AUP was rejected because missing KCC truth is not valid player fact. Leaving inactive frames at Frame = 0 was rejected because consumers cannot distinguish fresh no-bulkhead proof from bootstrap state. Polling Kinematics through registry/service was rejected because Construction owner must stay decoupled and consume only existing Vault proof lane.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra behavior is identical when KCC snapshot exists. During boot-order gaps or KCC failure, route fails inert instead of inventing player position.
Hardware Impact: Absent-player frames save one collision job schedule and prevent false collision work. Normal frames pay one branch after existing Vault resolve attempt.
Decision 2026-05-21 - Vault Lane Bounds And KCC Freshness
Problem: read-only audit found that SHINOBU collision route accepted stale KCC rows and that several unsafe-pointer jobs trusted states.Length while reading or writing companion Vault lanes. Partial Vault failure, hot-swap drift, or future lane-capacity mismatch could turn valid state slot into out-of-bounds write in AUP, plane, CSR, integrity, conductivity, or fluid-flow storage.
Solution: TryResolvePlayerState() now accepts dispatcher frame and rejects zero, future, and older-than-one-frame KCC snapshots. Collision output uses timing.FrameId as proof frame. Intent ingestion now computes writable lane count from min(states, aups, planes, csrEdges, moduleIntegrity), and FindOrAllocateSlot() cannot allocate beyond that bound. PreSimulation computes override/collision count from min(states, aups, planes). Simulation computes mutation count from min(states, csrEdges, conductivity, fluidFlow, moduleIntegrity). ApplyBulkheadLockJob now receives separate conductivity and fluid-flow counts.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting equal Vault capacities was rejected because buffer generations can fail or drift independently. Clamping only inside Burst jobs was rejected because intent ingestion writes from managed runtime code before jobs run. Stamping collision proof with player producer frame was rejected because consumers need proof of dispatcher tick that evaluated barrier.
Scalability potential: Low tier fails inert on stale or partial data instead of spending CPU on invalid proof. Middle/high/ultra keep same authority route and continuous quality cadence; richer shader deformation remains visual-only and does not change DTO layout or save identity.
Hardware Impact: Normal frames pay integer min operations and one freshness check. Stale KCC frames and partial Vault lanes save collision/mutation job schedule and prevent native memory corruption. No registry polling, .Complete(), managed allocation, collider, or GameObject route was introduced.
Decision 2026-05-21 - Locked Simulation Tick Delta
Problem: SHINOBU closure cadence and KCC prediction still used dispatcher FrameDelta. That value can vary with render frame pacing and violates lockstep rollback requirement that critical state changes consume fixed simulation tick, not Unity-style variable frame delta.
Solution: Added LockedSimulationTickDeltaSeconds = 1/60 and ResolveSimulationTickDelta(in DispatcherTimingDTO). helper uses FixedDelta when dispatcher provides finite positive fixed step and falls back to locked tick otherwise. PreSimulation prediction and Simulation closure accumulation now consume this helper.
Rejected Alternatives: Continuing to use FrameDelta was rejected because it ties authority to render cadence. Reading Unity Time.fixedDeltaTime directly was rejected because dispatcher timing DTO is owner-provided proof route. Making quality weight alter tick was rejected because GlobalQualityWeight may scale cadence/fidelity but must not mutate gameplay truth layout or authority identity.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra all keep same authoritative delta. Continuous quality still controls how often closure authority work is admitted and how rich shader fake becomes, not deterministic tick value itself.
Hardware Impact: Adds one finite check and clamp per phase using tick. Prevents divergent closure/collision state across variable frame pacing without adding build-wide dependency or main-thread barrier.
Decision 2026-05-21 - Door Physics Inquisition Sidecar And Evidence Scan
Problem: inquisition editor tool wrote directly over shared Construction optimization aggregate and scanned whole files with broad substring checks. That could delete sibling-agent report keys and could miscount CamelCase identifiers or cold AUP reads as physical door authority.
Solution: editor now emits SHINOBU-owned sidecar JSON and markdown files, then upserts only shinobu220bulkheaddod into shared aggregate. scan strips line comments, excludes /Editor/, uses token boundaries, records line/snippet evidence, and treats transform motion as actual transform writes or Animator usage only.
Rejected Alternatives: Full aggregate overwrite was rejected because report file is multi-owner. Broad Contains was rejected because it inflated proof counts and hid specific evidence line. Counting frame.position reads was rejected because cold AUP capture is not door movement route.
Scalability potential: Runtime behavior is unaffected on every tier. report proves that low-tier and high-tier closure both use mathematical CSR/KCC planes and shader-side visual fakes rather than physical door bodies.
Hardware Impact: Editor/cold only. Gameplay frame cost is 0 us. proof artifact now shows ownedRuntimePhysicsHits=0 with line evidence.
Decision 2026-05-21 - BaseAirlock Cached Bulkhead AUP Snapshot
Problem: Airlock repair snap and bulkhead publish paths could reconstruct AUP facts from runtime-space origin or transform data. That violates owner-local AUP doctrine and can drift across origin shifts.
Solution: BaseAirlock now owns cached bulkhead pose snapshot: AbsoluteUniversePosition center, finite float normal, shift sequence, and validity flag. Cold lifecycle refresh captures pose, origin-shift callbacks mark publication pending, publish emits cached AUP/normal with dispatcher frame, and repair snap AUPs offset from cached bulkhead pose. Missing snapshot or active origin shift fails inert.
Rejected Alternatives: GlobalSignals.CurrentRuntimeOriginAup() was rejected because read accessors cannot consume mutable global origin to fabricate authority. Per-publish transform-to-AUP reconstruction was rejected because publish route should consume owner snapshot state. Leaving Time.frameCount for whistle cadence was rejected because it is not dispatcher frame proof.
Scalability potential: All tiers share same AUP truth route. Low tier avoids extra transform/AUP work on publish; middle/high/ultra still spend saved CPU on shader fake fidelity, not on physical door simulation.
Hardware Impact: Adds five scalar fields to BaseAirlock. Valid publish path avoids repeated origin conversion; repair snap fails fast during invalid snapshot instead of producing wrong AUPs.
Decision 2026-05-21 - Editor Tuner Cached Telemetry Facade
Problem: UI Toolkit tuner only showed active count/quality/cadence/schedule and formatted interpolated string every inspector refresh. It did not expose closure/collision proof and risked becoming misleading facade.
Solution: Runtime caches last telemetry row fields it already reads during VisualSync: frame, average closure, collision edge hash, collision depth, and shader upload count. editor reads those cached scalars through TryReadEditorState, uses reusable StringBuilder, and updates label only when values actually change.
Rejected Alternatives: Resolving Vault telemetry from editor window was rejected because read accessors must remain pure and must not complete jobs or poll global storage from UI. Keeping string interpolation on every refresh was rejected as avoidable editor churn. Adding private NativeArray cache was rejected by H-Phi Vault law.
Scalability potential: Low tier can verify cheap closure cadence and zero/low shader upload counts. Middle/high/ultra can verify higher upload counts and richer shader-driven visual closure without changing gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: Runtime adds four scalar assignments on existing VisualSync telemetry read. Editor-only allocations are reduced by change-gated label rebuilds; gameplay hot path remains zero-GC.
Decision 2026-05-21 - Pose Read Accessor Purity
Problem: cached-pose patch initially allowed private TryResolveBulkheadPoseSnapshot accessor to call RefreshBulkheadPoseSnapshot() when snapshot was invalid. That created read-looking method with mutation, violating Global Systems Doctrine even though it was private.
Solution: Renamed read side to TryReadBulkheadPoseSnapshot and made it pure: it returns false when snapshot is invalid and only copies cached scalar fields. PublishBulkheadContainmentState now explicitly calls RefreshBulkheadPoseSnapshot() as command step before pure read.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving hidden refresh was rejected because read accessors must not mutate state, sync scene state, or search mutable context. Making every caller refresh was rejected where caller is purely repair snap read route; invalid snapshots should fail inert there.
Scalability potential: No tier changes authority identity. Low/middle/high/ultra all consume same cached AUP fact; quality remains visual/cadence only.
Hardware Impact: No measurable speed claim. Valid publish path keeps same work; invalid read paths fail without hidden transform/AUP refresh.
Decision 2026-05-21 - Repair Snap Transform Authority Purge
Problem: TryResolveRepairSnapRuntimePoints still derived hand-basis vectors from Transform.right, Transform.up, and Transform.forward, and cycle/manual override route still had cachedTransform.position fallbacks. That preserved scene-hierarchy authority inside bulkhead interaction surface after AUP snapshot pass.
Solution: Added TryReadBulkheadRuntimeBasis, pure cached-snapshot read that constructs forward/up/right from bulkheadPoseNormal with finite rsqrt guards and origin-shift fail-inert behavior. Cycle audio and manual flood visual anchors now use cached AUP-to-runtime position; if flood anchor cannot be resolved after command refresh, caller sends non-finite visual anchor so BaseModule selects its existing default breach anchor without Transform read.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping airlockTransform.right/up/forward was rejected because repair snap queries must not resync scene hierarchy state. Falling back to cachedTransform.position was rejected because it reintroduces object-door thinking into emergency route. Adding new cross-domain flood overload was rejected because existing BaseModule default-anchor behavior already handles non-finite visual anchors and avoids broader compile wall.
Scalability potential: Low tier now fails inert on missing/shifted pose instead of doing extra hierarchy reads. Middle/high/ultra retain same AUP truth and shader Dear Lie; richer visual behavior remains GPU-side and quality-scaled.
Hardware Impact: Removes three Transform property reads per repair snap query and three residual Transform-position reads from cycle/manual routes. Gameplay hot-frame cost is unchanged; benefit is authority hygiene and fewer native scene reads on interaction paths.
Decision 2026-05-21 - Shift Sequence Fence And Committed AUP Converter
Problem: cached bulkhead pose stored floating-origin shift sequence, but reads only checked validity bit. After origin shift, old AUP center could remain readable until later publish refreshed it. same review found compile-risk residue: RefreshBulkheadPoseSnapshot() called TryResolveAupFromRuntimeOrigin, but that method no longer existed after read-accessor split.
Solution: Added IsBulkheadPoseSnapshotCurrent() and required it in pose readback, repair basis, AUP conversion, and audio anchor reads. OnOriginShift invalidates pose immediately and marks bulkhead publish pending. RefreshBulkheadPoseSnapshot() now captures normalized forward and up, stores both with current shift sequence, and converts runtime position to AUP through HectonFloatingOrigin.ToAbsoluteUniversePositionDouble3() plus AbsoluteUniversePosition.FromAbsolutePosition() after finite checks.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting bulkheadPoseSnapshotValid alone was rejected because it ignores committed-origin changes. Reconstructing up from arbitrary axis was rejected because it loses airlock roll and produces hand-snap drift. GlobalSignals.CurrentRuntimeOriginAup() and AbsoluteUniversePosition.FromRuntimePosition() were rejected because this route should use committed floating-origin owner proof directly and must not resurrect global runtime-origin shortcut.
Scalability potential: Low tier gets deterministic fail-inert behavior during origin shifts instead of wrong-origin interaction math. Middle/high/ultra preserve exact gameplay truth and can spend budget on shader/audio overkill; GlobalQualityWeight still never changes DTO layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Adds one validity/sequence branch to cached pose reads and one extra cached float3 up vector. Removes one compile-risk dead method call and keeps AUP conversion in double precision. Interaction path remains allocation-free and no dispatcher job, collider, or Transform fallback is introduced.
Verification: Targeted red-flag scans returned no hits for stale converter names, GlobalSignals.CurrentRuntimeOriginAup, AbsoluteUniversePosition.FromRuntimePosition, Transform-position residue, Unity time usage, .Complete(), Pack=, or shader binary LOD tokens in SHINOBU target slice. git diff --check reported CRLF warnings only. JSON reports parse. Build was not launched because CPU gate reported 100.000000 even though no compiler process was active.

AbsoluteUniversePosition.ToRuntimeFloat3() internally routes through same global runtime-origin shortcut, so repair snap path still had unowned origin read.

Leaving ToRuntimeFloat3() was rejected because it hides GlobalSignals.CurrentRuntimeOriginAup() behind convenience method. Rewriting shared AbsoluteUniversePosition was rejected because it is outside SHINOBU domain and would touch global root type during parallel batch.

Decision 2026-05-21 - Finite Intent Packet And Collision NaN Fence
Problem: active audit found two source-authority defects. First, Core intent producer could write non-finite normals, sizes, or parent integrity into unmanaged Vault ring and rely on Construction consumer to skip packet. Second, EvaluateDoorCollisionsJob could consume non-finite closure, player radius, or plane values before telemetry had chance to flag and sanitize state. same pass also caught resurfaced GlobalSignals.CurrentRuntimeOriginAup() call in BaseAirlock.TryConvertRuntimePositionToAup, contradicting prior log.

EvaluateDoorCollisionsJob checks finite player AUP endpoints, plane center/normal/extents, closure progress, and player radius, marking BulkheadCollisionFlags.NonFinite and failing inert for poison rows. BaseAirlock.TryConvertRuntimePositionToAup now uses HectonFloatingOrigin.ToAbsoluteUniversePositionDouble3() plus AbsoluteUniversePosition.FromAbsolutePosition() after shift/finite gates.
Rejected Alternatives: Persisting non-finite packets with diagnostic bit was rejected because producer should not store poison data in owner ring when packet is unusable. Relying on telemetry job to sanitize collision inputs was rejected because KCC consumes collision proof earlier in frame. Trusting previous status text was rejected because source code is only authority.
Scalability potential: Low tier fails inert and avoids wasting KCC plane math on invalid bulkheads. Middle/high/ultra keep identical DTO layout, Vault ownership, rollback identity, and shader Dear Lie route; saved safety margin still buys visual-only shader detail through GlobalQualityWeight.
Hardware Impact: Cold/rare publish adds finite predicates before Vault ring write. Active KCC collision adds finite guard branches per active plane but prevents NaN propagation into KCC proof lane, Spatial Hash, and rollback telemetry. No managed allocation, collider, GameObject, registry hot poll, .Complete(), BufferID, DTO layout, or assembly route changed.

Decision 2026-05-21 - KCC Consumer Handle Bind And Collision Fault Telemetry
Problem: KCC consumer still read Shinobu220BulkheadCollisionResults with hot TryGetBuffer(BufferID...) lookup, and collision NonFinite diagnostics could remain trapped in collision proof DTO without forcing SHINOBU black-box dump. second source reconciliation also found KCC runtime AUP converter still reading GlobalSignals.CurrentRuntimeOriginAup().
Solution: PlayerKinematicsRuntime now caches VaultGenerationHandleBulkheadCollisionResultDTO for SHINOBU collision proof lane, resolves handle in fixed tick, and only attempts throttled 16-frame late bind when handle is absent or stale.
