Solution: Drive integration cadence with math.lerp(MinimumTickInterval, MaximumTickInterval, 1 - GlobalQualityWeight) and accumulate dt so battery/heat/wear totals remain accurate.
Rejected Alternatives: Fixed Update cadence and hardware-tier branches were rejected because they either waste CPU or produce discontinuous behavior.
Scalability potential: Low integrates at roughly 5 Hz with accumulated dt; Middle/High interpolate; Ultra can run near-frame cadence for tighter VFX response.
Hardware Impact: Low-end devices skip redundant frames and buy back roughly 3-8 microseconds when no equipment threshold changes occur.
Decision 011 - Black Box Trigger
Problem: NaN heat or invalid grid data must be diagnosable after fact.
Solution: Keep 300-entry EquipmentTelemetryEntry ring and dump it to Docs/AgentLogs/DumpSHINOBU224.bin on first fault flag.
Rejected Alternatives: Debug.Log-only reporting was rejected because it loses previous frame history and allocates strings.
Scalability potential: Same fixed 300-entry buffer on all tiers; high-tier can visualize richer telemetry from same ring.
Hardware Impact: One ring write per integration tick; estimated below 0.3 microseconds for 16-slot aggregation.
Decision 012 - Editor Facades
Problem: Tuning, CSV ingestion, and thermal gizmos are required for control, but runtime gameplay cannot pay managed UI or file parsing costs.
Solution: Keep UI Toolkit tuner and gizmo hooks behind editor-only paths, and keep CSV ingestion cold through ReadOnlySpanbyte into Vault-backed specs.
Rejected Alternatives: Runtime debug prefabs, runtime text labels, and managed CSV strings were rejected because they allocate and pollute equipment frame budget.
Scalability potential: Low devices ship only native runtime; High/Ultra editor/development builds can visualize and tune overkill thermal behavior.
Hardware Impact: Player-frame impact is 0 us for editor windows/scanner; cold CSV parse happens only on explicit ingest.
Decision 013 - Polish Fail-Closed Wear/AUP Ownership
Problem: AreEquipmentBuffersReady() did not require wear-rate Vault stream, and equipment refresh still sampled owner.transform.position per active slot.
Solution: Require activeEquipmentWearDrainRates before initialization, resolve equipped-tool AUP from cached IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot, and use PlayerTool cached-transform helpers only as non-equipped fallback.
Rejected Alternatives: Allowing service readiness with missing wear stream was rejected because it silently disables centralized durability. Per-slot Transform reads were rejected because they keep Unity object state in active equipment sampling path.
Scalability potential: Low uses one player-pose AUP for all equipped tools; Middle/High/Ultra preserve per-tool fallback only for detached or non-equipped registered tools.
Hardware Impact: Avoids up to 16 managed Transform bridge reads per equipment refresh; estimated low-end gain 0.3-1.2 microseconds and lower ARM64 cache/engine-object pressure.
Decision 014 - Compile Wall Boundary
Problem: Hecton8.Core.csproj build failed with 139 cross-domain missing-symbol errors unrelated to SHINOBU224 files.
Solution: Treat result as dependency wall and preserve SHINOBU224 changes; do not edit Logistics/Grid, docking, static data, construction socket, fluid, fauna kinematics, or binary pager domains.
Rejected Alternatives: Patching foreign domains from equipment agent was rejected because it violates domain boundary and risks merge conflicts with other agents.
Scalability potential: No runtime scalability impact; compile proof remains blocked until owning agents restore referenced contract assemblies/types.
Hardware Impact: No player-frame impact; build failed in 6.90s and did not produce runtime artifact.
Decision 015 - Hardware Specs CSV Key Bridge
Problem: toolhardwarespecs.csv was absent, and parser keyed rows by lower-case FNV while PlayerTool.RuntimeToolId uses Animator.StringToHash; name-keyed CSV row could parse successfully but never affect battery, heat, or cooldown math.
Solution: Add live CSV source, support numeric/hex row keys, cache second FNV spec key in PlayerTool, and resolve hardware specs by runtime hash first plus cached spec hash second.
Rejected Alternatives: Changing RuntimeToolId to FNV was rejected because that public runtime identifier already feeds modular equipment, signals, and durability mirrors. Allocating strings in parser to call Animator.StringToHash was rejected because Task 17 requires ReadOnlySpanbyte parser and cold zero-GC bridge.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain one contiguous spec table and no file I/O in gameplay; Middle/High/Ultra can tune richer power/thermal curves from CSV without recompiling C# or changing 32-byte DTO ABI.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost is one cached uint compare per candidate spec row only during equipment input refresh; expected cost below 0.1 microseconds for 16-slot local equipment cap, with 0 B GC in player-frame integration.
Decision 016 - Typed SignalBus Writers And Vault Descriptors
Problem: Burst equipment job emitted overheat/depletion edges into two equipment-owned NativeQueue buffers, then CompleteActiveEquipmentJob drained those queues and re-published each payload into SignalBusT. Buffer acquisition also used direct IDataVault.GetBufferT external views.
Solution: Remove two private equipment signal queues, configure typed SignalBusEquipmentOverheatSignal and SignalBusToolDepletedSignal lanes during cold init, pass their ParallelWriters directly into EquipmentStateIntegrationJob, and acquire Vault streams through GetGenerationHandleT plus TryResolveHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping local queues was rejected because it created duplicate native signal ownership and avoidable post-fence loop. Creating new cross-domain signal owner was rejected because SignalBusT already owns typed unmanaged broadcast lanes and bounded snapshots.
Scalability potential: Low devices skip post-fence queue-drain/re-publish pass; Middle/High/Ultra keep same richer VFX/audio payload surface through typed lane without widening 32-byte equipment DTO.
Hardware Impact: Removes two scene-lifetime private queue allocations from equipment domain and one bounded main-thread dequeue/enqueue loop per completed equipment tick; expected low-end gain is below 1 microsecond normally, with higher savings on threshold-burst frames.
Decision 017 - Power Runtime Coupling Reduction
Problem: ModularEquipmentEngine directly referenced Hecton8.Power runtime namespace only to subscribe as IPowerGridTelemetryListener, widening compile-wall coupling beyond Core power service contract.
Solution: Remove Power telemetry listener/subscription route and derive equipment brownout scalar from cached Core IPowerGridService.TotalGeneration, TotalConsumption, and BatterySnapshot.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping PowerGridTelemetryEvents was rejected because it creates sibling runtime dependency for scalar already exposed by Core registry contract. Adding new signal was rejected because needed value is private request/response state for this owner, not multi-consumer broadcast.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid listener bucket and event queue path; Middle/High/Ultra keep same brownout flicker scalar, with visual intensity still driven by downstream presentation quality.
Hardware Impact: Removes one cold listener registration and one cross-domain telemetry callback route from equipment domain; per-tick cached service scalar reads are bounded and allocation-free.
Decision 018 - PlayerTool Hot Registry Cache Closure
Problem: PlayerTool still read GlobalRegistry.ToolDurability, GlobalRegistry.Input, GlobalRegistry.InteractionSignals, and GlobalRegistry.PlayerInventoryRuntime from methods that can sit on active equipment/tool-use call paths. That violated cold-discovery rule even though central Burst solver itself did not poll registry.
Solution: Extend existing PlayerTool hot-swap cache to durability, input, interaction-signal, and player-inventory services. CurrentDurability, IsBroken, fallback durability drain, overcharge input checks, queued raycast helper calls, and overcharge inventory removal now use cached fields. ModularEquipmentEngine durability mirror registration now uses its cached durability service and refreshes mirrors when ToolDurabilityRuntime is rebound.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving getter-level registry reads was rejected because ModularEquipmentEngine.Tick() samples DurabilityNormalized while preparing equipment inputs. Adding new signal lanes for private durability/input/inventory queries was rejected because these are direct owner-service reads, not broadcasts.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid repeated registry property traversal during active use; Middle/High/Ultra preserve same richer overcharge and durability behavior through cached services without widening 32-byte equipment DTO.
Hardware Impact: Removes up to 16 durability registry reads per equipment refresh plus per-use input/interaction lookups; expected low-end gain is sub-microsecond to roughly 1 microsecond under active tool spam, with main value being deterministic ownership and 0 B GC call-stack hygiene.
Decision 019 - Empty World Namespace Coupling Sweep
Problem: ToolDurabilitySystem.cs imported Hecton8.World without using symbol from that namespace, leaving false sibling-domain coupling marker in SHINOBU224 static scans.
Solution: Remove unused using Hecton8.World; and keep file on UnityEngine.Transform plus existing gameplay/core contracts.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping import was rejected because compile-wall scans treat namespace edges as evidence, and import provided no runtime behavior.
Scalability potential: No gameplay curve changes; Low/Middle/High/Ultra all keep same centralized equipment/durability path with less dependency noise.
Hardware Impact: No measurable frame cost change; it protects iteration/build routing by removing one unnecessary compile-surface edge.
Decision 020 - Durability Vault And Save Cache Boundary
Problem: ToolDurabilitySystem.Tick() and durability owner resolution still reached GlobalRegistry.DataVault, GlobalRegistry.Save, and GlobalRegistry.Player through helper calls that can run during active equipment sampling or durability job scheduling.
Solution: Make ToolDurabilitySystem IGlobalRegistryHotSwapListener/IGlobalRegistryHotSwapRefListener, cache IDataVault, ISaveService, and IPlayerRuntimeContext during cold bootstrap, and rebind those references on registry replacement. TryResolveBufferT now resolves through dataVault, save registration uses saveService, and player tool ownership uses playerRuntimeContext.
Rejected Alternatives: Polling GlobalRegistry in Tick() was rejected because it violates cold-discovery rule even if lookup is allocation-free. Moving durability state into ModularEquipmentEngine was rejected because durability already owns repair/save/event mirrors and SHINOBU224 should not create second durability owner.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid repeated registry traversal around durability scheduling; Middle/High/Ultra preserve same centralized wear bridge, editor tuning, and overkill VFX signal surface without widening 32-byte active equipment DTO.
Hardware Impact: Removes per-tick vault/save/player registry lookups from durability bridge. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is sub-microsecond normally and roughly 0.5-1.0 microsecond under active tool spam; larger value is deterministic ownership and no hidden registry polling in equipment-adjacent runtime paths.
Decision 021 - Durability Generation Descriptor Migration
Problem: ToolDurabilitySystem still stored five obsolete VaultBufferHandleT fields. Those handles carry cached pointer metadata and violate current ledger rule that persistent Vault state must be pointer-free VaultGenerationHandleT descriptor.
Solution: Replace durability handles with VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve method-local NativeArrayT views through cached IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, reacquire missing or undersized lanes through GetGenerationHandleT, and release descriptors through IDataVault.ReleaseBuffer on DataVault rebind or destroy.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles was rejected because even if resolver ignores stale pointers, field type teaches future code to persist pointer-bearing metadata. Migrating entire ModularEquipmentEngine NativeArray surface in same patch was rejected because it touches main active-equipment owner across many runtime methods and needs its own isolated compile-risk loop.
Scalability potential: Low devices remove stale-pointer validation risk without extra per-frame allocation; Middle/High/Ultra keep same durability job throughput and can still feed richer active-equipment VFX through existing scalar lanes.
Hardware Impact: Runtime arithmetic cost is essentially unchanged; metadata safety improves by removing 24-byte pointer-bearing handles and retaining 16-byte descriptors. practical gain is relocation/defrag safety and less false H-Phi debt around durability bridge.
Decision 022 - Modular Equipment Vault View Migration
Problem: ModularEquipmentEngine still persisted Vault-resolved NativeArrayT aliases for equipment state, published state, AUP samples, grid-load requests, telemetry, tuning, and hardware specs. That violates Vault law because relocation/defrag generation bump can invalidate long-lived native views while owner still appears initialized.
Solution: Replace persistent native aliases with 16-byte VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors and method-local EquipmentVaultViews struct. Every tick, editor read, publish pass, telemetry pass, and mutation path resolves current phase-local views through cached IDataVault.TryResolveHandle; missing, undersized, or stale descriptors are released and reacquired through GetGenerationHandleT. Shutdown and DataVault rebind complete pending Burst job before releasing descriptors. Thermodynamic readback is no longer stored as private field; resolved grid view is local to scheduling and is handed directly to EquipmentStateIntegrationJob.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping scene-lifetime NativeArrayT fields was rejected because it hides pointer lifetime under safe-looking struct and makes Vault relocation unsafe. Replacing Vault buffers with private persistent arrays was rejected because it violates one owner/one route and breaks rollback snapshot routing. Polling GlobalRegistry.DataVault in each hot method was rejected because discovery remains cold and rebinds are handled by cached listener state.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same O(N) 16-slot equipment pass and avoid defrag-era stale pointer checks. Middle, High, and Ultra keep same continuous quality cadence, trilinear thermal blend, and richer signal/VFX surface while still resolving only local views for active phase.
Hardware Impact: hot math cost is unchanged except for bounded descriptor validation before scheduling; safety gain is removal of 17 persistent NativeArrayT aliases from main equipment owner. Stale-descriptor release prevents Vault refcount drift after relocation and protects ARM64/Quest-class hardware from dereferencing invalid native views.
Decision 023 - Runtime Transform Fallback And Descriptor Reacquire Closure
Problem: After Vault view migration, ToolDurabilitySystem.TryResolveBufferT() could overwrite stale or undersized generation descriptor without releasing it first. ModularEquipmentEngine also still had runtime fallback paths that could derive equipment water/depth/AUP from Unity object position and TryResolveSlot() could resolve Vault views before finding later owner mirror slot.
Solution: Release stale durability descriptors before reacquire, remove central runtime Transform/AUP fallbacks from equipment sampling, resolve player water/depth once per refresh or publish pass, make non-equipped tool AUP fail closed, and split TryResolveSlot() into owner-mirror scan followed by one Vault fallback scan. Layout offset reflection remains editor/development only; release player builds retain unmanaged size checks without runtime reflection.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing generation handle without ReleaseBuffer was rejected because it risks refcount drift after Vault relocation. Keeping Transform fallback was rejected because active equipment processor must not query MonoBehaviour hierarchy state during active execution phase. Resolving Vault views during owner mirror scan was rejected because most local lookups should complete from 16-slot mirror.
Scalability potential: Low devices use one cached player pose, one water state, and one depth scalar for all equipped tools in refresh. Middle/High/Ultra keep deterministic thermal and battery truth while presentation can still spend signal-driven VFX budget on overheat/depletion effects.
Hardware Impact: Removes late-slot Vault resolves and Unity object position fallback from common equipment lookup/sampling path. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.3-1.5 microseconds under active tool churn; Quest-class ARM benefits mostly from lower engine-object bridge and stale-descriptor safety.
Decision 024 - Durability Tick Guard Ordering
Problem: ToolDurabilitySystem.Tick() still resolved all five durability Vault lanes before checking enableDurabilityDrain and decayScheduled, then HasPendingDecay() resolved pending-decay lane second time before scheduling decay job.
Solution: Run cheap boolean guards before TryResolveNativeState(), pass already-resolved NativeArrayfloat pending-decay view into HasPendingDecay(), and clamp scan length to resolved buffer length. active equipment cadence/no-acquire tuning path was rechecked and left unchanged because source already gates full equipment view resolution behind GlobalQualityWeight cadence.
Rejected Alternatives: Resolving all lanes every dispatcher tick was rejected because disabled or already-scheduled durability frames do not need any Vault view. Re-resolving pending decay was rejected because descriptor was already proven in same phase. Scheduling editor mock job asynchronously was rejected because CI/editor readback should be deterministic immediately after cold facade call.
Scalability potential: Low devices now pay only cached save-service registration plus scalar guards when durability drain is disabled or decay job is already pending. Middle/High/Ultra keep same scheduled decay math and can still use richer equipment heat/battery signals without widening active equipment DTO.
Hardware Impact: Removes five descriptor validations on disabled/already-scheduled durability frames and one duplicate pending-decay validation before each scheduled decay. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.2-1.0 microseconds depending on durability cadence and pending work density; Quest-class ARM benefits from less Vault metadata traffic.
Decision 025 - Service Heartbeat Resolver Purge
Problem: ModularEquipmentEngine.IsServiceReady called TryResolveEquipmentViews(out ) and read GlobalRegistry.ModularEquipment. Any watchdog/bootstrap readiness poll could therefore touch full equipment Vault descriptor set and potentially reacquire buffers from property that should be side-effect free.
Solution: Make readiness local descriptor/flag check: isInitialized, registeredService, equipmentSignalLanesReady, and all 17 VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors must be created. Add GlobalRegistryServiceSlot.ModularEquipment hot-swap handling so registeredService tracks registry replacement without live registry read in property.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping TryResolveEquipmentViews(out ) in readiness was rejected because service heartbeat cannot be hidden Vault acquisition path. Keeping ReferenceEquals(GlobalRegistry.ModularEquipment, this) in property was rejected because registry reads belong to cold registration/rebind paths, not watchdog probes.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid descriptor validation bursts from watchdog/bootstrap service scans. Middle/High/Ultra preserve same service health semantics while active equipment still reacquires exact views only in initialization, tick, editor, or post-fence phases.
Hardware Impact: Removes up to one 17-lane equipment descriptor resolve/acquire attempt per readiness poll. Estimated low-end gain is 1-4 microseconds during service probe bursts, with larger value being elimination of side effects from property path.
Decision 026 - Brownout Feedback Narrow View
Problem: TryGetWirelessBrownoutFeedback() is presentation-only query from tool VFX/UI, but it resolved full EquipmentVaultViews set just to read one ToolState.UpgradeBitmask bit. TryGetToolBrownoutFeedback() also used TryResolveSlot(), whose fallback can resolve full active equipment views on mirror miss.
Solution: Add TryResolveToolStatesNoAcquire() for descriptor-only ToolState reads and TryResolveOwnerMirrorSlot() for cosmetic owner-local lookup. Brownout feedback now uses 16-slot owner mirror and one ToolState view, then fails closed when mirror is absent.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping full view resolution in visual flicker query was rejected because cosmetic feedback must not acquire all equipment lanes. Expanding IModularEquipmentService was rejected because this is internal implementation cut and changing public service surface would widen compile risk.
Scalability potential: Low devices skip full Vault metadata traffic during brownout pulse polling. Middle/High/Ultra keep same flicker scalar and can still spend saved CPU on stronger shader/audio presentation downstream.
Hardware Impact: Removes one 17-lane equipment view resolve from wireless brownout feedback and prevents full-view fallback for brownout pulse lookup. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.5-3 microseconds under UI/VFX polling, with Quest-class ARM benefiting from lower metadata/cache traffic.
Decision 027 - Public Tool Scalar Getter Narrowing
Problem: TryGetToolState() and TryGetToolStats() are read-only public getters used by many tool scalar accessors, but each call resolved full equipment view set after slot lookup. range, heat, cooldown, drain, recoil, or efficiency query therefore touched many unrelated Vault lanes.
Solution: Reuse descriptor-only TryResolveToolStatesNoAcquire() and add TryResolveToolStatsNoAcquire(). state getter reads only ToolState and clamps battery locally; stats getter reads only ToolStats. Authoritative mutations, publication, telemetry, and mirror writes still use full view where multiple lanes must stay coherent.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping getter convenience on TryResolveEquipmentViews() was rejected because scalar reads should not validate AUP, grid-load, telemetry, tuning, hardware-spec, published-state, and wear-rate lanes. Changing public method signatures was rejected because existing callers do not need contract change.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid broad Vault metadata traffic from active tool spam. Middle/High/Ultra retain identical scalar outputs while downstream presentation can use saved CPU on stronger tool feedback.
Hardware Impact: Removes up to 16 unrelated descriptor validations from each scalar getter call layered on TryGetToolStats() or TryGetToolState(). Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.5-4 microseconds under active use/UI polling; ARM benefits from lower cache churn.
Decision 028 - Published State And Telemetry Getter Narrowing
Problem: Published read-buffer, telemetry, and tuning getter APIs were resolving full equipment view set even when they only needed published DTO stream, telemetry ring/cursor, or one tuning row. UI/editor/debug callers could therefore validate many unrelated lanes.
Solution: Add no-acquire helpers for published active equipment and telemetry ring/cursor, and reuse existing no-acquire tuning helper for TryGetEquipmentTuning(). Mutation/editor write APIs still resolve full view when they must keep multiple lanes coherent.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving UI/debug readers on full resolver was rejected because read buffers and black-box telemetry are already separated Vault lanes. Expanding public method signatures was rejected because caller semantics did not need to change.
Scalability potential: Low devices read HUD/telemetry with only minimum descriptor set. Middle/High/Ultra preserve exact data while high-tier presentation can poll richer overlays without pulling unrelated gameplay lanes.
Hardware Impact: Removes unrelated tool-state, stats, AUP, grid-load, wear-rate, hardware-spec, and active-state descriptor checks from common published-state and telemetry reads. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.5-5 microseconds under HUD/tuner/debug polling.
Decision 029 - Telemetry Cursor Wrap Guard
Problem: After narrowing telemetry getters to ring/cursor lanes, read path still trusted telemetryCursor0 as if it were always inside 0, ringLength. stale Vault generation, corrupted cursor, or partial diagnostic write could produce out-of-range positive index and break black-box read path.
Solution: Add ResolveTelemetryHistoryIndex() to fail closed on invalid ring length, clamp requested history to ring capacity, and wrap arbitrary cursor deltas with modulo only when fast unsigned bounds check fails. Latest telemetry now uses same helper with history 0.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping negative-only while (index 0) wrap was rejected because it handles underflow but not cursor values greater than ring length. Saturating cursor was rejected because it would bias black-box reader toward last slot instead of preserving circular-buffer semantics.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep fast path as one unsigned range check and one read; Middle/High/Ultra retain exact 300-frame forensic access even if debug tooling requests deep history during heavy polling.
Hardware Impact: Normal path adds no modulo and remains sub-0.1 microseconds. Corrupted cursor recovery pays one integer modulo in debug/read path to prevent out-of-bounds telemetry read.
Decision 030 - Global Systems Read Accessor Purity
Problem: Several SHINOBU-adjacent read-shaped methods still hid side effects: durability getters could complete jobs, acquire Vault views, or register missing tools; PlayerTool contract/runtime ID helpers lazily called TryGetComponent, Animator.StringToHash, or cache mutation; legacy operational Get string bridge allocated through FixedCharBuffer.ToString().
Solution: Make public durability reads consume only managed mirror, rename acquiring durability helpers to Ensure, make HasNativeState() descriptor-only check, move PlayerTool contract/runtime ID/spec hash/item hash/transform capture to cold spawn/registration caches, rename queued raycast to action helper, and rename managed string bridge to explicit BuildLegacyOperationalString methods while preserving WriteOperational as zero-GC route.
Rejected Alternatives: Completing durability decay job from GetDurability() was rejected because read access cannot block dispatcher. Lazily resolving PlayerTool contracts from property getters was rejected because component search belongs to cold ownership setup. Keeping GetOperational wrappers was rejected because their allocation is intentional legacy behavior and must be named as builder, not read accessor.
Scalability potential: Low devices now avoid hidden job fences, component searches, and broad Vault acquisitions from HUD/tool polling; Middle/High/Ultra retain identical equipment truth and can spend recovered frame budget on richer signal-driven VFX/audio presentation.
Hardware Impact: Removes worst-case durability getter job-complete/readback stalls and prevents cosmetic or packet-building reads from triggering cold resolution. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.5-5 us under active tool/HUD polling, with larger frame-time variance reduction when durability job is still pending.
Decision 031 - Equipment Resolver Naming Closure
Problem: ModularEquipmentEngine.TryResolveEquipmentViews() and TryResolveOrAcquireEquipmentBufferT() looked like pure reads but can acquire or reacquire Vault generation descriptors. That leaves future regression path where getter, heartbeat, or UI query can call TryResolve helper and accidentally mutate Vault ownership.
Solution: Rename side-effecting helpers to EnsureEquipmentViews() and EnsureEquipmentBufferT(). Keep TryResolveEquipmentBufferT() and TryResolveNoAcquire() helpers unchanged because they only validate already-created descriptors through cached IDataVault.TryResolveHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving comments on old names was rejected because naming is first guard against hidden read-side mutation. Splitting equipment owner into another facade was rejected because this is contract hygiene fix inside existing owner and does not justify new abstraction.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid future accidental broad Vault acquisition from UI/read/watchdog paths. Middle/High/Ultra keep same 17-lane active-equipment model and can spend saved CPU on presentation, not metadata churn.
Hardware Impact: This loop changes no runtime math directly. It hardens call graph so broad equipment descriptor acquisition remains explicit and phase-owned; expected direct frame gain is 0 us, but it prevents reintroducing 1-5 us read-path spikes measured in prior narrowing loops.
Decision 032 - Side-Effect Resolver Verb Closure
Problem: Two SHINOBU-owned private helpers still used pure-looking Resolve names while performing side effects. ToolDurabilitySystem.ResolvePlayerOwners() can query player bootstrapper and cache scene components, and ModularEquipmentEngine.ResolveHeatWarningHaptic() can enqueue haptic command during readback publication.
Solution: Rename them to EnsurePlayerOwnersCached() and ApplyHeatWarningHapticGate(). durability helper now advertises cache/scene ownership work, and equipment helper now advertises action gate around presentation output.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving names with comments was rejected because future call sites search by verbs first and would treat Resolve as safe for getter/read-path reuse. Moving haptic gate into Burst job was rejected because presentation commands are not deterministic gameplay truth and must stay outside rollback DTO update.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid future accidental scene lookup or haptic queue emission from read-accessor reuse. Middle/High/Ultra keep same heat-warning presentation path and can still intensify downstream effects without changing active-equipment truth.
Hardware Impact: Direct frame cost change is 0 us because behavior is unchanged. hardening prevents reintroduction of hidden scene-search/haptic side effects into read paths; worst avoided spike is cost of cold TryGetComponent/bootstrap lookup or presentation queue emission from getter.
Decision 033 - Owner-Local ToolState Signal Throttle
Problem: ModularEquipmentEngine.ShouldPublishToolStateChanged() read GlobalSignals.TryGetLatestToolStateChangedSignal() to suppress small state deltas. That made SHINOBU-owned publication decision depend on global mutable latest-snapshot state, and another producer on same legacy bridge lane could affect equipment owner's cadence.
Solution: Keep GlobalSignals.Publish(in ToolStateChangedSignal) because it already pushes typed SignalBusToolStateChangedSignal lane, but move throttle comparison to owner-local scalar fields: last signal, last slot index, and valid flag. Reset cache on DataVault rebind and shutdown.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing GlobalSignals was rejected because it is core routing outside SHINOBU224 scope and wrapper already bridges into SignalBusT. Adding per-slot managed array was rejected because single-slot local cache matches prior latest-signal semantics without adding another array allocation or widening Vault state. Removing throttling entirely was rejected because it would increase UI/VFX signal traffic.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid one global latest read per non-terminal signal candidate and keep dirty-state coalescing. Middle/High/Ultra keep richer scalar publication while presentation systems still receive same typed lane through legacy wrapper.
Hardware Impact: Removes one global latest snapshot read and cross-producer cache dependency per publish candidate. Expected i3/MX350 gain is sub-0.5 microseconds normally; larger value is deterministic owner-local cadence and less global-state coupling in active equipment publication.
Decision 034 - Durability Player Context Owner Cache
Problem: ToolDurabilitySystem.EnsurePlayerOwnersCached() had cached IPlayerRuntimeContext, but still resolved playerRoot through GameBootstrapper.TryGetCurrentPlayerTransform() first and resolved playerSurvivalSystem through playerRoot.TryGetComponent(...). Only playerToolManager preferred cached context.
Solution: Hydrate playerRoot, playerSurvivalSystem, and playerToolManager from playerRuntimeContext before any bootstrap/component fallback. On GlobalRegistryServiceSlot.Player rebind, refresh or clear all three cached owners together.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping bootstrap/component lookup ahead of cached context was rejected because player runtime context is authority route for owner-local reads. Adding new durability/player interface was rejected because existing IPlayerRuntimeContext already exposes required owners.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid cold scene/component probes during environmental corrosion after context bind. Middle/High/Ultra retain identical corrosion math and can spend saved slow-tick budget on richer equipment presentation without changing gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: Saves up to one bootstrap lookup plus two TryGetComponent probes on first corrosion slow tick after player-context availability. Warm-cache frame gain is 0 us; value is fewer cold scene lookups and cleaner owner-route discipline.
Decision 035 - Deterministic Time And Pose Purge
Problem: SHINOBU-owned tool publication and interaction routes still used Unity frame/time APIs: ToolStateChangedSignal.Frame, durability-change signal frames, queued interaction packets, and recent-use durability corrosion. Brine corrosion also sampled playerRoot.position before cached player pose route, and overcharge damage probed component before reading cached health facade.
Solution: Use owner-local deterministic counters and dispatcher-owned elapsed state. ModularEquipmentEngine publishes tool-state frames from equipmentTickIndex; ToolDurabilitySystem owns durabilitySignalFrame; PlayerTool owns interactionFrameIndex; recent-use state is secondsSinceLastUse, advanced by AdvanceRuntimeActiveIntent(deltaTime). Brine sampling now consumes IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() first, and overcharge damage reads IPlayerRuntimeContext.PlayerHealth before component fallback.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Time.frameCount was rejected because Unity frame count is not rollback truth. Keeping Time.time was rejected because wall/frame time is not deterministic across rollback or platform cadence. Sampling playerRoot.position first was rejected because player runtime context already owns pose publication. Removing all fallbacks was rejected because cold bootstrap/editor paths still need degraded operation when context is unavailable.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid Unity time/Transform bridge traffic in active tool and durability paths. Middle/High/Ultra keep identical signal payload layouts and can spend recovered CPU budget on richer signal-driven VFX/audio without changing gameplay truth ownership.
Hardware Impact: Removes Unity time reads from active interaction/signal publication and makes corrosion brine sampling pose-snapshot first. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.2-1.0 microseconds under active tool spam and slow corrosion polling; Quest-class ARM benefits from lower engine-object bridge pressure and cleaner deterministic replay behavior.
Decision 036 - Runtime Transform Pose Fallback Purge
Problem: prior deterministic-time cut still left two Transform bridge residues inside owned runtime paths. Brine corrosion could fall back from player pose snapshot to playerRoot.position, and invalid tool ray directions could fall back to cachedTransform.forward. PlayerTool also retained unused cached-runtime-position/AUP helpers and stale cached Transform field, creating future regression path back to Transform-derived gameplay truth.
Solution: Make brine sampling fail closed unless IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() returns finite RuntimePosition. Make invalid-direction fallback use cached PlayerRuntimePoseSnapshot.Forward, normalized with rsqrt(max(sqrMagnitude, 0.0001)), then constant Vector3.forward if no valid snapshot exists. Remove TrySampleCachedRuntimePosition(), TrySampleCachedAup(), and cachedBaseTransform.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Transform fallback for degraded bootstrap was rejected because missing player pose means brine fact has no authoritative owner route. Keeping cachedTransform.forward was rejected because invalid-direction repair is not worth Unity object bridge in active tool path. Keeping unused cached-AUP helpers was rejected because unused internal APIs become attractive but incorrect future fallbacks.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid residual Unity object bridge reads during slow brine corrosion and invalid-direction tool actions. Middle/High/Ultra preserve same public contracts and can spend saved CPU on richer signal consumers without changing gameplay truth ownership, DTO layout, or Vault route.
Hardware Impact: Saves one Transform position read in brine slow-tick edge path and one Transform forward read in invalid-direction active tool actions. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.1-0.8 microseconds in those edge cases; Quest-class ARM benefits mainly from lower engine-object bridge pressure and deterministic replay hygiene.
Decision 037 - Sub-Agent Fallback Closure
Problem: read-only source auditor found three remaining side-effect surfaces: durability owner discovery still had runtime scene/component fallback, overcharge damage could still component-probe PlayerHealth, and editor gizmo drawing could call EnsureEquipmentViews() and acquire Vault lanes from debug read. legacy operational string builders also remained visible despite allocating through FixedCharBuffer.ToString().
Solution: Make durability environmental corrosion require cached IPlayerRuntimeContext owners only; remove playerRoot, GameBootstrapper.TryGetCurrentPlayerTransform, and component fallback. Make overcharge damage require IPlayerRuntimeContext.PlayerHealth. Change OnDrawGizmos() to TryResolvePublishedActiveEquipmentNoAcquire() so editor drawing reads only already-created published buffer. Hide legacy string builders from normal editor browsing while preserving zero-GC WriteOperationalSummary/Directive(ref FixedCharBuffer) as runtime route.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping scene/component fallback for degraded operation was rejected because missing runtime context is ownership failure and corrosion/overcharge can fail closed. Letting gizmos acquire Vault buffers was rejected because debug reads must not mutate native ownership. Marking legacy string methods obsolete was rejected because warning-as-error projects could turn intentional legacy bridge into compile noise.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid cold scene/component probes in slow corrosion and rare overcharge failures. Middle/High/Ultra keep identical gameplay truth, DTO layouts, signal routes, and visual budget; editor gizmos remain available but cannot create native buffers as side effect.
Hardware Impact: Removes bootstrap lookup plus two component probes from durability fallback and one health component probe from overcharge failure. Estimated i3/MX350 edge-path gain is 0.1-1.5 microseconds with lower frame-time variance; editor gizmo no-acquire avoids accidental Vault metadata churn while inspecting active tools.
Decision 038 - LogicSpanner Derived-Tool Action Route Cut
Problem: derived-tool scan found LogicSpannerTool still using Time.time for link-pulse HUD state, transform.position/forward for primary target ray, and GlobalRegistry.ConstructionRuntime inside primary action. That reintroduced wall-time, Transform pose truth, and registry read outside cold dependency setup in tool action path.
Solution: Replace link-pulse wall-time with dispatcher-advanced WasRecentlyUsed(0.75f) state. Resolve primary action ray from IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() with finite checks and rsqrt normalization. Cache ConstructionManager during spawn/equip and consume cached dependency during UsePrimary().
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Time.time was rejected because pulse is derived from same owner action that already advances recent-use state. Keeping transform.position/forward was rejected because player runtime pose owns action origin/direction for handheld tools. Applying broad mechanical patch to every derived tool in one pass was rejected because those tools have different authority surfaces and need separate proof cuts.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid Unity time/Transform/registry bridge cost during spanner actions. Middle/High/Ultra keep identical tool semantics and can spend recovered variance budget on richer connection-spline presentation without changing active-equipment DTOs or save identity.
Hardware Impact: Removes one wall-time read, one Transform position/forward read pair, and one action-time registry read from each primary logic-spanner action. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.1-0.7 microseconds per action; Quest-class ARM benefits from less engine-object bridge traffic and cleaner deterministic replay behavior.
Decision 039 - Environmental Analyzer Derived-Tool Route Cut
Problem: EnvironmentalAnalyzerTool still used bootstrap/component survival discovery, Time.time for feedback throttling, Time.frameCount for target assessment cache identity, cachedTransform.position/forward for analysis ray authority, and action-time GlobalRegistry.ScanLog reads during archive writes. That made derived active tool pull from scene state, Unity wall/frame time, and registry outside cold setup.
Solution: Resolve survival through IPlayerRuntimeContext.SurvivalSystem only, replace wall-time feedback with feedbackCooldownRemaining advanced by ToolTick(deltaTime), replace frame-count cache identity with targetAssessmentEvaluationStamp, resolve ray origin/forward from PlayerRuntimePoseSnapshot with finite checks and math.rsqrt(math.max(lenSq, 0.0001f)), and cache ScanLogSystem during spawn/equip for archive writes.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping bootstrap fallback was rejected because player runtime context owns survival state. Keeping Transform ray origin was rejected because held-tool aim comes from player pose truth. Keeping Time.time/Time.frameCount was rejected because rollback and platform cadence cannot depend on Unity wall/frame counters. Polling GlobalRegistry.ScanLog inside archive methods was rejected because registry access is cold DI only.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid Unity time, Transform, bootstrap/component, and registry bridge cost during analyzer actions. Middle devices keep identical analyzer outputs. High/Ultra can spend saved variance budget on richer HUD/audio/archive presentation without changing active-equipment DTO layout, save identity, or ownership route.
Hardware Impact: Removes one wall-time gate, one frame-count read, one Transform position/forward pair, one survival bootstrap/component fallback, and repeated registry property reads from analyzer action/archive paths. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.2-1.2 microseconds per analyzer action; Quest-class ARM benefits mostly from lower engine-object bridge pressure and deterministic replay hygiene.
Decision 040 - KnifeTool Derived-Tool Route And Allocation Cut
Problem: KnifeTool still drove blade origin/direction from cached Transform, throttled feedback through Time.time, keyed hit-cache validity to Time.frameCount, read GlobalRegistry.Localization from static helper, and built tactical assessment strings through new string before HUD/log publication.
Solution: Resolve blade rays from IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() with finite checks and math.rsqrt(math.max(lenSq, 0.0001f)), replace feedback with dispatcher-advanced cooldown, replace frame-count cache identity with hitEvaluationStamp, cache LocalizationManager during spawn/equip, and represent tactical assessment text as KnifeText templates plus args written directly into FixedCharBuffer.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached Transform was rejected because player pose snapshot owns handheld tool aim. Keeping Unity wall/frame time was rejected because tool feedback/read caching must survive rollback. Leaving ResolveLocalized() static was rejected because it hid action-time registry polling. Accepting formatted assessment strings was rejected because tactical secondary use is gameplay action path, not editor-only bridge.
Scalability potential: Low devices use one pose snapshot, one queued ray, and no per-assessment string allocations. Middle devices preserve identical blade semantics. High/Ultra can spend saved CPU/GC budget on stronger contact sparks, HUD readouts, or audio without changing equipment DTO layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Removes one Transform position/forward pair, multiple Time reads, one registry property read, and several short-lived strings from knife action/readout paths. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.3-1.8 microseconds per tactical read plus 0 B GC assessment route; Quest-class ARM benefits mainly from lower engine-object bridge and allocator pressure.
Decision 041 - GravityTether Pose Authority Cut
Problem: GravityTetherTool retained cachedTransform, refreshed it from transform, and used owner Transform position/forward to emit auxiliary gravity tether requests. That made compact active tool depend on Unity object pose even though player runtime context already publishes authoritative pose snapshot.
Solution: Remove cached Transform and resolve tether origin/forward from IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() with finite checks and math.rsqrt(math.max(lenSq, 0.0001f)). Keep optional chestTarget.position only as authored tether anchor endpoint; fail closed if no valid player pose exists.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Transform fallback was rejected because missing player pose means request has no authoritative owner route. Creating new auxiliary equipment pose contract was rejected because IPlayerRuntimeContext already supplies needed origin/forward.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid Unity object bridge reads on repeated tether requests. Middle/High/Ultra preserve identical request payload semantics and can spend saved variance on richer auxiliary tether visuals without changing equipment DTO layout or ownership route.
Hardware Impact: Removes one cached Transform field and one Transform position/forward pair from each eligible tether request. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.05-0.4 microseconds per request; Quest-class ARM benefits from lower engine-object bridge pressure and cleaner rollback replay.
Decision 042 - StunPistol Action Route And Component Allocation Cut
Problem: StunPistolTool still used cached Transform origin/forward for shot authority, Time.time and Time.frameCount for feedback and assessment cache identity, action-time GlobalRegistry.Input, static GlobalRegistry.Localization, per-assessment new string formatting, display-writer raycasts, and ai.gameObject.AddComponentStunTargetRuntime() during primary fire. That stacked Unity object bridge reads, wall-time drift, registry polling, heap allocation, and runtime component mutation onto player action.
Solution: Resolve stun rays from IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() with finite checks and math.rsqrt(math.max(lenSq, 0.0001f)); use feedbackCooldownRemaining advanced by dispatcher ToolTick(deltaTime); expose protected cached IInputService accessor on PlayerTool; cache LocalizationManager on spawn/equip; represent tactical assessment text as StunText template/argument data written directly into FixedCharBuffer; and make StunTargetRuntime register from lifecycle while TryApply() only uses pre-authored, already-registered runtimes. Operational writers now read last action-owned assessment snapshot instead of triggering fresh query.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Transform authority was rejected because handheld aim belongs to player runtime pose owner. Keeping Unity time was rejected because stun feedback/read caching must survive rollback. Keeping GlobalRegistry.Input and static localization reads was rejected because registry is cold DI only. Keeping hot AddComponent was rejected because component creation is managed allocation and scene mutation during tool shot. Keeping display-writer target queries was rejected because write/read surfaces must not publish or search.
Scalability potential: Low devices use one pose snapshot, one queued ray, cached services, pre-authored stun runtime only, and no per-assessment string allocation. Middle devices retain identical shot and fauna interaction semantics. High/Ultra can spend saved CPU/GC budget on richer stun arcs, HUD readouts, audio, or screen-space distortion without changing equipment DTO layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Removes one Transform position/forward pair, multiple Unity time reads, one hot input registry property, static localization registry reads, several short-lived assessment strings, display-triggered raycasts, and runtime component creation from stun action paths. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.4-2.4 microseconds per stun action plus 0 B tactical assessment GC; Quest-class ARM benefits mainly from lower engine-object bridge and allocator pressure.
Decision 043 - Propulsion Tool Pose/Time/Name Route Cut
Problem: PropulsionTool still used cachedTransform.position/forward for push, pull, tractor hold, tow-break, queued raycast, and launch authority; Time.time/Time.frameCount for feedback and assessment cache identity; GlobalRegistry.PlayerMotor inside MaintainLock; display-writer target queries; static localization; and body.gameObject.name in action/log/assessment paths.
Solution: Resolve all propulsion origin/forward vectors from IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() with finite checks and math.rsqrt(math.max(lenSq, 0.0001f)); replace wall/frame time with feedbackCooldownRemaining advanced by ToolTick(deltaTime); arm presentation cooldown through continuous HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight curve; use IPlayerRuntimeContext.PlayerRigidbody as tractor anchor; cache LocalizationManager on spawn/equip; make operational writers read last action-owned assessment snapshot; and replace Unity object-name labels with localized generic cargo label while preserving authored FieldTargetDescriptor semantic assessments.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Transform fallback was rejected because handheld tool pose truth belongs to player runtime context. Keeping Unity time was rejected because feedback/read caching must survive rollback. Polling GlobalRegistry.PlayerMotor in tractor loop was rejected because registry is cold DI only. Reading gameObject.name was rejected because Unity object names are managed presentation labels, not active-equipment truth. Letting operational summary/directive queue raycast was rejected because read/write surfaces must not search or publish.
Scalability potential: Low devices get one pose snapshot, one queued ray, no player-motor registry poll, no display-time raycast, and slower presentation cadence from continuous quality curve. Middle devices retain identical gameplay truth with fewer engine-object bridge reads. High/Ultra can spend saved variance on richer tractor beam, launch, HUD, and audio effects without changing ActiveEquipmentDTO, save identity, StateRingBuffer truth, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Removes one Transform position/forward pair from push/pull/hold/launch, multiple Unity Time reads, one hot player-motor registry lookup per hold tick, display-time raycasts, and Unity object-name string reads. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.4-2.0 microseconds per active propulsion action/hold tick; Quest-class ARM benefits mainly from reduced engine-object bridge and allocator pressure.
Decision 044 - Harpoon Tool Pose/Time/Name/Sibling Edge Cut
Problem: HarpoonLauncherTool still retained cached Transform pose authority, Unity wall/frame time for feedback and assessment cache identity, direct Hecton8.AI / FaunaBrain inspection for assessment state, Unity gameObject.name labels, static GlobalRegistry.Localization polling, dead mutable uppercase string cache, and display-triggered target reads. Hubble side audit also found ResolvePlayerMovement() could fall back to GetComponentInParent from tether registration.
Solution: Resolve fire/reel/tether/tracer/recoil vectors from IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() with finite checks and math.rsqrt(math.max(lenSq, 0.0001f)); replace wall/frame time with feedbackCooldownRemaining and owner-local assessment stamps; arm feedback through math.lerp(1.65f, 0.85f, smoothstep(GlobalQualityWeight)); cache LocalizationManager, HectonPlayerMovement, and player Rigidbody only during spawn/equip; remove AI namespace and direct FaunaBrain branch; route target meaning through FieldTargetDescriptor semantics or generic labels; and delete uppercase string cache.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Transform fallback was rejected because handheld aim belongs to player runtime context. Keeping direct FaunaBrain reads was rejected because it creates sibling AI runtime dependency and component discovery path inside equipment tool. Keeping object-name labels was rejected because Unity names are managed presentation strings, not deterministic equipment facts. Keeping ResolvePlayerMovement() fallback in tether registration was rejected because action paths must consume cold-cached owner context or fail closed. Simulating cable physics was rejected; harpoon tether presentation remains shader/line proxy plus scalar force/tow requests.
Scalability potential: Low devices receive one pose snapshot, one queued ray, generic labels, no AI component discovery, no Unity Time, no object-name reads, and slower presentation cadence from continuous quality curve. Middle devices retain identical gameplay force/tether truth with less engine-object bridge traffic. High/Ultra can spend saved variance on richer tether shader, recoil, HUD, and audio presentation without changing ActiveEquipmentDTO, save identity, StateRingBuffer truth, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Removes one Transform position/forward pair from fire/reel/tether/recoil/tracer paths, multiple Unity Time reads, direct AI component discovery, object-name string reads, static localization registry polling, and uppercase string-cache mutation. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.5-2.4 microseconds per active harpoon action/tether tick; Quest-class ARM benefits mainly from reduced engine-object bridge, fewer managed string hazards, and one fewer sibling runtime compile edge.
Decision 045 - LaserCutter Pose/Binding/Name Route Cut
Problem: LaserCutter.cs still used cached tool/player Transforms for action rays, DOD request staging, cut damage, open-water boil, deconstruction completion, salvage pull intent, and laser-line projection. It also scraped player components through GameBootstrapper.TryGetCurrentPlayerTransform, sampled module.transform.position for deconstruction TargetAup, and wrote module Unity names into telemetry. cutter event sidecar also exposes Transform, but Tesla verified AbyssalThermalManager still consumes it for cable-cut stamping, so deleting it would create cross-domain behavior break.
Solution: Route cutter-owned action pose through IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() with finite checks and math.rsqrt(math.max(lenSq, 0.0001f)). Hydrate inventory, movement, rigidbody, and survival caches only from IPlayerRuntimeContext. Use hitInfo.point or pose-derived debug target point for deconstruction TargetAup instead of module Transform center. Project beam visual by hit distance along local forward rather than InverseTransformPoint. Replace module names in operation logs with generic target-module label. Keep public LaserCutterEvents Transform sidecar as documented compatibility bridge until World owns payload pose route.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing LaserCutterEvents.TryResolveCutterTransform was rejected because AbyssalThermalManager uses it for live cable-cut position/forward. Keeping cached Transform fallback was rejected because handheld cutter aim belongs to player pose ownership. Keeping player-root TryGetComponent fallback was rejected because missing runtime context is owner-route failure and cutter can fail closed. Keeping module Transform center as target truth was rejected because hit point is actual tool-owned interaction point.
Scalability potential: Low devices use one pose snapshot for cutter actions, no player-root component probes, no module-name labels, and no inverse Transform projection. Middle devices keep identical cut/deconstruct semantics with lower variance. High/Ultra can spend saved CPU budget on richer beam, boil, spark, haptic, and cable-stamp presentation without changing ActiveEquipmentDTO, save identity, StateRingBuffer truth, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Removes one Transform position/forward pair from primary/secondary cutter ray, DOD request, cut damage, open-water boil, deconstruction completion, and debug recovery paths; removes four player-root component probes from cold binding; removes module Unity-name reads from operation telemetry. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.4-2.1 microseconds per active cutter action, with Quest-class ARM benefiting mainly from less engine-object bridge pressure.

Creating new salvage service contract was rejected because this cut only consumes existing player/input/scan/localization surfaces.

Middle devices retain same salvage semantics. High/Ultra can spend saved variance on richer recovery HUD, haptics, or scan-log presentation without changing ActiveEquipmentDTO, save identity, StateRingBuffer truth, or authority route.

Decision 051 - RepairTool Continuous Quality Scalar Cut
Problem: RepairTool still scaled sparks and hull-repair signal presentation through GlobalRegistry.ScalabilityTier, GlobalRegistry.ScalabilityTierProfileByte, and IsLowRepairSparkTier() boolean. Hull-repair QualityTier remains existing byte field but now carries 0..255 quantized continuous quality weight.

Polling GlobalRegistry from repair publication was rejected because registry is cold DI only. Renaming or widening HullRepairedSignal was rejected because this cut must not change cross-domain payload layout or save identity.

Middle devices receive intermediate spark counts and caps without hard hardware tier branch. High/Ultra receive richer spark budgets and compute-shard presentation without changing repair truth or hull dent mutation.

Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.05-0.4 microseconds per repair signal burst; stronger value is architectural: presentation quality no longer depends on binary hardware tier or hot registry route.

Solution: Add cachedSpatialAudioManager, hydrate it in CacheRepairAudioCold() during Awake, OnSpawn, and OnEquip, and clear it on disable/despawn/unequip. TryAssignRepairAudioMixerRoute() now only consumes cached manager and leaves mixer unchanged if no cold audio service is available.

Adding new active-equipment audio contract was rejected because this cut only needs existing SpatialAudioManager.SfxGroup sidecar. Clearing repairLoopAudio.outputAudioMixerGroup on release was rejected because that would create avoidable visual/audio churn and is not required for dependency ownership.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid registry property read during repair beam audio route retries and can fail closed with no mixer assignment if cold service is absent. Middle/High/Ultra preserve identical repair loop audio while keeping richer spark/beam presentation budget separate from registry polling.
Hardware Impact: Removes one global audio registry read from each repair mixer assignment retry after cold cache. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.02-0.2 microseconds per beam visual transition; main value is route discipline and lower registry pressure under repeated repair visual toggles.
Decision 053 - RepairTool Cold Vault Cache
Problem: RepairTool.ResolveDataVault() lazily read GlobalRegistry.DataVault. That helper is reached from hull-dent repair and blackbox recording, so first action after lifecycle entry could bootstrap Vault dependency ownership from hot repair path.
Solution: Add CacheRepairVaultCold() on Awake, OnSpawn, and OnEquip. If cached Vault service changes, release current repair descriptors first, then store new IDataVault. ResolveDataVault() now returns dataVault only. Existing VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors remain buffer route.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping lazy action-time discovery was rejected because GlobalRegistry is cold identity/DI only. Holding old owned blackbox descriptors across Vault service swap was rejected because it risks refcount leakage. Changing hull dent or repair blackbox buffer IDs was rejected because this cut is only ownership-route repair.

Decision 054 - RepairTool Cold Renderable And Localization Cache
Problem: RepairTool.ResolveDiegeticTooltipSystem() was static read accessor that scanned GlobalRegistry.Renderables whenever integrity diagnostics were published or cleared. ResolveLocalized() also read Hecton8.Core.GlobalRegistry.Localization from static HUD/log helpers, so repair display paths still contained hidden registry polling after action, quality, audio, and Vault cuts.

Add scachedRepairLocalizationManager, hydrate it in CacheRepairLocalizationCold() during same lifecycle entries, and make static ResolveLocalized() consume that cold cached service. static localization cache is not cleared on despawn because localization service identity is global and clearing it from one pooled repair instance could break another active instance.

Rewriting every static repair HUD/log builder into instance methods was rejected for this loop because it would mix routing cut with broad legacy formatter migration. Clearing static localization cache on every disable/despawn was rejected because pooled multi-instance ordering would become hidden dependency.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid O(R) renderable scans and repeated localization registry property reads during repair diagnostics and HUD/log emission. Middle devices retain identical text and diagnostic behavior. High/Ultra can spend saved variance on richer repair diagnostic styling, sparks, haptics, or shader scalar presentation without changing repair truth, ActiveEquipmentDTO, save identity, Vault buffers, or SignalBus payload layouts.
Hardware Impact: Removes one renderable bucket scan from each integrity diagnostic publish/clear and one global localization registry read from each repair HUD/log resolve. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.05-0.6 microseconds per diagnostic/HUD event, with Quest-class ARM benefiting from lower global bucket traversal and managed service access pressure.

Widening ToolEffectSignal to carry AUP source was rejected because this loop must not alter shared payload ABI without route card. Removing weldLight/particle Transform placement was rejected because those are presentation-owned component transforms, not gameplay ray authority.

High/Ultra can spend saved variance on richer beam width, sparks, or shader scalars while repair truth remains AUP dent mutation plus typed signals.
Hardware Impact: Removes one cached Transform field, one Awake transform capture, two local-space transform position/rotation/scale reads per repair beam hit/preview update, and one transform-position blackbox fallback. Compute unchanged-signal float delta through math.smoothstep and math.lerp across existing low/mid/high/ultra delta constants. Removing legacy low-tier flag was rejected because downstream consumers may still use bit; scalar-derived compatibility is safer.

Hardware Impact: Removes one scalability registry dependency and tier switch/branch cluster from unchanged tool-state publication checks. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.03-0.35 microseconds per unchanged slot publication check, with larger value from smoother low-pressure signal throttling.
