Interior carrier recoil now resolves HullRigidbody from cached submarine context, falling back to cached context's fluid owner only for rigidbody component.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Time.frameCount was rejected because dispatcher-owned frame identity is project route. Keeping parent search was rejected because carrier identity is already registry-published runtime context. Caching SubmarineFluidDynamics directly was rejected because active equipment should not own fluid runtime identity.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid hierarchy scraping when player is inside vehicle/base interior. Middle/High/Ultra preserve recoil behavior and can spend recovered variance on richer impact feedback through typed signals.
Hardware Impact: Removes one Unity frame read per loadout signal and one parent component scrape from interior carrier refresh. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.03-0.4 microseconds per affected event; larger value is compile-wall and route discipline.
Decision 064 - ToolHitUtility Bounded Search And Typed Impact Lane
Problem: ToolHitUtility still used unbounded parent component probes in active damage, item, rigidbody, and mobility routes, and pure ImpactSignal publication went through broader GlobalSignals.Publish wrapper.
Solution: Route all component resolution through existing 32-parent bounded helper, prefer Collider.attachedRigidbody before fallback parent walk, and publish impact packets via SignalBusImpactSignal.Push. ModularEquipmentEngine intentionally keeps GlobalSignals.Publish(in ToolStateChangedSignal) because that wrapper updates latest-tool snapshot used by visor and diegetic tool UI.
Rejected Alternatives: Scene search, reflection, and SendMessage were rejected because they are unbounded and not type-safe. Replacing ToolStateChangedSignal with raw SignalBusT was rejected after inspection because it would drop TryGetLatestToolStateChangedSignal side effects.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid unbounded utility lookups on hits and collectibles. Middle/High/Ultra preserve behavior and use saved variance for impact audio/VFX consumers without changing hit truth or signal payload layout.
Hardware Impact: Removes several unbounded component lookups from active tool-hit paths and one pure publish shim from impact events. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.05-0.6 microseconds on hit-heavy frames, with improved branch predictability from direct attached-rigidbody first.
Decision 065 - Active Equipment Physics And Pickup Contract Route
Problem: active equipment hit/recoil/pickup edge still had direct PhysicsForceRouter use for player-body impulse, concrete HectonItem/PickupItem type checks for collectible preview/quantity, legacy AUP/frame helpers in pickup signals, and action-time GlobalRegistry.ObjectPool reads during item consumption.
Solution: Split hit impulse routing by ownership: player bodies now use cold-cached IPlayerMovementForceSink.QueueExternalVelocityChange, while non-player rigidbodies use cold-cached IPhysicsService. Add IInventoryPickupPreviewSource as optional inventory read model so ToolHitUtility can preview item/quantity through contracts. Cache player inventory, player pose context, and object pool in HectonItem/PickupItem lifecycle paths. Build acquired-item AUP from IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() and stamp item signals with TimeSliceScheduler.CurrentFrameId.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping generic physics on player bodies was rejected because it bypasses movement authority and rollback-owned velocity integration. Replacing CombatDamageRuntime was rejected because no current contract preserves weakspot/status/mobility damage semantics. Replacing item torque/ambient physics was rejected because IPhysicsService has no torque route and dropping torque would change item overflow/loose-current presentation. Replacing RepairTool.BaseModule or scanner voxel links was rejected by audit because no behavior-equivalent contract exists yet.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid concrete pickup type tests, active registry reads, and generic player-force routing. Middle devices preserve existing pickup/recoil semantics through cached contracts. High/Ultra can spend saved edge variance on richer impact, pickup, and overheat presentation because gameplay truth remains one owned route and item/quantity readback is still deterministic.
Hardware Impact: Removes concrete item checks from active hit collection, one generic physics enqueue path for player recoil, one player-inventory registry read, one object-pool registry read per pooled item consumption, and legacy frame/AUP helper dependencies. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.05-0.8 microseconds per hit/pickup/recoil edge, with lower variance on Quest-class ARM.
Decision 066 - Item Overflow Physics Service Route
Problem: Loop 57 left item overflow scatter on direct PhysicsForceRouter.QueueForce / QueueTorque because I assumed public physics service did not expose torque. Source proof in GlobalRegistryContracts.cs and PhysicsApplySystem.cs shows IPhysicsService.QueueTorque is available for critical deferred packets. Keeping direct overflow routing would preserve avoidable static router edge in item pickup overflow while cold DI route already exists.
Solution: Add cold cached IPhysicsService references to HectonItem and PickupItem, reset them on subsystem registration, refresh them from lifecycle cold entries, and route overflow scatter impulse/torque through IPhysicsService.QueueForce / QueueTorque. HectonItem now refreshes cache in Start() as well as Awake() / OnEnable() to cover bootstrap ordering. PickupItem loose-current drift remains on PhysicsForceRouter.QueueAmbientForce / QueueAmbientTorque because service contract does not expose ForcePacketPriority.Ambient or biome buoyancy flags.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving overflow on PhysicsForceRouter was rejected because behavior-equivalent service contract exists. Routing loose-current ambient drift through critical IPhysicsService.QueueForce was rejected because it would silently change packet priority and biome-buoyancy metadata. Editing public physics service contract in this loop was rejected because that is core physics route card, not active-equipment patch. Removing overflow torque was rejected because it would weaken item scatter presentation.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid static router EnsureRuntimeInstance work on inventory-overflow scatter while retaining same deferred packet owner. Middle devices keep identical item spill feedback. High/Ultra can preserve richer scatter torque and spend saved variance on pickup VFX/audio without changing item truth, save identity, or pickup signal layout.
Hardware Impact: Removes direct static force-router calls from item overflow paths and uses cached service slot instead. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.03-0.35 microseconds per overflow scatter edge; Quest-class ARM benefits mainly from fewer static router and service-resolution branches. Ambient current drift remains documented as pending ambient-service contract.
Decision 067 - Active Equipment Pose-Relative AUP Conversion
Problem: ScannerTool, RepairTool, and ModularEquipmentEngine still had owned helpers that converted runtime positions through GlobalSignals.CurrentRuntimeOriginAup(). That helper is legacy global bridge and treats runtime coordinates as origin-relative offset; active tools already cache player pose snapshots, so continuing to use bridge violates owner-local AUP precision policy.
Solution: Replace those conversions with pose-relative math. Scanner acoustic pings pass already-resolved PlayerRuntimePoseSnapshot into ping publisher. Repair tool world points resolve through TryGetPlayerRuntimeContext() and TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot(). Modular equipment thermal-grid root conversion uses playerRuntimeContext. Each route subtracts snapshot.RuntimePosition from target runtime position, offsets snapshot.Aup by that double-precision delta, and validates finite output.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping GlobalSignals.CurrentRuntimeOriginAup() was rejected because it is global bridge, not cached player authority. Using raw AbsoluteUniversePosition.FromRuntimePosition was rejected because it reintroduces runtime-origin ambiguity. Adding new global AUP service was rejected because cached player pose is already authoritative owner for these tool-space conversions.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid global bridge reads and get deterministic fail-closed behavior when no valid pose snapshot exists. Middle devices keep identical scanner ping, repair spark, hull dent, and thermal-grid behavior when pose is available. High/Ultra retain same AUP truth and can spend saved variance on richer acoustic, spark, and thermal presentation without changing DTO layout or authority routes.
Hardware Impact: Removes one global AUP bridge read from scanner acoustic pings, repair voxel/spark/blackbox/hull dent conversions, and modular thermal-grid root refresh. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.02-0.4 microseconds per affected event, with primary gain being precision safety at large world offsets.
Decision 068 - Item Acquisition Typed Signal Lane
Problem: HectonItem and PickupItem still published ItemAcquiredSignal through GlobalSignals.Publish. Source proof in GlobalSignals.cs shows this specific wrapper only calls EnsureInitialized() and SignalBusItemAcquiredSignal.Push, so item owner path can use first-party typed lane directly without losing latest-state side effects.
Solution: Replace two item-owner GlobalSignals.Publish(in signal) calls with SignalBusItemAcquiredSignal.Push(in signal). ToolStateChangedSignal remains on GlobalSignals.Publish in ModularEquipmentEngine because that wrapper updates latest-tool snapshot used by UI consumers.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving item path on GlobalSignals.Publish was rejected because it preserves legacy bridge where typed lane is behavior-equivalent. Replacing ToolStateChangedSignal was rejected because it is not behavior-equivalent. Adding new pickup event bus was rejected because SignalBusItemAcquiredSignal is already canonical hot broadcast path.
Scalability potential: Low devices skip one wrapper call on manual pickup acquisition signals. Middle devices preserve acquisition telemetry. High/Ultra can spend saved variance on richer pickup presentation while item truth, DTO layout, and save identity stay unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes one legacy bridge call per manual item acquisition. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.01-0.08 microseconds per pickup signal; main value is route discipline and first-party SignalBus proof.
Decision 069 - Scanner Pickup Preview Contract
Problem: ScannerTool still stored concrete PickupItem in ScanAggregate and read pickup.ItemData during scan classification. That reintroduced scanner-to-pickup concrete edge after IInventoryPickupPreviewSource already existed for active pickup preview.
Solution: Change scanner aggregation to store IInventoryPickupPreviewSource, assign it from hit.Owner as IInventoryPickupPreviewSource, and add TryPeekPickupItemData() to fetch ItemData and quantity through contract. Scanner item discovery and resource-pickup classification now use interface read model.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping PickupItem in scanner aggregate was rejected because it violates same compile-wall contract route fixed in ToolHitUtility. Duplicating item metadata into scanner-only DTO was rejected because existing preview contract is sufficient. Dropping pickup scan classification was rejected because item/resource discovery is user-facing scanner behavior.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid concrete pickup type dependency and keep one compact contract call per pickup aggregate. Middle devices preserve scanner item/resource classification. High/Ultra can spend saved dependency surface on richer scanner presentation without changing scan truth or signal layouts.
Hardware Impact: Runtime gain is small, estimated 0.01-0.12 microseconds per pickup aggregate, but compile-wall isolation improves because scanner no longer references PickupItem concrete type for discovery.
Decision 070 - ToolHitUtility Packet Damage Fallback
Problem: ToolHitUtility.ApplyDamage() still had direct HectonSurvivalSystem.TakeDamage(damage) fallback after central combat and cuttable routes failed. That made active equipment survival concrete caller and kept read-shaped bounded hierarchy search named TryResolveParentComponent.
Solution: Remove survival concrete fallback. If target has IDamageReceiver but is not registered with CombatDamageRuntime, send canonical DamagePacket with DamageChannel.Integrity, finite local point, impact type, and DamageSourceIds.EnvironmentHazard. Registered targets still use central combat queue. Rename bounded search helpers to TryFindParentComponentBounded, TryFindCuttableTarget, and TryFindDamageReceiverTarget. Add finite guards for damage magnitude, impulse magnitude, normalized direction, and local point packing.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding new survival-specific damage contract was rejected because IDamageReceiver and DamagePacket already exist as canonical packet ingress. Calling IPlayerRuntimeContext.PlayerHealth.TakeDamage was rejected because it would create another concrete player-health side route and bypass packet metadata. Directly calling ReceiveDamage on registered combat targets was rejected because it would bypass weakspot/status/telemetry handling owned by CombatDamageRuntime.
Scalability potential: Low devices skip concrete survival probe and get fail-closed finite packet data. Middle devices preserve packet damage behavior for unregistered contract receivers. High/Ultra can spend saved edge variance on richer impact feedback while damage truth remains central queue first, packet receiver second, cuttable owner when authored.
Hardware Impact: Removes one direct survival component probe from non-central/non-cuttable hit edges and avoids NaN direction/local-point propagation into combat packets. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.02-0.2 microseconds per edge hit; Quest-class ARM benefits mainly from cleaner branch routing and fewer concrete gameplay type dependencies.
Decision 071 - RepairTool Audio Contract Mixer Cache
Problem: RepairTool cached SpatialAudioManager and read SfxGroup only to route its loop AudioSource. That preserved active-equipment to audio concrete dependency, even though public IAudioService contract already owns mixer group exposure.
Solution: Replace cachedSpatialAudioManager with cachedRepairAudioMixerGroup. CacheRepairAudioCold() reads GlobalRegistry.Audio once from lifecycle cold paths and stores audioService.AmbientGroup as mixer route. TryAssignRepairAudioMixerRoute() now assigns only cached AudioMixerGroup; it does not cast to SpatialAudioManager or poll registry. Existing authored AudioSource.outputAudioMixerGroup still wins.
Rejected Alternatives: Widening IAudioService to expose SfxGroup was rejected because that touches massive global contract and all audio implementations for narrow repair-tool cut. Keeping concrete cast was rejected because it preserves compile-wall edge. Assigning new serialized required mixer was rejected because existing prefab data may not be authored and this pass must remain source-safe.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid concrete audio service casts and repair-loop mixer dependency churn. Middle devices keep deterministic cold routing through audio owner. High/Ultra can spend recovered variance on richer repair sparks/loop modulation while audio truth remains owned by audio service and repair gameplay truth is unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes one concrete manager cast and one SfxGroup property dereference from repair audio cold refresh paths. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.02-0.2 microseconds per repair lifecycle refresh; compile-wall isolation is primary gain.
Decision 072 - Scanner Scientific Voxel Read Model
Problem: ScannerTool imported Hecton8.Caves, called HectonVoxelVolume.TryRaymarchAnyPublishedSdf, stored write-only HectonVoxelVolume, and sampled density through volume concrete. That made active equipment depend on voxel/caves runtime and used static read path that prunes stale published-volume entries while answering read.
Solution: Extend existing IVoxelSonarSdfReadModel contract with exact-source SDF raymarch and nearest-density sample methods, add 64-byte explicit VoxelSonarSdfRaycastHit DTO, and add IVoxelSonarSdfSampleSource for owner-local spatial hits. HectonVoxelEngine implements read model by looping its existing active volume registry without mutating static published-volume list. HectonVoxelVolume implements sample-source contract. ScannerTool cold-caches GlobalRegistry.VoxelSonarSdf, hot-swaps on VoxelEngineRuntime, consumes contract payload, and removes caves import plus write-only volume field.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping scanner on HectonVoxelVolume.TryRaymarchAnyPublishedSdf was rejected because it preserves sibling concrete edge and mutating read helper. Returning only hit without exact SDF payload was rejected because overlapping volumes could make scanner resample wrong nearest SDF. Deleting voxel scientific contact was rejected because it is user-facing scanner behavior. Adding new registry slot was rejected because existing voxel-engine runtime already exposes IVoxelSonarSdfReadModel.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cheap SDF raymarch "Dear Lie" instead of Unity physics or mesh colliders, with scanner cadence still controlled by continuous quality weight. Middle devices preserve scientific density/chemical classification through exact payload sampling. High/Ultra can spend saved coupling and static-list churn on richer scanner presentation while voxel truth stays world-owned.
Hardware Impact: Removes scanner-to-caves compile edge, one static published-volume route, and write-only managed volume field from focused scientific SDF scans. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.03-0.4 microseconds per focused scanner resample; Quest-class ARM benefits primarily from fewer cross-domain branches and pure owner-read route.
Decision 073 - Scanner Hazard Read Model And Pose-AUP Route
Problem: ScannerTool.ResolveScientificWaterMetrics() still called HectonHazardManager.GetHazardIntensity(Vector3, HazardType.Toxicity). That static helper resolves hazard owner through registry fallback and converts runtime position through legacy runtime-origin AUP bridge. scanner also had no interface boundary for hazard intensity reads.
Solution: Add IHazardZoneReadModel with pure AUP-based GetHazardIntensity(in AbsoluteUniversePosition, HazardType) method, implement it on HazardZoneManager, and cache that read model inside ScannerTool during cold service binding and Environment/HazardZone hot-swap notifications. Scanner toxicity now builds AUP from cachedPlayerContext.TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot() plus local runtime delta through existing pose-relative TryResolveRuntimeAup, then queries cached hazard read model.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping HectonHazardManager was rejected because it hides registry fallback and runtime-origin conversion in read helper. Storing HazardZoneManager directly in scanner was rejected because it preserves concrete hazard edge. Changing IEnvironmentRuntimeContext.HazardZones to new interface was rejected in this loop because it would widen global context ABI used by many systems; scanner can cast existing owner to read interface without destabilizing environment contract.
Scalability potential: Low devices fail closed to zero toxicity if player pose or hazard read model is unavailable and avoid static bridge in scientific scanner contacts. Middle devices preserve toxicity/salinity behavior through same hazard owner. High/Ultra can spend cleaner route on richer scanner water-column visualization; GlobalQualityWeight remains presentation/cadence only and does not change hazard truth, DTO layout, save identity, or ownership.
Hardware Impact: Removes one static hazard helper call and one legacy runtime-origin AUP conversion from each scientific water-metric toxicity sample. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.02-0.25 microseconds per scientific contact, with stronger precision safety at large coordinates and lower compile-wall pressure.
Decision 074 - Scanner Survival Environment Read Model
Problem: ScannerTool still stored HectonSurvivalSystem and read EnvironmentTemperature / Depth from scientific water metrics. value was read-shaped, but scanner kept concrete survival owner and retry timer only to fetch two scalar facts.
Solution: Add explicit 16-byte PlayerSurvivalEnvironmentSnapshot and IPlayerSurvivalEnvironmentReadModel. HectonSurvivalSystem owns scalar snapshot, PlayerRuntimeContextService exposes it through player context service, and ScannerTool cold-caches interface via player runtime context. Scanner water metrics fall back to IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetMovementRuntimeState() for depth plus scanner's abyssal default temperature when survival is unavailable.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping survival concrete in scanner was rejected because it preserves compile-wall edge for two scalar reads. Reading IPlayerRuntimeContext.SurvivalSystem from scanner was rejected because it still exposes concrete survival owner. Widening PlayerSurvivalRuntimeState was rejected because that 128-byte rollback-facing snapshot should not be resized for scanner presentation. Defaulting depth to zero was rejected when movement already publishes valid depth scalar.
Scalability potential: Low devices get same cheap scalar water-column model with no survival concrete cache and no retry timer. Middle devices preserve ambient temperature/depth scientific text. High/Ultra can spend saved variance and cleaner ownership on richer scanner water-column rendering while survival truth, save identity, and rollback DTO layout remain unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes one concrete survival field/cache, one retry timer branch, and concrete property reads from scientific water metrics. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.02-0.2 microseconds per scientific scan contact; compile-wall isolation is primary gain.
Decision 075 - Scanner Chemical Influence Read Model
Problem: ScannerTool still imported Hecton8.World and called ChemicalInfluenceGrid static/published-buffer helpers for chemical channels, nearest blood scent, and attractant gradients. Those helpers are read-shaped to scanner but can touch static runtime selection and published buffers owned by world chemical system. Scanner also carried HazardType only to request toxicity from hazard read model.
Solution: Add IChemicalInfluenceReadModel to core contracts, register active ChemicalInfluenceGrid owner through new ChemicalInfluenceRuntime GlobalRegistry slot, and move scanner chemical reads to cold-cached interface plus hot-swap update. ChemicalInfluenceGrid exposes pure read methods for normalized channels, nearest blood waypoint, and blood/exhaust gradients using its own Vault-backed buffers. IHazardZoneReadModel now exposes GetToxicityIntensity(in AbsoluteUniversePosition) so scanner avoids hazard enum dependency.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping static grid methods was rejected because active equipment would still depend on world concrete ownership and static publication state. Copying chemical buffers into scanner memory was rejected because it creates shadow state and violates one owner per fact. Widening scanner signals was rejected because chemical truth and payload layout do not need to change. Leaving HazardType in scanner was rejected because toxicity is only scanner hazard read in this path.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep O(1) chemical channel samples and bounded O(N breadcrumbs) owner-side gradient pass only when scanner scientific feedback asks for it; cadence/presentation still degrade through existing continuous scanner quality weight. Middle devices preserve blood/exhaust guidance. High/Ultra can spend cleaner route on richer shader/visor presentation while chemical truth, DTO layout, save identity, and authority route remain unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes scanner's sibling world import, one static chemical runtime bridge, and hazard enum dependency from scientific contact sampling. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.03-0.45 microseconds per scientific chemical contact; Quest-class ARM benefits mainly from lower branch/static-router variance and compile-wall isolation.
Decision 076 - Scanner Atlas Signal Read Snapshot
Problem: ScannerTool still cached AtlasSignalSystem and read CurrentStrength, CurrentRevealStage, and DirectionToCore. DirectionToCore getter resolves player AUP internally through Atlas owner, so scanner read path could trigger hidden owner lookup instead of using scanner's cached player pose.
Solution: Add explicit 32-byte AtlasSignalReadSnapshot and IAtlasSignalReadModel. AtlasSignalSystem implements read model and computes direction from observer AUP supplied by scanner. GlobalRegistry.AtlasSignalReadModel exposes interface without changing existing Atlas runtime slot. Scanner operational summary/directive now call TryReadAtlasSignalSnapshot(in poseSnapshot.Aup, out snapshot) and consume raw fields.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping concrete AtlasSignalSystem cache was rejected because it preserves sibling runtime edge for scalar text. Reading old DirectionToCore getter was rejected because it hides player-context resolution in read accessor. Moving Atlas event queues into core was rejected because scanner still needs existing Atlas event lane and this loop only cuts scalar read path.
Scalability potential: Low devices skip hidden Atlas player-resolution during scanner text refreshes and fail closed if player pose is unavailable. Middle devices preserve Atlas detection/navigation text. High/Ultra can spend cleaner route on richer scanner bearing visualization while Atlas truth, save identity, event payloads, and scanner blackbox layout remain unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes one concrete Atlas runtime cache and one hidden player-AUP resolution path from scanner operational refreshes. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.02-0.25 microseconds per scanner operational string refresh; compile-wall isolation is main gain.
Decision 077 - Scanner Lore Unlock Read Model
Problem: ScannerTool cached LoreDatabaseManager only to ask whether threat-prediction lore hash was unlocked. existing LoreDatabaseManager.IsUnlocked(uint) path calls TryGetRecordIndex, which can build lore hash dictionary through BuildLookupIfNeeded; that violates pure read-accessor discipline when reached from scanner scientific presentation.
Solution: Add ILoreUnlockReadModel and expose it as GlobalRegistry.LoreUnlockReadModel. LoreDatabaseManager implements IsLoreUnlocked(uint) with fixed IndustrialLoreBitMask.RecordCount linear scan over static srecords, then calls IsUnlocked(index) for already-resolved index. ScannerTool now caches ILoreUnlockReadModel, removes narrative import, and calls IsLoreUnlocked.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping concrete LoreDatabaseManager cache was rejected because it preserves narrative runtime edge. Reusing IsUnlocked(uint) was rejected because it may mutate/build dictionary. Adding scanner-owned unlock cache was rejected because lore unlock truth belongs to narrative/lore persistence. Moving title buffers into scanner was rejected because this pass only needs single unlock bit.
Scalability potential: Low devices get deterministic bounded 50-record static scans only when scientific fauna contact has nonzero threat lore hash. Middle devices preserve flanking/threat text behavior. High/Ultra can spend cleaner route on richer scanner decryption presentation while lore truth, save identity, and scanner DTO layout stay unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes scanner's concrete lore database dependency and hidden dictionary-build risk. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.02-0.35 microseconds per rare threat-lore check; primary gain is read-path purity and compile-wall isolation.
Decision 078 - Scanner Hazard Fallback Interface Property
Problem: After hazard read-model cut, ScannerTool.SelectHazardZoneReadModelCold() still had last-resort GlobalRegistry.HazardZones read. It was cold, but static scans still saw scanner reaching toward concrete hazard owner.
Solution: Add GlobalRegistry.HazardZoneReadModel and map IHazardZoneReadModel to HazardZoneRuntime. Scanner fallback now reads interface property, not concrete hazard property.

Decision 079 - Repair Voxel Weld Command Interface
Problem: RepairTool still imported Hecton8.Caves, cached HectonVoxelVolume, and called ApplyRepairWeldDda directly when repairing voxel terrain. operation is legitimate tool behavior, but concrete caves owner in active equipment keeps compile-wall dirty.
Solution: Add IVoxelRepairWeldTarget beside existing voxel sonar contracts, implement it explicitly on HectonVoxelVolume, and have RepairTool discover/cache only interface. method name is TryApplyRepairWeldDda because it is command that mutates voxel delta state, not pure read accessor.

Moving voxel delta mutation into RepairTool was rejected because it would violate voxel ownership and duplicate DDA/weld logic. Decision 080 - Scanner Atlas Event Listener Removal
Problem: ScannerTool still imported Hecton8.AtlasSignal, implemented IAtlasSignalEventListener, and registered with AtlasSignalEvents only to invalidate legacy operational string cache. Atlas scalar read path was already moved to IAtlasSignalReadModel, so event listener kept sibling event-bus dependency with no gameplay-truth ownership.

Moving AtlasSignalEvents into core was rejected because it would widen core contract surface and affect non-SHINOBU consumers. Duplicating Atlas fields in scanner was rejected because Atlas truth belongs to Atlas owner.

High/Ultra can spend presentation budget on richer bearing/UI effects while Atlas truth, payloads, save identity, and authority route remain unchanged.

Decision 081 - Voxel Scanner Contracts Namespace Cut
Problem: Assets/Project/Scripts/Core/Contracts/GroundRadarContracts.cs was physically in Core contracts assembly, but scanner/repair voxel contracts declared namespace Hecton8.World. Scanner had already removed its world import, so this was both compile-risk and misleading compile-wall marker.

Adding duplicate World aliases was rejected because interface aliasing would create assignability traps.

Decision 082 - LaserCutter Audio Residency And Survival Snapshot Contracts

Problem: ToolDurabilitySystem still stored HectonSurvivalSystem for underwater/stress corrosion and reached ResourceDistributionDirector.ActiveRuntimeInstance for brine density. That put durability owner on concrete survival and world-resource routes during slow-tick corrosion.
