Decision 084 - Modular Equipment Player Snapshot Route
Problem: ModularEquipmentEngine still used IPlayerRuntimeContext.SurvivalSystem and IPlayerRuntimeContext.PlayerMovement to resolve depth, underwater state, and fallback equipment AUP. That gave equipment owner concrete survival/movement access while preparing native tool input.
Solution: Use IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetMovementRuntimeState for depth and underwater flags, and TryGetPlayerPoseSnapshot for equipment AUP. concrete movement fallback was removed; unavailable snapshots fail closed to zero depth/no AUP instead of searching concrete owners.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping HectonPlayerMovement.CurrentAup as fallback was rejected because pose snapshots already publish owner-approved AUP route. Keeping HectonSurvivalSystem.Depth was rejected because movement snapshots already carry sanitized depth. Adding equipment-local pose cache was rejected because it would create shadow state.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid concrete component dereferences while refreshing active tool inputs. Middle devices keep identical depth and underwater behavior from published player snapshot. High/Ultra can use same clean route for richer equipment VFX and telemetry without changing gameplay truth, save identity, or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: Removes concrete movement/survival property chains from equipment input refreshes. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.03-0.45 microseconds per refresh edge; more important gain is compile-wall isolation and snapshot-only authority.
Decision 085 - Manta Movement Stress Snapshot Route
Problem: MantaScooter still stored HectonPlayerMovement, HectonSurvivalSystem, and bootstrap player-transform fallback only to read underwater state, depth, predicted AUP, hull stress, and abyssal counter-drive scalar. That kept active equipment bound to concrete player/survival ownership during active scooter ticks.
Solution: Add PlayerMovementStressRuntimeState as explicit 16-byte player-runtime snapshot: offset 0 HullStress01 (4), offset 4 UnderwaterStressIntensity01 (4), offset 8 AbyssalCounterDriveEnergyMultiplier (4), offset 12 Flags (4), total 16 bytes. PlayerRuntimeContextService publishes it in player owner phase beside existing 128-byte movement snapshot. MantaScooter now reads movement, depth, predicted AUP, underwater flags, and stress through IPlayerRuntimeContext.TryGetMovementRuntimeState / TryGetMovementStressRuntimeState.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping playerMovement as fallback was rejected because fallback concrete reads are still concrete reads. Moving hull stress or overstrain into Manta was rejected because player movement owns those facts. Widening PlayerMovementRuntimeState was rejected because it is 128-byte existing ABI used by multiple consumers; separate 16-byte snapshot avoids layout churn.
Scalability potential: Low devices get fail-closed scooter activation when player snapshots are absent and avoid bootstrap/component search during active use. Middle devices preserve depth, underwater, hull-stress misfire, and abyssal battery-overstrain behavior from owner-published data. High/Ultra can spend cleaner route on richer headlight/silt/BRG presentation while gameplay truth, save identity, and authority route stay unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes concrete component chains and bootstrap transform search from scooter activation/movement/depth paths. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.04-0.55 microseconds per active scooter tick/input edge; larger gain is compile-wall isolation and deterministic snapshot authority.
Decision 086 - Manta Acoustic Cue Interface
Problem: After player snapshot cut, MantaScooter still imported Hecton8.Audio, stored AcousticZoneController, and read GlobalRegistry.AcousticZone only to play one hull-stress misfire cue. That single cue kept sibling audio runtime type in active equipment.
Solution: Add IToolAcousticCueService in core contracts, expose GlobalRegistry.ToolAcousticCues from existing AcousticZoneRuntime slot, and implement interface explicitly on AcousticZoneController. Manta caches interface and calls PlayMantaMisfire(float) without seeing concrete audio owner.
Rejected Alternatives: Deleting cue was rejected because audio feedback is authored damage affordance. Keeping concrete controller was rejected because it preserves compile-wall edge. Adding new SignalBus lane was rejected because this is one local one-shot audio command, not shared state broadcast.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep cheap edge cue or can ignore audio downstream; Middle devices preserve misfire feedback. High/Ultra can enrich acoustic owner implementation later without changing Manta or gameplay truth. Quality weight does not affect Manta state ownership or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: Removes one concrete audio field and one concrete registry property from Manta. Edge-path gain is small, estimated 0.01-0.12 microseconds on i3/MX350-class hardware, with compile-wall isolation as practical win.
Decision 087 - Manta Babel Localization Contract
Problem: MantaScooter still resolved HUD/directive strings through GlobalRegistry.Localization and LocalizationManager.GetOrFallback, using legacy string keys from LocalizationKeys. That left active equipment with concrete localization owner read even though Core IBabelLocalization contract already exists.
Solution: Cache IBabelLocalization through existing registry hot-swap path, include LocalizationRuntime in relevant service slots, and resolve Manta labels by generated H8LocHashes.MANTA hashes through TryGetLocalizedBuffer. String materialization remains cold/event cache step because existing Manta summary and warning fields are string-backed; no Tick/LateFrame localization lookup was added.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping LocalizationManager.GetOrFallback was rejected because it preserves concrete localization compile edge. Polling IBabelLocalization.ActiveLanguageId from gameplay frames was rejected because it turns clean invalidation event into hot service polling. Adding private SignalBus lane for one tool was rejected because localization language changes already have first-party invalidation route.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep fallback strings and avoid any per-frame localization work. Middle devices preserve live language refresh through existing event lane. High/Ultra can later consume same Babel buffers directly with TMP SetCharArray without changing Manta gameplay truth, DTO layout, save identity, or equipment authority.
Hardware Impact: Removes one concrete localization registry read and legacy string-key route from each Manta localization refresh. Hot-frame gain is 0 us because path is cold/event-driven; cold/event edge gain is estimated 0.01-0.08 microseconds, with compile-wall isolation as practical benefit.
Decision 088 - RepairTool Babel Localization Contract
Problem: RepairTool still carried static LocalizationManager cache, read GlobalRegistry.Localization, and passed legacy LocalizationKeys.REPAIRTOOL strings through GetOrFallback. Several call sites sit on UsePrimary, UseSecondary, and operational text paths, so converting Babel buffers to strings at each call would preserve allocation risk.
Solution: Replace concrete cache with IBabelLocalization, hydrate all H8LocHashes.REPAIRTOOL labels into static cached strings during existing cold lifecycle calls, and gate cold refresh by cached interface plus ActiveLanguageId. Runtime label reads now return cached string references from uint hash switch; only new string(buffer, 0, length) path is cold refresh helper.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping LocalizationManager.GetOrFallback was rejected because it preserves concrete localization owner in active equipment. Resolving TryGetLocalizedBuffer on every tool-use call was rejected because it would materialize managed strings during gameplay edges. Adding new SignalBus/event lane for repair labels was rejected because localization already owns language changes and repair tool only needs cached presentation strings.
Scalability potential: Low devices use fallback literals and no per-frame localization work. Middle devices keep generated Babel strings from same cached contract. High/Ultra can later route these cached buffers into TMP SetCharArray or richer visor diagnostics without changing equipment truth, save identity, DTO layout, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Removes one concrete localization registry route and per-call legacy string-key lookup from repair tool diagnostics. Hot-frame allocation impact is 0 B for localized label reads after cold cache; estimated i3/MX350 edge gain is 0.01-0.12 microseconds on repair HUD/log message construction, with compile-wall isolation as primary gain.
Decision 089 - ScannerTool Babel Localization Contract
Problem: ScannerTool still cached LocalizationManager, read GlobalRegistry.Localization, and used legacy LocalizationKeys.SCANNER values through GetOrFallback. Unlike single mode label, scanner text is used by scan results, operation logs, recommendations, cooldown warnings, bearings, and operational directives, so direct Babel buffer conversion at each call would move managed string materialization into gameplay-facing edges.
Solution: Convert scanner localization to generated H8LocHashes.SCANNER uint keys, replace concrete manager cache with IBabelLocalization, and hydrate 52 scanner strings into static cached references during cold lifecycle, language-change, and LocalizationRuntime hot-swap paths. cache is gated by interface reference plus ActiveLanguageId; ResolveLocalized(uint, string) is now fixed hash switch returning cached strings or fallback literals.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping LocalizationManager.GetOrFallback was rejected because it preserves concrete localization owner in active equipment. Resolving TryGetLocalizedBuffer from every scan/recommendation/directive path was rejected because it would allocate managed strings during gameplay-facing text construction. Adding scanner-specific SignalBus lane was rejected because localization already owns language-change event route.
Scalability potential: Low devices use fallback literals and avoid all per-frame localization work. Middle devices keep Babel-provided labels with event-driven refresh. High/Ultra can spend presentation budget on TMP SetCharArray, richer visor typography, or RTL/font-owner work downstream without changing scanner truth, save identity, DTO layout, blackbox layout, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Removes concrete localization owner coupling and prevents per-call Babel string materialization in scanner text edges. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.01-0.14 microseconds per scanner HUD/log/directive text edge; primary gain is compile-wall isolation and 0 B hot-path label allocation after cold cache.
Decision 090 - LaserCutter Babel Localization Contract
Problem: LaserCutter still cached LocalizationManager, read GlobalRegistry.Localization, and resolved legacy LocalizationKeys.LASER values through GetOrFallback. old manager route tracked CurrentLanguage at call time, so naive cached Babel replacement would either allocate strings on every cutter text edge or become stale after language changes.
Solution: Convert cutter text keys to generated H8LocHashes.LASER hashes, replace concrete manager cache with IBabelLocalization, hydrate 29 cutter strings into instance cached references, and register as ILocalizationLanguageChangedListener plus IGlobalRegistryHotSwapListener. ResolveLocalized(uint, string) now returns cached string references from fixed hash switch; refresh is gated by interface reference plus ActiveLanguageId.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping LocalizationManager.GetOrFallback was rejected because it preserves concrete localization owner in active equipment. Converting Babel buffers inside UsePrimary, diagnosis, heat lockout, or operational readouts was rejected because it would materialize managed strings during gameplay-facing paths. Waiting until re-equip for language changes was rejected because it regresses old CurrentLanguage behavior.
Scalability potential: Low devices use fallback literals and no per-frame localization work. Middle devices preserve live Babel labels through localization events. High/Ultra can route cached labels into richer diegetic visor/TMP presentation later without changing cutter damage truth, thermal state, blackbox layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Removes concrete localization owner coupling and per-call legacy string-key lookup from cutter warning/log/readout edges. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.01-0.13 microseconds per text edge, with 0 B hot-path label allocation after cold cache. pre-existing LaserCutterTargetRegistry cold ListCollider scratch remains separate non-localization cleanup target.
Decision 091 - LaserCutter Player Cutting Tension Contract
Problem: LaserCutter still cached HectonPlayerMovement and Rigidbody, read movement properties (IsPlayerSubmerged, CurrentAup, CurrentCuttingTensionNormalized), and invoked movement methods (ApplyCuttingTensionAnchor, ClearCuttingTensionAnchor) directly. tool legitimately needs heavy-salvage tension intent, but direct concrete movement ownership in active equipment violates compile wall and makes recovery logic depend on player internals.
Solution: Add IPlayerCuttingTensionService as narrow command/read facade: set anchor, clear anchor, read normalized tension. HectonPlayerMovement implements it explicitly; PlayerRuntimeContextService exposes it as IPlayerRuntimeContext.CuttingTensionService. LaserCutter now uses pose/movement snapshots for AUP, velocity, and underwater flags, and only sends tension commands through facade.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping concrete movement fallback was rejected because fallback concrete reads are still compile-wall leaks. Moving cutting tension force simulation into LaserCutter was rejected because player movement owns locomotion forces. Widening 128-byte PlayerMovementRuntimeState for tension command data was rejected because command intent does not belong in immutable snapshot.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid concrete movement and rigidbody dereferences in recovery/boil/recoil edges while preserving fail-closed behavior if snapshots are unavailable. Middle devices preserve heavy salvage recovery behavior through player owner. High/Ultra can spend cleaner ownership on richer cutter visuals and haptics while movement truth, save identity, and DTO layout remain unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Removes two concrete fields, one rigidbody velocity read, and several movement property/method calls from cutter recovery/boil/recoil paths. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.03-0.50 microseconds per active cutter recovery edge; compile-wall isolation is primary gain.
Decision 092 - LaserCutter World Command Facades
Problem: LaserCutter still cached SargassumCutManager, called DestructibleOrganicManager.ActiveRuntimeInstance, and dereferenced SubmarineFluidDynamics through submarine.FluidDynamics for open-water heat. Those are world/submarine concrete routes in active equipment hit and boil edges.
Solution: Add ISargassumCutWriteService, IOrganicToolHitService, and IWaterHeatInjectionService. SargassumCutManager, DestructibleOrganicManager, and SubmarineFluidDynamics implement facades; GlobalRegistry exposes SargassumCutWrite and OrganicToolHits; ISubmarineRuntimeContext exposes WaterHeatInjectionService. LaserCutter caches and hot-swap refreshes interfaces only.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping concrete fallbacks was rejected because it preserves compile-wall leak. Deleting organic/sargassum feedback was rejected because authored cutter feedback would regress. Moving world/fluid mutation into LaserCutter was rejected because those facts belong to their owners. Hot-polling registry per beam hit was rejected because registry is cold DI only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep cheap command facades and fail closed if owners are absent. Middle devices preserve cut-mask, organic-hit, and water-heat feedback. High/Ultra can enrich owner implementations with stronger GPU/shader presentation without changing LaserCutter truth, DTO layout, save identity, or authority routes. Quality weight remains presentation/cadence only.
Hardware Impact: Removes three concrete owner dereferences and one static ActiveRuntimeInstance lookup from active cutter hit/boil edges. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.03-0.45 microseconds per active cutter hit edge; compile-wall isolation is primary gain.
Decision 093 - EquipmentInteractionHandler Command Facades
Problem: EquipmentInteractionHandler still imported caves/physics and dispatched queued signals through concrete HectonVoxelVolume, DestructibleOrganicManager.ActiveRuntimeInstance, FloraInteractionManager.ActiveRuntimeInstance, and SubmarineFluidDynamics via submarine.FluidDynamics. That made late-frame interaction queue sibling-runtime router instead of contract dispatcher.
Solution: Add IVoxelPlasmaCutTarget beside voxel Core contracts and implement it explicitly on HectonVoxelVolume. Extend IOrganicToolHitService with TryApplyAttachedFloraToolHit, implemented by DestructibleOrganicManager using its owner-local flora interaction reference. Change queued boil dispatch to consume ISubmarineRuntimeContext.WaterHeatInjectionService. EquipmentInteractionHandler now depends on Core contracts plus existing gameplay/building types.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping concrete fallbacks was rejected because dispatcher would still compile against caves/world/submarine implementation classes. Adding separate flora singleton interface was rejected because attached-flora arbitration belongs with organic owner and would keep two world-owner routes in dispatcher. Moving plasma/organic/fluid mutation into interaction handler was rejected because it would create shadow truth.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep bounded command dispatch and fail closed when owner facades are absent. Middle devices preserve plasma DDA, attached-flora parasite cuts, and boil feedback. High/Ultra can spend clean route on richer owner-side visual overkill while interaction signal layout, Vault queue ownership, save identity, and gameplay truth stay unchanged. Quality weight does not change signal authority.
Hardware Impact: Removes concrete component/static owner checks from late-frame signal dispatch edges and deletes caves/physics import from handler. Estimated i3/MX350 gain is 0.04-0.60 microseconds per queued cutter signal cluster; compile-wall isolation is practical gain.
Decision 094 - EquipmentInteractionHandler Base Module Marker
Problem: After command facade routing, EquipmentInteractionHandler still imported Hecton8.Building only to resolve BaseModule before sending attached-flora cuts. That is concrete building dependency for boolean host proof.
Solution: Add IBaseModuleInteractionHost in Interaction contract file and implement it on BaseModule. handler keeps existing base-module layer gate, then resolves marker interface instead of concrete class.
Rejected Alternatives: Reusing IKinematicRepairTarget was rejected because repair snap capability is not same fact as attached-flora host identity. Trusting layer alone was rejected because it would remove component proof. Keeping concrete BaseModule resolve was rejected because it preserves building compile edge in interaction dispatcher.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same bounded parent search and fail closed if marker is absent. Middle devices preserve attached flora routing. High/Ultra can spend owner-side presentation budget on richer flora reaction without changing interaction signal ABI, Vault queue ownership, save identity, or gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: No meaningful arithmetic gain; this is compile-wall hygiene. It removes one concrete generic component resolution from attached-flora dispatcher path and keeps interaction queue independent of building implementation.
Decision 095 - Repair/Manta Stale Physics Imports
Problem: RepairTool and MantaScooter still imported Hecton8.Physics after prior loops moved movement, hydrodynamic, and repair target behavior onto player snapshots and Core/Interaction contracts. imports no longer resolved any type but still appeared as active equipment physics coupling in static audits.
Solution: Remove stale physics imports and leave runtime code unchanged.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping unused imports was rejected because compile-wall proof relies on source-level dependency hygiene. Expanding this into broader Repair/Manta refactor was rejected because there was no runtime behavior to change in this pass.
Scalability potential: No quality curve changes. Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged; this removes only stale source coupling.
Hardware Impact: 0 microseconds hot-path gain. gain is audit clarity and reduced false dependency surface for active equipment files.
Decision 096 - Repair Module Snapshot Contract
Problem: RepairTool still treated habitat integrity as concrete BaseModule read/write target in active repair and diagnostic edges. That preserved building-runtime authority type in active equipment and encouraged repeated property-style reads (CurrentIntegrity, MaxIntegrity, IsFlooded, IsDraining, HasPower) from tool path.
Solution: Use IRepairableModuleTarget as tool-facing command/read facade and ModuleRepairReadSnapshot as compact immutable repair read model. BaseModule implements interface explicitly, fills snapshot from its owned integrity component, and remains only mutable integrity owner. RepairTool caches only IRepairableModuleTarget, applies repair through ApplyRepair(float), and computes diagnostics from 32-byte snapshot. ToolEffectEvents now carries IRepairableModuleTarget so pre-repair effects stay interface-routed.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping BaseModule in RepairTool was rejected because it keeps compile wall open. Moving integrity/flood flags into RepairTool was rejected because it creates shadow truth. Reading individual module properties repeatedly was rejected because tool only needs coherent diagnostic snapshot.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay one compact snapshot read for repair diagnostics and can fail closed if interface is absent. Middle devices preserve flood, drain, no-power, and restored messages. High/Ultra can spend presentation budget on richer diegetic repair effects downstream without changing integrity ownership, DTO layout, save identity, or authority route. GlobalQualityWeight does not change gameplay truth here.
Hardware Impact: snapshot is StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit, Size = 32): offset 0 float CurrentIntegrity (4), offset 4 float MaxIntegrity (4), offset 8 uint Flags (4), offset 12 uint Pad0 (4), offset 16 ulong Pad1 (8), offset 24 ulong Pad2 (8). Total = 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 8 + 8 = 32 bytes, aligned to 8/16/32-byte boundaries and pointer-free. Estimated active repair/diagnostic edge gain is 0.03-0.35 microseconds on i3/MX350-class hardware from fewer repeated owner reads and cleaner compile-wall routing.
Decision 097 - LaserCutter Fixed Target Registration Scratch
Problem: LaserCutterTargetRegistry used static ListCollider only to collect module child colliders during lifecycle registration. Capacity was preallocated, but it still kept System.Collections.Generic, resize-capable managed collection, and Unity's list-based GetComponentsInChildren route in active-equipment file.
Solution: Replace list with fixed Transform4096 traversal stack. Module registration walks transform tree without allocation and registers first collider on each transform; cache misses in TryResolveModule lazily resolve parent BaseModule once and store collider key. Module unregister scans fixed 4096-slot table and clears all entries owned by that module.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping list was rejected because source audits cannot distinguish safe cold list from future hot misuse. Using GetComponentsInChildrenT() was rejected because it allocates array. Registering every possible collider component on transform through managed component lists was rejected because lazy miss cache covers uncommon multi-collider transforms without retaining list.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid managed list scratch and keep hit route table-first. Middle devices preserve module salvage targeting. High/Ultra can add richer salvage presentation behind same lookup route without changing cutter truth, save identity, DTO layout, or authority ownership.
Hardware Impact: Cold lifecycle cost becomes bounded transform traversal plus fixed-table writes. First hit on unregistered secondary collider pays one bounded 32-depth parent walk and is then cached; normal hit lookup remains O(1). Estimated hot-path gain is 0 us after cache fill; value is zero-GC audit closure and removal of managed-list dependency surface.
Decision 098 - Manta Damage Receiver Fixed Array
Problem: MantaScooter owned ListIDamageSignalReceiver for private transport damage callbacks. Initial capacity was one, but collection could grow and preserved resize-capable managed container in active handheld transport state.
Solution: Replace list with IDamageSignalReceiver4 and damageReceiverCount. Registration deduplicates by reference and fails closed at fixed capacity. Unregistration swaps with last occupied slot and clears tail. Dispatch reads damageReceiverCount once and uses index-based loops.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping list was rejected because active equipment should not own growable managed containers. Publishing every scooter trauma callback through global event bus was rejected because this is private local transport feedback, not cross-domain broadcast fact. Allocating arrays or spans per dispatch was rejected because it moves problem to hot path.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain tiny fixed listener surface for player trauma dispatcher. Middle devices preserve current damage feedback. High/Ultra can add richer presentation behind fixed-capacity downstream receiver without changing scooter truth, active equipment DTOs, save identity, or authority routes.
Hardware Impact: receiver table is managed reference array, not rollback DTO, so no ARM64 blittable layout claim is made. Runtime dispatch avoids List count/indexer and cannot resize; estimated steady-state gain is below 0.1 microseconds, with main value being zero-GC audit closure.
Decision 099 - PlayerTool Equipped State Explicit Field
Problem: active equipment scanner still found public bool IsEquipped get; private set; on PlayerTool. This is managed lifecycle state, not Burst DTO, but auto-property setter hides exact mutation sites and keeps property pattern that SHINOBU audit explicitly tries to remove from active equipment surfaces.
Solution: Replace auto-property with private bool isEquipped and public bool IsEquipped = isEquipped. All equip/despawn lifecycle mutations now write isEquipped directly inside PlayerTool; external consumers keep same read-only API.
Rejected Alternatives: Making IsEquipped public field was rejected because external mutation would destroy lifecycle ownership. Replacing every caller with ReadIsEquipped() was rejected because it churns unrelated call sites and still emits method call. Leaving auto-property was rejected because static audit residue matters in this batch.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra behavior is unchanged. value is explicit ownership and cleaner active equipment audits; gameplay truth, active equipment DTO layout, save identity, and authority route do not change.
Hardware Impact: No measurable runtime gain expected. patch removes one compiler-generated setter/backing-field pattern from shared active tool base and keeps mutation visible for future audits.
Decision 100 - RepairTool SHINOBU Dump Identity
Problem: RepairTool still wrote its repair blackbox dump to Docs/AgentLogs/DumpWELDINGREPAIRLOGIC.bin, stale previous-domain identity. That breaks audit trail when QA collects SHINOBU artifacts.
Solution: Rename repair-specific dump to Docs/AgentLogs/DumpSHINOBU224RepairTool.bin. central active equipment telemetry dump remains Docs/AgentLogs/DumpSHINOBU224.bin because it has different record layout.
Rejected Alternatives: Reusing DumpSHINOBU224.bin for both equipment telemetry and repair dent telemetry was rejected because blind binary dumps with incompatible record formats are harder to triage. Leaving old filename was rejected because forensic ownership must match active agent.
Scalability potential: No quality-tier behavior changes. Low/Middle/High/Ultra all use same crash-only path; runtime gameplay truth and DTO layout are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: 0 microseconds in normal frames. Crash-path file naming only.
Decision 101 - ScannerTool SHINOBU Dump Identity
Problem: ScannerTool still wrote blackbox dumps to DumpDIEGETICLORESCANNER.bin, another stale functional-domain filename that does not identify SHINOBU224 ownership.
Solution: Rename scanner forensics to Docs/AgentLogs/DumpSHINOBU224ScannerTool.bin. Scanner keeps its own binary format and does not collide with central equipment telemetry or repair tool dump.
Rejected Alternatives: Reusing central DumpSHINOBU224.bin was rejected because scanner blackbox entries have separate header/record format. Leaving lore-scanner filename was rejected because ownership must be explicit in QA artifacts.
Scalability potential: No runtime quality changes. All hardware tiers share same crash-only path; scanner gameplay truth, DTO layout, and authority routes are unchanged.
Decision 102 - WFC Door Laser-Cut Facade
Problem: LaserCutterTargetRegistry still stored concrete SealedDoor references for WFC door cutting. That made tool registry depend on gameplay door implementation and kept cutter close to owner-local door/WFC state.
Solution: Add IWfcDoorLaserCutTarget and WfcDoorLaserCutReadSnapshot in Interaction contract surface. SealedDoor implements interface explicitly and returns only sector hash, cell index, and current flags needed by WfcLaserCutRuntime; LaserCutter stores interface and writes back only scalar progress.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping SealedDoor was rejected because cutter should not own door implementation identity. Copying WFC flags into LaserCutter was rejected because it creates shadow state. Routing around WfcLaserCutRuntime was rejected because WFC door truth already has dedicated owner path.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep O(1) interface table and scalar progress. Middle devices preserve WFC seal cutting. High/Ultra can add richer door-edge VFX/audio behind owner-side presentation without changing door truth, save identity, DTO layout, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: WfcDoorLaserCutReadSnapshot is StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit, Size = 16): offset 0 ulong SectorHash (8), offset 8 ushort CellIndex (2), offset 10 byte CurrentFlags (1), offset 11 byte Pad0 (1), offset 12 uint Pad1 (4). Total = 16 bytes, pointer-free, no Pack=1, and aligned for ARM64 reads. Runtime ALU gain is effectively 0; compile-wall and ownership hygiene are gain.
Decision 103 - EquipmentInteractionHandler Hot Registry/Vault Cut
Problem: queued interaction dispatcher still had hot fallback routes where Publish, TryReadQueuedSignal, raycast queueing, raycast completion, and staged raycast scheduling could call GetBufferHandleT if Awake prewarm or rebind missed Vault lane. It also read GlobalRegistry.Submarine and GlobalRegistry.OrganicToolHits from late-frame dispatch helpers.
Solution: Split cold acquisition from hot resolution. Cold setup/rebind calls EnsureSignalQueueHandle(createIfMissing: true) and EnsureRaycastBufferHandles(createIfMissing: true). Hot publish/read/raycast paths call same helpers with createIfMissing: false and fail closed if lane is absent. CacheRegistryDependenciesCold caches ISubmarineRuntimeContext and IOrganicToolHitService, and hot dispatch uses those cached interfaces.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping hot GetBufferHandleT fallback was rejected because missed prewarm would create/grow Vault lanes inside gameplay. Polling GlobalRegistry from each queued signal was rejected because registry is cold DI only. Creating private NativeArrays was rejected because global interaction lanes are Vault-owned.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid any emergency lane acquisition inside late-frame dispatch. Middle devices preserve queued tool signals and raycast batching. High/Ultra can spend interaction output on richer owner-side effects while signal queue identity, Vault buffer IDs, save authority, and DTO layout remain fixed. Quality weight can change cadence/capacity only through existing owner policy, not truth ownership.
Hardware Impact: Removes hot fallback allocation/acquisition branches from interaction signal and raycast paths. Expected resolved-path gain is small, roughly 0.01-0.08 microseconds per signal/raycast cluster on i3/MX350-class hardware; main value is preventing pathological missed-bootstrap lane creation inside frame.
Decision 104 - ToolDurability Cold-Create / Hot-Resolve Vault Split
Problem: ToolDurabilitySystem.Tick() called TryRegisterSaveService() and then EnsureNativeStateViews(). If handles were stale or missing, call chain could release and reacquire durability lanes with GlobalDataVault.GetGenerationHandleT from active update path.
Solution: Remove Tick-side save registration and add create flag to native-state resolution. EnsureNativeStateCold() is only helper that passes createIfMissing:true; it runs in Awake, OnEnable, Start, cold clear/load setup, and DataVault rebind. Tick and gameplay mutation helpers resolve existing handles only through createIfMissing:false; missing lanes fail closed. GetGenerationHandleT remains in one guarded helper.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving Tick fallback acquisition was rejected because it makes Vault ownership depend on runtime timing. Adding private NativeArrays was rejected because durability rows already belong to Vault. Keeping Tick-side save registration was rejected because save service rebind already handles late availability without making every gameplay Tick registration probe.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep durability drain as pure resolve/schedule path and skip work if bootstrap state is unavailable. Middle devices preserve environmental corrosion and durability events. High/Ultra can add stronger presentation behind durability signals without changing durability truth, DTO layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Eliminates hot fallback Vault allocation route and one Tick-side save-registration branch. Normal math cost is unchanged; worst-case missed-bootstrap frame avoids potentially expensive GetGenerationHandleT and dictionary/save registration edge.
Decision 105 - ModularEquipment Cold-Create / Hot-Resolve Vault Split
Problem: ModularEquipmentEngine.Tick() and late-frame completion both called EnsureEquipmentViews(). That helper resolved every active equipment, telemetry, tuning, and upgrade-matrix lane, but on stale/missing handles it released and reacquired with GlobalDataVault.GetGenerationHandleT, which can grow or reallocate Vault storage.
Solution: Give EnsureEquipmentViews explicit createIfMissing flag with default false. InitializeActiveEquipmentNativeState() is only caller that passes true; it is reached during service initialization and DataVault rebind. EnsureEquipmentBuffer now returns false before handle release or GetGenerationHandleT when createIfMissing is false, so Tick, late-frame completion, public service writers, tuning readers, CSV fallback helpers, and post-rebind readback are no-acquire paths.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving default acquisition in Tick and CompleteActiveEquipmentJob was rejected because it permits Vault growth during active simulation and readback. Creating private NativeArrays was rejected because active equipment rows are cross-domain Vault truth. Forcing every public writer to initialize service again was rejected because it can create hidden bootstrap work behind read/write facades.
Scalability potential: Low devices fail closed instead of creating lanes during loaded frame. Middle devices preserve active equipment integration and upgrade-matrix behavior after cold bootstrap. High/Ultra can increase cadence/telemetry/presentation using existing quality curves without changing DTO layout, BufferID identity, save authority, or Vault owner route.
Hardware Impact: Removes worst-case Vault growth/reallocation from active equipment Tick and late-frame completion. Steady-state path is unchanged after handles resolve. remaining DispatcherJobFence.TryFinalizeCompleted is guarded by equipmentIntegrationHandle.IsCompleted; fault-only synchronous telemetry dump remains separate residual crash-export issue.
Decision 106 - Repair/Scanner Blackbox Cold-Create Guard
Problem: RepairTool.ToolTick() records blackbox heartbeat rows every tool tick, and RecordRepairBlackBox could call EnsureRepairBlackBoxHandle, which acquired RepairToolBlackBox through GetGenerationHandleT if cold setup missed lane. Scanner's blackbox allocation was only cold in current call graph, but helper did not encode that boundary.
Solution: Add explicit create gating. CacheRepairVaultCold() calls EnsureRepairBlackBoxHandle(dataVault, createIfMissing:true); RecordRepairBlackBox and DumpRepairBlackBox use default no-create path. ScannerTool.EnsureScannerBlackBoxVault now requires createIfMissing argument and only EnsureScientificNativeState() passes true. Hot scanner writes continue to use TryReadScannerBlackBoxRing only.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Repair hot fallback acquisition was rejected because telemetry proof must not allocate while tool is ticking. Dropping blackbox rows entirely was rejected because 300-frame forensic ring is mandatory. Creating private native buffers was rejected because proof ring is Vault lane.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid blackbox lane acquisition during repair heartbeat/repair-hit paths and simply skip rows if cold setup failed. Middle devices preserve crash forensics after normal bootstrap. High/Ultra can add richer diagnostic exports behind same Vault ring without changing gameplay truth, DTO layout, save identity, or route ownership.
Hardware Impact: Removes worst-case GetGenerationHandleRepairToolBlackBoxEntry from repair tick and hit paths. Scanner runtime cost is unchanged, but cold-create boundary is now explicit. Normal blackbox row writes remain fixed-size NativeArray writes.
Decision 107 - LaserCutter WFC Owner Context Cadence
Problem: LaserCutter.ToolTick() refreshed WFC laser-cut owner context every equipped frame. That call reads WFC and system-health SignalBus snapshots even when cutter is idle, locked out, cooling, or hitting non-WFC target.
Solution: Move WfcLaserCutRuntime.RefreshOwnerPhaseContext() out of ToolTick and into TryApplyWfcDoorCut immediately before WFC runtime mutates door progress. context scan is now paid only by actual registered WFC door cut attempt.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping refresh in ToolTick was rejected because idle presentation/state cleanup should not scan WFC signals. Adding tiny scheduled job was rejected because this is narrow owner-context refresh and not amortized batch work. Copying WFC context into LaserCutter was rejected because it would create shadow state.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid WFC context scans on idle equipped cutter frames. Middle devices preserve WFC door cutting without cadence change. High/Ultra can spend saved frames on owner-side shader clip/spark richness through existing WFC feedback signals; gameplay truth and DTO layout do not change.
Hardware Impact: Removes two SignalBus frame-snapshot scans from ordinary idle cutter frames. Active WFC door cutting still performs same O(k) signal scan before mutation, preserving correctness.
Decision 108 - Scanner Hazard Read-Model Purity
Problem: Scanner hazard selection used environmentContext.HazardZones. In current environment runtime implementation that property can sync/ensure scene state and fallback to manager, making it unsafe to treat as pure read accessor.
Solution: Cache GlobalRegistry.Environment and GlobalRegistry.HazardZoneReadModel only during cold binding/hot-swap. SelectHazardZoneReadModelCold now uses environmentContext as IHazardZoneReadModel plus cached hazard fallback and never invokes environmentContext.HazardZones.
Rejected Alternatives: Expanding IEnvironmentRuntimeContext with new pure TryGetHazardZoneReadModel was rejected in this pass because interface expansion has broader compile-wall impact. Keeping property getter was rejected because read accessors must not mutate/sync scene state. Hot registry fallback was rejected by GlobalRegistry cold-DI doctrine.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid accidental manager ensure/sync during scanner service binding. Middle devices preserve hazard toxicity reads through cached IHazardZoneReadModel. High/Ultra can enrich scanner presentation using same cached toxicity scalar without changing scanner truth ownership, save identity, or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: FastTick toxicity sampling remains cached interface call. gain is removing latent cold-bind scene-sync/property side effect, not changing normal ALU cost.
Decision 109 - Scanner Blackbox Deferred File Export
Problem: ScannerTool.FastTick() could hit WriteScannerBlackBox - DumpScannerBlackBoxOnce on invalid state, executing Directory.CreateDirectory, FileStream, and BinaryWriter from frame route.
Solution: Split detection from disk export. FastTick route records fixed-size Vault row, publishes GlobalTelemetryBus.PublishMathGuardInvalidNumber, and marks scannerBlackBoxDumpPending. OnApplicationQuit and OnDestroy flush pending scanner dump before disposing Vault handle.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping synchronous file I/O inside FastTick was rejected because NaN frame should not add disk stalls to already unstable simulation. Creating new global exporter was rejected because project already has crash telemetry ownership and this pass should not expand global surface. Dropping scanner-specific dump was rejected because blackbox proof artifact is mandatory.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid disk stalls during scanner frames. Middle devices keep forensic rows with lifecycle export. High/Ultra can later route same pending flag into pre-owned background exporter without changing ScannerBlackBoxEntry layout or gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: Normal scanner frame cost is unchanged. Fault frame avoids synchronous file I/O; remaining cost is one bool flag write plus existing math-guard signal publish.
Decision 110 - ModularEquipment Success-Gated Fault Dump Export
Problem: Equipment and upgrade fault detection had been moved off frame route, but deferred exporter cleared equipmentFaultDumpPending / upgradeTelemetryFaultDumpPending before proving that ring resolved and writer succeeded. DumpEquipmentTelemetry and DumpUpgradeTelemetry also marked their dumped flags before validating ring.
Solution: Make both dump helpers return bool. FlushPendingFaultDumps() clears pending flags only after successful writer. Ring resolution failures leave pending state intact for next lifecycle/rebind flush, and file/compiler export failures publish EQDF / UPDF telemetry fault hashes.
Rejected Alternatives: Clearing pending before proof was rejected because it can erase only forensic export request. Writing immediately from fault frame was rejected because disk I/O belongs outside frame processing. new global crash exporter was rejected in this pass because it expands shared surface beyond SHINOBU ownership.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep fault detection as one bool flag write and avoid disk stalls. Middle devices retain same 300-frame forensic ring and lifecycle export. High/Ultra can later route same pending flags into pre-owned background exporter without changing EquipmentTelemetryEntry, UpgradeTelemetryEntry, BufferID identity, or authority ownership.
Hardware Impact: Normal active equipment frames are unchanged. Fault frames avoid millisecond-class FileStream work. Lifecycle/rebind export now pays one branch per pending dump and preserves proof intent on failed writer attempts.
Decision 111 - RepairTool Success-Gated Blackbox Export
Problem: Repair blackbox invalid-math handling had been deferred, but flush helper cleared repairBlackBoxDumpPending before writer returned. OnDespawn also reset pending flag immediately after flush attempt, preventing ReleaseVaultState() from retrying against still-bound Vault handle if first writer failed.
Solution: Make DumpRepairBlackBox return bool, clear repairBlackBoxDumpPending only on success, and remove despawn-side unconditional pending reset. ReleaseVaultState() can now retry failed despawn export before releasing Vault handle.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping void dump helper was rejected because caller state could not distinguish success from skipped export. Clearing flag during despawn was rejected because it destroys proof intent before handle release. private repair ring was rejected because blackbox rows are Vault-owned proof lane.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep repair invalid-frame cost to fixed NativeArray row plus one bool flag. Middle devices preserve lifecycle dump behavior. High/Ultra can add richer diagnostic export without changing RepairToolBlackBoxEntry layout, gameplay truth, save identity, or BufferID ownership.
Hardware Impact: Normal repair tick/hit paths are unchanged. Fault frames avoid file I/O; failed lifecycle writer attempts preserve pending flag for one more release-time retry.
Decision 112 - Scanner Success-Gated Blackbox Export
Problem: Scanner invalid-state detection was already deferred out of FastTick, but FlushPendingScannerBlackBoxDump() cleared scannerBlackBoxDumpPending before writer succeeded, and DumpScannerBlackBoxOnce() set scannerBlackBoxDumped before validating file output.
Solution: Make DumpScannerBlackBoxOnce return bool. Pending state clears only on success, scannerBlackBoxDumped is assigned only after write loop completes, and writer exceptions report through CrashTelemetryBuffer.ReportBlackBoxExportFailure() while preserving retry intent.
Rejected Alternatives: Clearing pending before writer proof was rejected because it can erase only scanner blackbox export request. Setting dumped before file output was rejected because it lies to later lifecycle flushes. Reintroducing immediate fault-frame export was rejected because scanner FastTick must stay free of disk I/O.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep invalid scanner frames to Vault row, math-guard signal, and bool flag. Middle devices preserve quit/destroy export. High/Ultra can later replace lifecycle writer with pre-owned async exporter without changing ScannerBlackBoxEntry layout, scanner authority, or BufferID route.
Hardware Impact: Normal scanner frames are unchanged. Failed quit export can now retry during destroy; frame-route cost remains one pending flag write.
Decision 113 - ToolDurability No-Create Resolver Must Not Release Vault Buffers
Problem: EnsureDurabilityView had correct createIfMissing guard around GetGenerationHandleT, but it still called ReleaseDurabilityHandle before returning false on no-create paths. Hot durability reads/writes could therefore call GlobalDataVault.ReleaseBuffer on stale handles even when they were supposed to be pure no-acquire resolves.
Solution: Move ReleaseDurabilityHandle behind createIfMissing branch. No-create calls now clear only local cached handle and fail closed. Cold create, dispose, and rebind paths still release/reacquire explicitly.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving release-before-no-create was rejected because it mutates shared Vault ownership from hot helper paths. Reacquiring missing handles from gameplay helpers was rejected by Vault law. Private NativeArrays were rejected because durability rows are cross-domain save/rollback data.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid pathological ReleaseBuffer call during already-loaded frame if handle goes stale. Middle devices keep same durability decay and breakdown events after cold bootstrap. High/Ultra can increase durability telemetry/presentation without changing BufferID ownership, DTO layout, or save identity.
Hardware Impact: Steady-state cost is unchanged. Stale-handle hot frames avoid global Vault mutation and any release-side synchronization cost.
Decision 114 - Scanner Blackbox Cold Reacquire on Stale Generation
Problem: EnsureScannerBlackBoxVault(createIfMissing:true) only called GetGenerationHandleScannerBlackBoxEntry when local handle was not created. If DataVault rebind or compaction left created but stale generation handle, cold scanner setup returned false and blackbox proof lane stayed unavailable.
Solution: Keep no-create reads fail-closed, but make create path reacquire BufferID.ShinobuScannerToolBlackBox whenever existing handle does not resolve to valid ring.
Rejected Alternatives: Letting FastTick acquire ring was rejected because blackbox rows must not allocate/grow during scanner frames. Releasing Vault ownership from scanner no-create paths was rejected because scanner does not own global lane lifetime. Leaving dead handle was rejected because it disables mandated forensic proof after rebind.
Scalability potential: Low devices still pay zero acquisition cost from scanner frames. Middle devices recover scanner forensics after cold bootstrap/rebind. High/Ultra can use same proof lane for richer diagnostics without changing ScannerBlackBoxEntry layout or BufferID authority.
Hardware Impact: Normal scanner frame cost is unchanged. Cold rebind can recover stale handle with one GetGenerationHandle call outside hot route.
Decision 115 - Equipment Update Inquisition Uses SHINOBU Sidecar
Problem: EquipmentUpdateInquisition wrote directly to Docs/Reports/CONSTRUCTIONOPTIMIZATIONREPORT.json. That file is already populated by another construction-domain report and contains sidecar references from other agents, so SHINOBU run would overwrite shared evidence.
Solution: Change editor scanner to write Docs/Reports/CONSTRUCTIONOPTIMIZATIONREPORTSHINOBU224.json and include sharedReportCompatibilityPath pointing at shared construction report. Add current sidecar report with zero forbidden update/coroutine hits across SHINOBU tool candidate set.
Rejected Alternatives: Overwriting shared report was rejected because it violates simultaneous-agent discipline. Adding Roslyn references to Hecton8.Editor.asmdef was rejected because it broadens large editor assembly and risks compile wall; scanner records honest custom parser route. Leaving no sidecar was rejected because Task 19 requires concrete proof artifact.
Scalability potential: No runtime scalability impact. validator protects low/mid/high/ultra tiers by proving active tool scalar updates route through centralized equipment solver rather than per-tool MonoBehaviour loops.
Hardware Impact: 0 microseconds runtime. Editor-only scan/report path.
Decision 116 - Repair Hull Dent Handle Borrowing Is Cold-Only
Problem: repair hit path could call EnsureHullDentsHandle, and that helper could fall through to TryGetGenerationHandle(BufferID.HullDents) when cached handle was missing or stale. That is Vault generation lookup from gameplay repair mutation.
Solution: Add allowBorrow gate. Cold CacheRepairVaultCold() borrows construction-owned hull dent handle. Hot repair mutation uses default no-borrow path and fails closed if cold caching did not establish valid handle.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving hot TryGetGenerationHandle was rejected because hull dent ownership belongs to construction/hull domain, not repair tool. Creating local dent buffers was rejected because it would shadow damage truth. Acquiring buffer from repair path was rejected by Vault law.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid generation-table lookups from repair hits. Middle devices keep hull repair when cold bootstrap finds lane. High/Ultra can enrich repair sparks/lighting while dent truth stays in owner Vault lane.
Hardware Impact: Normal resolved path is unchanged. Missed-cache hot frames avoid Vault lookup and fail closed instead of discovering ownership during gameplay.
Decision 117 - Interaction Frame Stamps Use Dispatcher Frame Identity
Problem: EquipmentInteractionHandler used Time.frameCount for packet admission limits and asynchronous raycast result aging. Tool hit coherence should follow central dispatcher frame, not Unity's frame counter.
Solution: Add ResolveSimulationFrameIndex() backed by SystemDispatcher.CurrentFrameId and use it for packet admission, completed hit lookup, and completed raycast frame stamps.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Time.frameCount was rejected because it bypasses dispatcher frame identity. Adding another timing service dependency was rejected because SystemDispatcher already exposes current frame id. Changing DTO layouts was rejected because frame identity can be corrected at call sites.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same O(1) frame stamp. Middle/High/Ultra preserve asynchronous raycast batching while aligning hit aging with central simulation cadence.
Hardware Impact: No meaningful ALU change. Removes Unity time dependency from SHINOBU interaction/raycast coherence.
Decision 118 - Thermal Grid Index Uses 64-Bit Flattening
Problem: EquipmentStateIntegrationJob.ReadThermalCell flattened int3 coordinates with 32-bit integer multiplication. If thermal-grid dimensions are corrupt or extreme, expression can overflow into false-valid small positive index and read wrong cell.
Solution: Compute flattened index as long, validate it against ThermalGridLength as unsigned 64-bit range check, and only then narrow to int for NativeArray pointer read.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting thermodynamic grid dimensions was rejected because equipment kernel must fail closed on malformed metadata. Clamping dimensions was rejected because it hides owner-side grid corruption. Absolute float sampling was rejected because it violates AUP precision rules.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay few integer ALU ops per thermal sample and avoid undefined behavior. Middle/High/Ultra retain nearest-to-trilinear quality blending through GlobalQualityWeight.
Hardware Impact: Adds negligible integer math inside thermal sampling. Prevents invalid memory read path under corrupted grid metadata.
Decision 119 - SHINOBU224 Forensic Self-Audit Artifact
Problem: latest polish loops had static evidence across status/log/rationale, but task-20 proof needed single current XML artifact with 20-task reconciliation, byte layout proof, Vault route, aliasing graph, compile guard, and Dear Lie explanation.
Solution: Add Docs/Reports/SHINOBU224SELFAUDIT.xml as static-source proof artifact and append same audit boundary into SHINOBU log stream. Keep runtime/profiler/build proof as non-claim because active CPU/build gate forbids rebuild while CPU is under load.
Rejected Alternatives: Reporting audit only in chat was rejected because AGENTS requires durable log artifacts. Reusing shared construction report was rejected because that is different proof stream. Claiming runtime proof from static scans was rejected because Unity import/profiler/player proof has not run in this pass.
Scalability potential: Low devices use same cadence collapse, nearest thermal sampling, and deferred crash export routes documented in audit. Middle/High/Ultra use same DTO/Vault identities while spending saved CPU on richer downstream VFX/audio via signals and shader scalars.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime microseconds; documentation/proof artifact only.
Decision 120 - Source Import Sweep After Subagent Compile-Wall Finding
Problem: read-only subagent correctly identified that asmdef edge was clean but several SHINOBU-owned runtime files still carried direct sibling namespace imports. Four core equipment files imported Hecton8.World only to name or reach AbsoluteUniversePosition, and additional derived-tool files carried stale Building, Construction, Physics, or World imports that resolved no symbols.
Solution: Replace avoidable AUP static calls in ModularEquipmentEngine, EquipmentInteractionHandler, and PlayerTool with existing instance methods on cached pose/origin AUP, then remove unused Hecton8.World imports from those files and ToolDurabilitySystem. Remove stale Building/Construction imports from LaserCutter, ScannerTool, and EnvironmentalAnalyzerTool; remove stale Physics imports from RepairTool, HarpoonLauncherTool, and PropulsionTool; remove stale World import from ToolHapticsRuntime.
Rejected Alternatives: Moving AbsoluteUniversePosition out of Hecton8.World was rejected because it is 48-byte cross-project ABI type embedded in Core contracts, signal payloads, save/rollback paths, and many non-SHINOBU owners. Replacing AUP payloads with raw double3 in scanner/repair/cutter/beacon signals was rejected because it would alter signal ABI and owner authority without route card. Keeping stale imports was rejected because source-level coupling proof must not rely on compiler ignoring unused imports.
Scalability potential: Low devices gain no material ALU change, but fewer sibling imports reduce compile-wall noise and make future hot-path audits cheaper. Middle/High/Ultra keep identical AUP precision and visual overkill signal routes because payload identity did not change.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime microseconds for stale import removal. practical gain is compile-surface hygiene and less false-positive audit work; AUP-bearing routes remain explicit pending separate global ABI migration.
Decision 121 - Secondary Active-Tool Import Qualification Sweep
Problem: first import sweep left MantaScooter importing Hecton8.Physics only for AupPrecisionMath, which already lives in Core contracts. scan also surfaced WfcLaserCutRuntime and LaserCutterDodRuntime, but current batch prompt identifies those DOD runtime files as SHINOBU225-owned.
Solution: Remove stale Hecton8.Physics import from MantaScooter only. Restore DOD runtime world imports and AUP factory spelling because those files belong to adjacent laser-cutter DOD agent and their DumpSHINOBU225.bin proof path is correct for that prompt.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing SHINOBU225-owned DOD files for local import tidiness was rejected after re-reading batch boundary. Migrating DebrisSpawnSignal.PositionAup away from AbsoluteUniversePosition was rejected because that signal ABI is shared and not owned by SHINOBU224. Hiding AUP construction behind local wrapper was rejected because it would obscure, not remove, ABI dependency.
Scalability potential: Low devices see no frame-time change. Middle/High/Ultra preserve identical scooter AUP velocity/headlight scalar presentation while SHINOBU224 source import surface becomes easier to audit.
Hardware Impact: 0 runtime microseconds. This is compile-wall, domain-boundary, and evidence hygiene only; no DTO layout, SignalBus payload, Vault lane, or math path changed.

Rationale_SHINOBU_225.md
SHINOBU225 Rationale
Date: 2026-05-20
Agent: SHINOBU225
Role: LASERCUTTERDODREWRITE
Status: PENDING VERIFICATION
Decision 000: Scope And Mandate Selection
Problem: Laser cutter task crosses tools, physics queries, AUP precision, VFX staging, DataVault/global authority, and telemetry. Editing without narrowing mandate set creates refactor spread.
Solution: Read and apply eight task-relevant mandates: tools/raycast/heat, ARM64 layout, zero-GC, native memory/jobs, visual fake first, AUP precision, execution phases, and signal lane segregation. Treat SHINOBU225 XML block as only batch directive.
Rejected Alternatives: Reading full mandate registry would pollute context and violate 2-8 mandate rule. Relying on memory would miss current R45 global authority boundaries.
Scalability potential: Low/MX350 gets bounded request counts and shader fakes. Middle keeps full deterministic cutter truth at normal cadence. High increases debug/telemetry density only after budget proof. Ultra spends saved CPU on richer GPU sparks/deformation, not more simulation truth.
Hardware Impact: Expected low-end gain comes from removing synchronous physics stalls and prefab burst churn. Exact i3/MX350 gain is PENDING PROFILER; static estimate range is 40-3000 us depending on old call site.
Decision 001: Product Route Relevance
Problem: laser cutter rewrite could become isolated tech work with no first-20-minutes relevance.
Solution: Scope it as removal of equipment-route blocker: cutter interaction against salvage/module surfaces must not stall Copper Wire/tool route through sync physics or prefab spawn spikes.
Rejected Alternatives: Building broad global systems unrelated to route. New global authority surfaces remain blocked unless existing source already provides lanes/buffers or work is owner-local.
Scalability potential: Same gameplay truth across devices, presentation weight scales by GlobalQualityWeight.
Hardware Impact: Prevents low-end frame hitch during repeated cutter impacts; exact microseconds PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 002: Existing Raycast Backend Boundary
Problem: batch prompt names synchronous cutter Physics.Raycast as threat, but source archaeology shows LaserCutter.TryGetCutHit already routes through IInteractionSignalService.TryRaycastPrimary, and EquipmentInteractionHandler schedules RaycastCommand.ScheduleBatch later instead of blocking cutter frame.
Solution: Keep existing equipment interaction raycast owner as live route and add SHINOBU-owned cutter DTO/jobs/tooling around it for deterministic profiling, staged hit evaluation, telemetry, and future dispatcher binding. Do not create second gameplay raycast dependency in LaserCutter.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing TryRaycastPrimary with parallel static scheduler would duplicate raycasts, double physics query load, and create race with interaction owner. Forcing direct Physics.RaycastNonAlloc would violate mandate and regress already-deferred route.
Scalability potential: Low devices continue using one deferred interaction ray per cutter frame. Middle/high/ultra can run SHINOBU mock and visual-overkill evaluation buffers for richer presentation without changing gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: Avoids adding estimated 40-120 us duplicate physics query on i3/MX350-class hardware while preserving no-blocking raycast route.
Decision 003: Sparks As Signals, Not ParticleSystem Mutation
Problem: LaserCutter.UpdateSparks still moves serialized ParticleSystem, changes emission rate, and calls Play/Stop during active cutting. Even without Instantiate, this is component-state churn in tool hot path and does not guarantee GPU-only visual staging.
Solution: Replace hot spark operation with DebrisSpawnSignal/tool spark signal path using absolute hit AUP and continuous GlobalQualityWeight intensity/count scaling. Remove cutter-adjacent ParticleSystem references in LaserCutter, SealedDoor, and SargassumCutResponder so focused cutter scans show zero particle-system code.
Rejected Alternatives: Pooling or rate-tuning existing ParticleSystem keeps CPU component writes in cutter loop. Spawning prefab spark bursts is explicitly forbidden. Keeping inert serialized fields was rejected after static scan proved they still leave cutter-focused ParticleSystem evidence.
Scalability potential: Low quality collapses spark quantity to zero GPU requests. Middle/high raises density smoothly. Ultra spends saved CPU on up to 500 GPU spark/debris requests and shader glow, not extra physical particles.
Hardware Impact: Expected low-end gain is 20-150 us during cutter impact frames by removing transform/emission/Play/Stop calls; exact profiler proof remains pending.
Decision 004: Owner-Local Buffer IDs
Problem: New cutter DOD buffers need DataVault residency, but extending global BufferID enum is cross-domain authority change that can collide with parallel agents.
Solution: Use SHINOBU owner-local buffer ID block cast to BufferID, mirroring existing scoped systems such as ballistics and procedural wreckage. Document IDs in contracts and keep them inside Tools domain.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing H8Memory.cs would enlarge global authority for tool-local feature. Allocating persistent NativeArray fields outside DataVault violates native memory mandate.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra share fixed capacities with bounded request/result buffers; only quality scalar and staged visual counts vary.
Hardware Impact: Fixed vault buffers avoid allocator churn. Expected i3/MX350 benefit is stability rather than single measurable microsecond win.
Decision 005: Shader Deformation Truth Boundary
Problem: Cutter impact wants visible molten scars and hull dents, but CPU mesh mutation or runtime mesh rebuilds are over budget for equipment hot path.
Solution: EvaluateCutterRaycastHitsJob writes LaserCutDeformationStateDTO, LaserCutGlowDecalRequestDTO, and LaserCutImpactVfxDTO only. deformation is shader/decal contract: center AUP, normal, radius, depth, heat, and progress. Geometry truth remains outside cutter.
Rejected Alternatives: Runtime vertex edits and RecalculateNormals are main-thread hazards. Mesh scar prefabs would add object lifetime churn. binary low/high visual switch was rejected; spark count, glow, and dent radius consume continuous GlobalQualityWeight.
Scalability potential: Low uses tiny dent radius and zero-to-low GPU spark quantity. Middle uses standard glow/decal density. High and Ultra increase radius/lifetime/spark density through continuous weights without changing gameplay damage truth.
Hardware Impact: Avoids estimated 300-3000 us mesh mutation spikes on i3/MX350-class devices. Actual gain remains PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 006: Editor And Report Scope
Problem: Designers need tuning and static evidence, but runtime UI or manual grep would either cost gameplay frames or fail repeatability.
Solution: Add editor-only UI Toolkit tuner, editor gizmo, and CutterRaycastInquisition static report writer. Runtime remains DataVault/signal based; editor code is isolated in Editor folders or UNITYEDITOR guards. Write SHINOBU sidecar report and add non-destructive appendix field to shared construction report.
Rejected Alternatives: In-game debug UI was rejected because it adds player-route cost. IMGUI was rejected because mandate and existing tuner pattern use UI Toolkit. Full rewrite of another agent's shared construction report was rejected; SHINOBU adds only appendix and keeps detailed report in sidecar file.
Scalability potential: No runtime cost on any tier. Top-tier devices only gain optional editor visualization density during development.
Hardware Impact: Runtime impact is zero in builds. Editor-only overhead is irrelevant to i3/MX350 gameplay budgets.
Decision 007: Request ABI Padding Correction
Problem: first implementation used offsets 52/56/60 of LaserCutRequestDTO for Frame, Flags, and RequestSequence. XML contract explicitly reserves bytes 52-63 as padding. That made ABI technically 64 bytes but semantically wrong for blind MemCpy/layout proof.
Solution: Restore LaserCutRequestDTO to exact mandated shape: double3 RayOriginAUP@0, float3 RayDirection@24, float CuttingPower@36, float MaximumDistance@40, uint ToolHashID@44, uint ParentEntityID@48, and explicit pad0/pad1/pad2 at 52/56/60. Move frame/flags/sequence/cooldown metadata into separate 64-byte LaserCutRequestMetaDTO stored in owner-local RequestMetaBuffer=71336.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping metadata inside padding was rejected because it violates exact batch ABI. Shrinking metadata to 16-byte row was rejected because 64-byte row avoids false-sharing ambiguity and keeps request/meta lanes cache-line regular under parallel writes.
Scalability potential: Low devices get predictable cache-line fetches and no unaligned metadata reads. Middle/high/ultra keep same truth buffer but can use meta lane for richer telemetry/cooldown proofs without touching request ABI.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 gain is structural, not measured frame win: fewer cache-line surprises and exact ARM64-aligned row loads. Profiler proof remains pending behind CPU/build guard.
Decision 008: Hot Resolve Only, Cold Acquire Only
Problem: Live cutter staging and scheduled raycast setup could still fall back to GlobalRegistry.DataVault or acquire Vault handles if bootstrap was missed. That is hidden hot-path authority lookup/allocation hazard.
Solution: Keep EnsureInitialized() as cold bootstrap/acquire gate. Live QueueLiveRequest, TryScheduleRaycastBatch after bootstrap, evaluation finalization, and GPU VFX staging now resolve already-acquired handles with allowAcquire:false. If Vault route is not booted, hot path fails closed instead of polling GlobalRegistry or calling GetGenerationHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Reacquiring handles opportunistically during tool fire was rejected because it hides boot failures inside gameplay. Caching private NativeArray aliases was rejected because Vault sovereignty requires generation handles plus method-local resolved views.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid metadata traffic during repeated trigger frames. Middle/high/ultra keep same route; extra visual density comes from cached quality weights, not additional authority lookups.
Hardware Impact: Expected low-end gain is removal of unpredictable metadata/registry stalls in cutter path; exact microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 009: Door VFX Decoupling
Problem: SealedDoor temporarily called LaserCutterDodRuntime.StageGpuSparkSignal, creating Gameplay - Tools source dependency for generic door spark effect.
Solution: Replace that call with local DebrisSpawnSignal publisher using door-local species hashes and continuous HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight quantity scaling. Tools owns cutter DTOs; Gameplay door owns its prop VFX signal.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping Tools call was rejected as cross-domain coupling. Reintroducing ParticleSystem sparks was rejected by Task 02.
Scalability potential: Low collapses door spark quantity toward zero; middle/high/ultra increase GPU spark/debris quantity continuously without binary quality branch.
Hardware Impact: Keeps door-cut feedback on signal/GPU path and avoids direct tool-runtime coupling. Microsecond proof pending.
Decision 010: Exact Spark Continuum And Live Tuning Consumption
Problem: Task 11 explicitly requires GPU spark presentation to scale from 0 on minimum quality to 500 on Ultra, and Editor Facade must tune actual Burst evaluation math. fixed 8..128 constant range and hardcoded dent/glow/battery values leave part of mandate decorative.
Solution: Set LowSparkCount=0, UltraSparkCount=500, feed tuning LowSparkCount, UltraSparkCount, SparkIntensityScale, DentRadiusMinMeters, DentRadiusMaxMeters, GlowLifetimeSeconds, and BatteryWattsAtPowerOne into EvaluateCutterRaycastHitsJob, and smooth presentation with math.smoothstep(GlobalQualityWeight).
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping old 128 cap was rejected because it fails XML ceiling. Applying tuning only in editor was rejected because designers would see controls that do not affect runtime job. Binary tier thresholds were rejected because HECTON requires continuous quality shedding.
Scalability potential: Low collapses spark quantity to zero and keeps shader deformation at minimal radius. Middle raises density and lifetime gradually. High/Ultra spends saved CPU on up to 500 GPU-only spark requests, larger shader dent radius, longer glow, and richer decal presentation without changing simulation truth.
Hardware Impact: Low-end silicon avoids visual request pressure under thermal clamp; Ultra routes visual overkill to GPU lanes. Exact i3/MX350 microseconds remain PENDING PROFILER.
Decision 011: Telemetry Tail Converted To Burst Work Estimate
Problem: black-box ring recorded battery watts but did not expose even deterministic proxy for Burst work intensity, leaving Task 15 weaker than forensic mandate.
Solution: Replace final telemetry tail reserve at byte 124 with BurstWorkEstimateMicros, derived inside EvaluateCutterRaycastHitsJob from hit state, quality curve, and spark count. UI Toolkit tuner now displays estimate as Burst us.
Rejected Alternatives: Measuring wall-clock time inside Burst was rejected because job has no deterministic timer and such timing would break rollback consistency. Editor-only profiler markers were rejected as sole black-box source because dumps must survive runtime fault capture.
Scalability potential: Low estimates shrink with zero spark count; Ultra estimates rise with 500-count visual pressure, giving QA stable proxy for quality-weight stress.
Hardware Impact: No extra allocation and one uint write per telemetry row. Profiler proof remains pending.
Decision 012: Preserve Job-Computed Spark Count At Signal Boundary
Problem: EvaluateCutterRaycastHitsJob computed tuned SparkCount, but PublishImpactSignals routed DTO through live staging helper, which recalculated quantity from cached quality and intensity. That silently discarded tuning SparkIntensityScale and exact 0..500 job result.
Solution: Split signal publication into PublishGpuSparkSignals. Live StageGpuSparkSignal computes direct tool presentation quantity from same no-acquire Vault tuning fields (LowSparkCount, UltraSparkCount, SparkIntensityScale) and stages impact DTO. Post-evaluation publishing now forwards LaserCutImpactVfxDTO.SparkCount directly to DebrisSpawnSignal.Quantity and disables VFX-buffer restaging.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving recalculation was rejected because it makes Burst DTO lie. Adding another DTO just for signal publication was rejected because existing impact VFX row already carries required scalar.

Decision 013: Pure Readers And Cold Scheduler Binding
Problem: continuation mandate tightened Global Systems Doctrine: TryGet, Resolve, and Read accessors must be pure. SHINOBU runtime still had public TryGetTuning, TryGetLatestTelemetry, and gizmo readers calling EnsureInitialized(), and TryGetTuning could seed default tuning as hidden write. second defect was structural: cold boot acquired only core request lanes, while simulation scheduler later used allowAcquire:false for command/result lanes that might not have been bound yet.
Solution: Public readers now only resolve already-bound handles with allowAcquire:false and return false if boot has not provided lane. Default tuning seeding moved into cold EnsureInitialized() through EnsureTuningSeeded. Cold boot now binds scheduler, hit, deformation, battery, decal, impact VFX, telemetry, request, and meta lanes before hot scheduling. foreign scalability-state handle is cached during cold boot only; hot quality refresh resolves cached handle or falls back to HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight without hot TryGetGenerationHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping hidden reader bootstrap was rejected because it violates read purity and masks missing boot order. Letting TryScheduleRaycastBatch acquire scheduler buffers opportunistically was rejected because it puts allocation/authority work back into tool route. Caching NativeArray fields was rejected because Vault generation handles remain only persistent memory identity owned by runtime.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid cold allocation spikes during cutter/gizmo/editor polling. Middle/high/ultra keep same truth route; richer presentation still comes from continuous quality and tuning rows, not new authority paths.
Hardware Impact: Estimated 5-40 us worst-case hitch avoidance on i3/MX350-class hardware by removing reader-triggered Vault acquisition and hidden boot work from tool/editor polling paths. Deferred scheduler false-negative avoidance has correctness value first; profiler proof remains pending behind external compile wall.

Caching NativeArray fields was again rejected; Vault generation handles remain persistent memory identity.

High and Ultra can spend saved CPU headroom on existing shader/decal/GPU spark continuum without increasing authority routes or DTO layout.
