Rationale_SHINOBU_230.md
SHINOBU230 Rationale
Status: IMPLEMENTED / POLISH PASS APPLIED / SUB-AGENT CONCURRENCY FINDINGS APPLIED / SCOPED BUILD BLOCKED BY EXTERNAL DELETED FILE
Decision 01 - Charger Ownership Boundary
Problem: BatteryCharger and BatteryChargerModule exposed charger-named managed cadence paths. BatteryChargerModule still registered into GlobalRegistry.RegisterSlowTickable, and BatteryCharger retained dead object-charging loop after early return.
Solution: Removed charger slow-tick registration from BatteryChargerModule, changed charger power rating to zero, reduced BatteryCharger.SlowTick() to cold compatibility no-op, and made BatteryCharger register only integer ChargerLinkDTO handles.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping managed SlowTick as "rare enough" was rejected; it keeps per-object execution surface and invalidates static scanner proof. Inventing tool-battery SOA link for BatteryChargerModule was rejected because no authoritative tool inventory slot contract exists in this domain.
Scalability potential: Low tier has no charger MonoBehaviour charge execution. Middle/high/ultra tiers spend cycles in one Burst batch and GPU-side indicators, not per-prefab scripts.
Hardware Impact: Estimated low-end i3/MX350 saving is 20-80 us per 100 active chargers by removing managed dispatch, grid dirty churn, and component-side charge loops.
Decision 02 - Inventory As Source Of Battery Truth
Problem: Charger state previously lived in BatterySlot managed objects and ItemData references. That is heap-scattered and cannot be snapshotted or charged by SIMD-friendly kernel.
Solution: Physical UI remains cold facade, but hot charge truth is InventorySlotDTO.ItemHashID, Quantity, ConditionFlags as math.asuint(float charge01), and ReservedLock. Insert/remove writes one SOA slot state; job reads only native array.
Rejected Alternatives: Battery, ListBattery, DictionarySlot,Battery, and GetComponent lookup were rejected because they create cache misses, managed iteration, and dependency on scene object lifetime.
Scalability potential: Low uses same slot schema with fewer simulation ticks. Middle/high/ultra use identical data layout with larger link counts and richer visual buffers.
Hardware Impact: Estimated saving is 10-30 us per 1,000 batteries versus managed slot traversal on weak desktop/mobile CPUs.
Decision 03 - ARM64 DTO Layout
Problem: Linkage data must bridge inventory and power graph without CS1612 copies or ARM64 misalignment.
Solution: ChargerLinkDTO is StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit, Size = 32): offset 0 InventorySlotIndex, 4 PowerGraphNodeIndex, 8 ChargeRate, 12 EfficiencyScalar, 16 Flags, offsets 20-31 explicit byte padding. Layout audit uses UnsafeUtility.SizeOf, AlignOf, and GetFieldOffset.
Rejected Alternatives: Auto-layout structs and C# properties were rejected because they obscure offsets and can force defensive copies during Burst iteration.
Scalability potential: Low-to-ultra all use one 32-byte DTO. Higher tiers increase presentation richness, not layout complexity.
Hardware Impact: 32-byte contiguous links keep two links per 64-byte cache line; expected gain is 5-15 us per 5,000 links compared with scattered object references.
Decision 04 - Emergency 5,000 Link Mock Grid
Problem: charger kernel cannot wait on live base/inventory authoring to provide dense test data.
Solution: GenerateMockChargerNetworkJob fills 5,000 ChargerLinkDTO, SOA inventory slots, power nodes, node hashes, AUPs, and visual states. Runtime fallback schedules job as IJobParallelFor with Burst and exposes generated records only after dispatcher fence reports completion.
Rejected Alternatives: Hand-authored scene prefabs and editor-only mock MonoBehaviours were rejected because they test object plumbing, not math throughput.
Scalability potential: Low can execute same mock with throttled cadence. Middle/high/ultra validate full link count and visual overkill buffers.
Hardware Impact: Mock generation is cold. Runtime proof target remains under 10 us for 1,000 links and suspicious above 100 us for 5,000 links until profiler evidence exists.
Decision 05 - Atomic Energy Transaction
Problem: Inventory slots and power graph nodes can be touched by separate systems. charge transfer must not clone or destroy energy under contention.
Solution: Job acquires InventorySlotDTO.ReservedLock using Interlocked.CompareExchange, CAS-writes ConditionFlags, CAS-deducts PowerNodeDTO.Potential, and rolls inventory charge back with Interlocked.Exchange under same slot lock if CSR CAS loses. Atomic conflict counters and fault flags are written through Interlocked operations.
Rejected Alternatives: Plain writes, lock, Monitor, NativeParallelHashMap, and bounded power-refund loops were rejected. Managed locks are illegal in Burst/hot path; hash maps are extra indirection for fixed slot-to-node links; power-refund retries are not absolute conservation proof.
Scalability potential: Low tiers reduce cadence, not correctness. Ultra tiers can add richer telemetry; transaction math remains identical.
Hardware Impact: Interlocked cost is paid only on contested writes. Expected steady-state cost is 10-40 us for 5,000 links on desktop CPUs; exact Unity profiler data still blocked by CPU guard.
Decision 06 - Continuous Cadence And Efficiency Curve
Problem: Charging every frame is unnecessary, but changing cadence must not change economy.
Solution: Scheduler maps HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight through smoothstep to 5-60 Hz and passes accumulated dt into Burst job. Transfer uses pow(max(0.0001, 1 - charge01), EfficiencyCurveExponent) for internal-resistance cheat.
Rejected Alternatives: Binary low/high switches and fixed 60 Hz simulation were rejected because they waste low-end CPU and violate continuous quality weight rules.
Scalability potential: Low 5 Hz, Middle ~24-36 Hz, High ~45-55 Hz, Ultra 60 Hz plus richer visual/audio output. Energy over time is conserved by integrated dt.
Hardware Impact: Low-end can shed up to ~91% of charger scheduling frequency while preserving time-to-full.
Decision 07 - GPU LED Dear Lie
Problem: Per-charger material or MaterialPropertyBlock writes move visual status through CPU renderer state.
Solution: Removed MaterialPropertyBlock allocation and renderer writes from BatteryCharger. Burst writes ChargerVisualStateDTO status values; VISUALSYNC double-buffers global GraphicsBuffer and exposes H8BatteryChargerStatusBuffer.
Rejected Alternatives: Changing emissive material colors from BatteryCharger was rejected because it creates CPU render work proportional to charger count.
Scalability potential: Low gets coarse LED status at no per-renderer CPU cost. Ultra can spend same buffer on richer shader animation.
Hardware Impact: Estimated saving is 15-60 us per 100 visible chargers versus individual renderer property writes.
Decision 08 - AUP Audio And Gizmo Precision
Problem: Charger hums and debug lines must not drift at far map coordinates.
Solution: Runtime stores charger and node double3 AUPs. Audio emits unmanaged AcousticPingSignal with AbsoluteUniversePosition. Gizmo converts AUP to runtime-local Vector3 only at draw time.
Rejected Alternatives: Attaching AudioSource components or storing world float3 positions was rejected due component count and 100 km precision loss.
Scalability potential: Low emits fewer signals through existing SignalBus limits. Ultra can render more x-ray/gizmo detail without changing simulation contract.
Hardware Impact: Removes AudioSource overhead; estimated saving is 10-40 us during active charger clusters plus lower scene object memory.
Decision 09 - Black Box, X-Ray, CSV, Scanner
Problem: Without forensic telemetry and static proof, charger optimization cannot be audited.
Solution: Added 300-entry ChargerTelemetryEntry ring, binary dump to Docs/AgentLogs/DumpSHINOBU230.bin, UI Toolkit X-Ray window, span-based CSV parser, live gizmo, and ChargerOOPScanner. shared report file preserves previous agent data in reports.
Rejected Alternatives: Console-only logging, string.Split, float.Parse, and overwriting shared JSON were rejected because they allocate, lose history, or damage concurrent agent output.
Scalability potential: Low keeps minimal telemetry and no per-frame UI. Ultra can inspect histograms and visual links while simulation remains flat native data.
Hardware Impact: Hot path stays zero-GC. Editor-only tools allocate in editor/cold paths only. Dump cost occurs only on 0.5 ms fault or NaN.
Verification Constraint
Problem: Compile verification is required, but current machine CPU load stayed above 50% across repeated checks (55-100% observed) and no dotnet/csc process was active. User rule forbids build when CPU load is above 50%.
Solution: Did not launch dotnet build, msbuild, or csc. Ran static grep scanner, git diff --check for tracked edits, targeted forbidden-pattern scan, and re-read changed source.
Rejected Alternatives: Building under 100% CPU load was rejected because it directly violates batch rule and would contaminate concurrent agents.
Scalability potential: Compile gate can be rerun unchanged once CPU drops below 50% and no compiler process exists.
Hardware Impact: No extra compiler load was added to already saturated workstation.
Decision 10 - Managed Facade State Eviction
Problem: charger MonoBehaviour still retained slotChargedFlags and registeredLinkIndices managed arrays. Even though they were cold allocations, they preserved object-owned charging state and required each prefab to remember native link handles.
Solution: Removed both arrays and resize helper. BatteryCharger now writes SOA inventory slot state and registers links without retaining link indices. Unregistration is native range operation keyed by inventorySlotStartIndex, slotCount, and powerGraphNodeIndex.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cold int handle cache was rejected because it makes charger object secondary owner of logistics truth. Using managed dictionary from slot to link was rejected as worse heap fragmentation and illegal hot-path temptation.
Scalability potential: Low tier pays zero per-charger heap allocations for logistics handles. Middle/high/ultra can spawn dense charger walls without multiplying object-owned state; Vault remains owner.
Hardware Impact: Low-end i3/MX350 avoids small managed array allocations per charger and removes stale handle churn during enable/disable. Runtime hot-path saving is structural rather than per-frame: charge job still consumes only Vault arrays.
Decision 11 - False Sharing Counter Lanes
Problem: first counter implementation used one 64-byte ChargerAtomicCountersDTO lane. It was correctly padded, but every worker thread still wrote same cache line via Interlocked increments, causing avoidable MESI invalidation under 5,000-link stress path.
Solution: Vault allocation for AtomicCounters is now 128 lanes, each lane exactly 64 bytes. ExecuteBatteryChargingJob receives NativeSetThreadIndex and writes plain increments into its lane; PostSimulationTick aggregates lanes after DispatcherJobFence.TryFinalizeCompleted.
Rejected Alternatives: Retaining shared Interlocked telemetry counters was rejected because telemetry does not need per-increment atomic visibility inside completed job. NativeParallelHashMap reducer was rejected because fixed worker lanes are contiguous, deterministic, and cheaper.
Scalability potential: Low tier schedules fewer cadence ticks and touches fewer lanes. Middle/high/ultra can run high link counts without telemetry cache-line fights; extra CPU budget can feed richer LED shader states.
Hardware Impact: Expected low-end gain is contention-dependent: negligible for one worker, material under multiple workers. change removes repeated shared-cache-line invalidation on Active/Full/Unpowered/Failure telemetry writes.
Decision 12 - Read Accessor Purity
Problem: TryReadCharge01, TryGetTelemetryReadOnly, and TryGetGizmoLink reached buffers through same resolver used by mutation paths. That resolver could cold-bind vault from GlobalRegistry, which violates doctrine that read-looking methods do not mutate global or owner state.
Solution: Renamed mutating vault path to BindVaultFromRegistry and confined it to bootstrap, mutation entrypoints, and dispatcher phases. generic ResolveT now uses only cached vault; public read accessors fail closed if runtime has not already bound Vault.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping resolver because it only mutated cache was rejected. Read accessors are consumed by editor windows, gizmos, and UI facades; hidden owner-state writes would make diagnostics order-dependent.
Scalability potential: Low-to-ultra behavior is unchanged. gain is authority hygiene: readers consume immutable snapshots and generation handles rather than causing bootstrap side effects.
Hardware Impact: Runtime microsecond gain is negligible; value is eliminating hidden global mutation and making read paths deterministic under heavy editor diagnostics.
Decision 13 - Deferred Emergency Mock Hydration
Problem: emergency mock job scheduled 5,000 links and immediately forced TryComplete during initialization. That is same-frame schedule/readback loop and violates dispatcher completion-window doctrine unless restricted to teardown.
Solution: Mock hydration is now scheduled and exposed only after DispatcherJobFence.TryFinalizeCompleted reports completion. While mock is pending, EnsureVaultState returns false so no consumer sees half-hydrated mock links. Forced completion remains only in Shutdown, where teardown must drain owned jobs before releasing buffers.
Rejected Alternatives: Directly executing job.Execute(i) was rejected because assignment requires Burst job. Keeping forced completion was rejected because it masks stalls and breaks phase ownership.
Scalability potential: Weak devices can finish mock hydration over dispatcher window without blocking frame. High-tier devices finish quickly and then expose same 5,000-link stress data.
Hardware Impact: Removes potential cold bootstrap stall proportional to 5,000 link writes. Exact us requires Unity profiler; static proof shows no runtime forced completion path remains.
Decision 14 - Vault Scratch CSV Reload And Explicit Gizmo AUP
Problem: Editor CSV monitor used File.ReadAllBytes, creating managed byte, and gizmo used no-offset ToRuntimePosition overload, hiding global floating-origin read per endpoint.
Solution: CSV monitor now streams into Vault-owned CsvScratch NativeArray through unsafe Spanbyte and parses that span directly. gizmo samples committed offset once and calls explicit AUP conversion overload for both charger and node endpoints.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping managed file reads because path is editor-only was rejected; Task 17 requested span parser and doctrine rejects managed staging where native scratch buffer exists. Keeping no-offset AUP conversion was rejected because diagnostics should show same explicit route being audited.
Scalability potential: Low-tier editor and CI paths avoid managed byte arrays on profile reload. Ultra/debug paths can draw more links without multiplying hidden origin reads.
Hardware Impact: CSV reload allocation drops from one managed byte array sized to file into zero managed bytes for file payload staging. Gizmo offset read drops from two hidden origin lookups per drawn link to one explicit offset sample per draw pass.
Decision 15 - Deterministic Registration Window
Problem: link buffers are intentionally requested with NativeArrayOptions.UninitializedMemory. After read-accessor and deferred mock passes, real charger could register before emergency mock job had initialized full 5,000-link window. Scanning whole Vault capacity in TryRegisterChargerLink would then read uninitialized Flags values and make registration order nondeterministic.
Solution: Registration now scans only 0..activeCount, which is initialized window already written by prior real registrations or by completed mock hydration. If no reusable inactive/mock row exists, new real link is written at initializedCount; no byte beyond initialized window is read. same registration path also advances powerNodeCount to cover registered CSR node index, preventing live pre-mock link from being clipped to one-node simulation window.
Rejected Alternatives: Clearing buffer with UnsafeUtility.MemClear was rejected because Task 14 explicitly forbids blanket clearing. Completing mock job synchronously was rejected because it violates dispatcher completion-window doctrine. Maintaining managed free list was rejected because it would reintroduce object-side ownership.
Scalability potential: Low tier can construct chargers before mock stress hydration without nondeterministic skips. Middle/high/ultra retain hole reuse inside initialized window and keep 5,000-link flat Vault layout.
Hardware Impact: Removes undefined cold registration behavior without adding hot-path work. Registration remains cold O(initialized rows), while simulation job still consumes only deterministic contiguous Vault records and required CSR node prefix.
Decision 16 - Mock Power Node Single Writer Fence
Problem: GenerateMockChargerNetworkJob used nodeIndex = index % powerNodeCount and wrote PowerNodesnodeIndex from every link index. With normal 5,000-node fallback this is one writer per node, but shorter Vault node buffer would make multiple parallel job lanes write same node row.
Solution: scheduler refuses to schedule emergency mock hydration when resolved power-node window is zero. Its pending active count is now clamped to common link-side window across Links, LinkAup, ExpectedPowerNodeHashes, VisualStates, and inventory slots. mock job also treats powerNodeCount = 0 as fail-closed no-op and writes PowerNodesnodeIndex plus PowerNodeAupnodeIndex only when index powerNodeCount. Link rows can still reference modulo node indices, but each power node row is initialized by exactly one job lane.
Rejected Alternatives: Reducing link count to power-node count was rejected because it weakens 5,000-link stress test when links and nodes intentionally have different capacities. Serializing node initialization into separate job was rejected because single-writer guard removes race without adding another dispatcher fence.
Scalability potential: Low-tier and CI fallback mocks remain robust under reduced buffer capacities. Middle/high/ultra keep full 5,000-link stress path while retaining deterministic node initialization.
Hardware Impact: Removes possible mock-hydration data race with no steady-state simulation cost. Branch cost is cold fallback only and paid once per synthetic link during mock generation.
Decision 17 - Raw Pointer Buffer Lock Coverage
Problem: ExecuteBatteryChargingJob receives raw pointers for Links, LinkAup, ExpectedPowerNodeHashes, VisualStates, inventory slots, power nodes, and counters. lock chain covered writable buffers but did not lock two read-only pointer buffers, so Vault relocation/growth could still invalidate raw pointers. same chain could leave partial lock mask until later phase if later lock failed.
Solution: TryLockJobBuffers now locks every buffer whose raw pointer enters job, including LinkAup and ExpectedPowerNodeHashes. Every lock failure immediately calls UnlockJobBuffers before returning false, so no partial lock survives failed schedule admission.
Rejected Alternatives: Assuming read-only buffers do not need locks was rejected because relocation invalidates raw pointers regardless of write intent. Leaving cleanup to PostSimulationTick was rejected because schedule admission can fail before simulationScheduled is true.
Scalability potential: Low-to-ultra behavior is unchanged. improvement is relocation safety under Vault pressure and deterministic lock ownership during concurrent agent/system operation.
Hardware Impact: Adds two cold scheduler lock calls per admitted charge job. Hot Burst math is unchanged; cost buys raw-pointer validity and removes potential deadlock/stale-lock failure mode.
Decision 18 - MonoBehaviour Charging Shadow State Removal
Problem: BatteryCharger still carried isCharging, RefreshChargingDemand, HasChargeWork, SetChargingState, and MarkPowerGridDirty. They no longer transferred energy, but they preserved second local charging-state route and dirtied legacy grid based on managed slot facade state.
Solution: Removed local charging state and demand refresh path. OnPowerStatusChanged now only caches cold power flag and refreshes disabled legacy indicators. Insert/remove still write SOA inventory state; energy flow remains exclusively in ExecuteBatteryChargingJob over inventory and CSR power node buffers.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping isCharging as harmless UI state was rejected because shader LED state already comes from ChargerVisualStateDTO, and PowerRating is zero. Dirtying legacy grid from managed slot facade would keep old object-charge architecture alive.
Scalability potential: Low tier avoids object-side demand churn. Middle/high/ultra preserve same SOA/CSR route and spend saved presentation work in global LED StructuredBuffer shader path.
Hardware Impact: Removes cold managed branch work on insert/remove/power callback and eliminates stale grid-dirty signal. Hot charge job cost is unchanged, but ownership ambiguity drops.
Decision 19 - Visual Pointer Window Clamp
Problem: ExecuteBatteryChargingJob receives raw ChargerVisualStateDTO and writes VisualStatesindex without separate visual length field. normal Vault allocator gives link-side buffers same capacity, but schedule proof must survive reduced or externally repaired buffer windows.
Solution: Registration capacity and simulation linkCount now clamp against common link-side window: Links, LinkAup, ExpectedPowerNodeHashes, and VisualStates. row can only be admitted or scheduled when every raw pointer array used at index contains that row.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding separate VisualStateCount to Burst job was rejected because hot kernel already treats LinkCount as authoritative row window; wider job contract would add another branch to every link instead of fixing scheduler invariant.
Scalability potential: Low-tier degraded Vault capacities fail closed by reducing active rows. Middle/high/ultra retain same flat 5,000-link path with no extra hot-branch cost.
Hardware Impact: Hot Burst math is unchanged. change removes possible out-of-bounds visual pointer write under buffer-window mismatch with zero steady-state CPU cost.
Decision 20 - Tool Dock Shadow-State Removal
Problem: BatteryChargerModule was still carrying isCharging, SetChargingState, and MarkGridDirty. state never performed real charging after PowerRating = 0, but it contradicted scanner report and kept legacy grid-dirty route alive in charger-owned file.
Solution: Removed isCharging, charging prompt branch, SetChargingState, MarkGridDirty, and all grid-dirty calls from docking/restore/power callbacks. module is now cold physical tool-dock facade; battery energy transfer remains in BatteryChargerLogisticsRuntime.
Rejected Alternatives: Reclassifying module as unrelated was rejected because it is charger-named owned file included in SHINOBU230 scanner scope. Keeping grid dirty as harmless was rejected because PowerRating is zero and there is no authored power demand to publish.
Scalability potential: Low tier avoids unnecessary grid invalidations from tool docking. Middle/high/ultra keep same SOA/CSR battery transaction route and can spend saved CPU in GPU-driven charger visuals.
Hardware Impact: Removes cold docking/restore grid-dirty churn and eliminates false report condition. Hot Burst charge cost is unchanged.
Decision 21 - Scanner Shadow-State Coverage
Problem: ChargerOOPScanner counted Update/coroutine/list/slow-tick patterns, but did not count exact class of miss found by sub-agent: local charger isCharging state and legacy grid-dirty methods.
Solution: Expanded scanner to count isCharging, SetChargingState, RefreshChargingDemand, HasChargeWork, MarkPowerGridDirty, MarkGridDirty, and Grid.MarkDirty within charger-named files. These counters now contribute to forbiddenPatternHits and generated verdict.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping scanner scope narrow was rejected because scanner report includes BatteryChargerModule.cs and must fail on charger-owned shadow-state, not only on explicit Update() loops.
Scalability potential: Low-to-ultra runtime is unaffected. gain is CI/editor regression detection for ownership drift before it reaches playmode.
Hardware Impact: Editor-only scan cost increases by few token-count passes per charger file. Runtime cost is 0 us.
Decision 22 - Inventory Slot Contract Extraction
Problem: BatteryChargerLogisticsRuntime and BatteryChargerLogisticsContracts compile under root Hecton8.Core asmdef, while InventorySlotDTO was defined inside sibling Hecton8.Inventory.Routing.Runtime. Referencing that sibling from Core would create circular asmdef dependency because Inventory Routing already references Core.
Solution: Moved shared InventorySlotDTO ABI into Hecton8.Core.Contracts at Assets/Project/Scripts/Core/Contracts/InventorySlotDTO.cs, preserving namespace Hecton8.Inventory, explicit 32-byte layout, and offsets 0/4/8/16/20. Removed duplicate definition from InventoryRoutingNetwork.cs. Charger logistics consumes only contract DTO and no longer calls InventoryRoutingNetwork.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding Hecton8.Inventory.Routing.Runtime to Hecton8.Core.asmdef was rejected as compile-wall/circular-dependency breach. Duplicating InventorySlotDTO in Power was rejected because it would split rollback/save identity and allow ABI drift.
Scalability potential: Low-to-ultra behavior is unchanged; gain is assembly isolation. Power can operate on SOA slot ABI while Inventory Routing keeps ownership of higher-level query/transaction implementation.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost is 0 us. impact is production velocity and correctness: charge kernel can compile without sibling runtime reference and without changing slot memory layout.
Decision 23 - Cold Slot Atomic Facade And Raw Dump
Problem: cold TryWriteInventorySlotState facade wrote InventorySlotDTO fields directly and reset ReservedLock, which could race with scheduled charge kernel. telemetry dump also serialized each field through BinaryWriter, while assignment requested raw ReadOnlySpanbyte dump.
Solution: TryWriteInventorySlotState now locks BufferID.ShinobuInventorySlots, acquires ReservedLock via Interlocked.CompareExchange, writes item hash, quantity, and charge bits, then releases both slot and Vault locks. WriteDump writes fixed little-endian header and then streams raw telemetry ring as ReadOnlySpanbyte over native array.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping direct cold writes was rejected because insert/remove can coincide with dispatcher phases. Keeping BinaryWriter was rejected because it is managed per-field serializer and not requested raw black-box payload.
Scalability potential: Low devices fail closed when slot buffer is locked instead of stalling. Middle/high/ultra keep same hot kernel; crash dumps stay compact and ABI-faithful.
Hardware Impact: Cold insert/remove adds buffer lock plus one uncontended CAS. Hot charge job is unchanged. Fault dump path avoids per-entry/per-field writer dispatch and writes contiguous telemetry bytes.
Decision 24 - Scoped Build Gate External Block
Problem: CPU and compiler-process gates opened, so scoped compile was required. dotnet build Hecton8.Core.csproj --no-restore -v:minimal stopped before SHINOBU230 files at CS2001 because Assets/Project/Scripts/Gameplay/HectonScannerProjectionState.cs is still included by generated project but is deleted in worktree.
Solution: Classified failure as external compile-wall/stale-project block. Verified file is absent, git status --short reports it as deleted, and Hecton8.Core.csproj still references it. Did not restore, recreate, or remove reference because that file is outside battery charger logistics domain and project file is Unity-generated.
Rejected Alternatives: Reverting deleted gameplay file was rejected because it is unrelated work by another agent or user. Editing Hecton8.Core.csproj was rejected because it is generated and would hide real project-state problem.
Scalability potential: Low-to-ultra runtime behavior is unchanged. This decision preserves concurrent-agent boundaries and keeps compile evidence honest instead of forcing local-only build artifact.
Hardware Impact: No runtime effect. Build load was limited to one scoped project attempt after CPU gate opened; no full rebuild was launched.
Decision 25 - ABI Placement Recheck
Problem: Post-build static verification found new InventorySlotDTO file under Assets/Project/Scripts/Inventory/InventorySlotDTO.cs, while rationale and compile-wall fix require ABI to live under Core/Contracts so Hecton8.Core consumes only Hecton8.Core.Contracts.
Solution: Moved DTO and its GUID-preserving .meta to Assets/Project/Scripts/Core/Contracts/InventorySlotDTO.cs. Re-ran definition scan and confirmed exactly one public struct InventorySlotDTO under Assets/Project/Scripts, at contract path.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving file in Inventory/ was rejected because path ownership would contradict compile-wall contract even if namespace resolution worked. Duplicating DTO was rejected because it would split rollback/save ABI identity.
Scalability potential: Low-to-ultra runtime behavior is unchanged. value is assembly ownership: SOA slot layout is now shared ABI, while Inventory Routing remains implementation consumer.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost is 0 us. Compile-wall risk is reduced by keeping shared DTO in contracts layer.
Decision 26 - Post-Resume ABI Filesystem Drift Recheck
Problem: On 2026-05-21 resume pass, disk verification again found InventorySlotDTO staged under Assets/Project/Scripts/Inventory/InventorySlotDTO.cs, while active compile-wall contract requires ABI under Assets/Project/Scripts/Core/Contracts/InventorySlotDTO.cs.
Solution: Re-applied move with same GUID-preserving .meta, then verified only public struct InventorySlotDTO under Assets/Project/Scripts is at Core.Contracts path and that Inventory-root staging path is absent.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting previous log was rejected because disk state is authority. Keeping DTO under Inventory was rejected because it would make Hecton8.Core consume sibling implementation folder instead of contracts-layer ABI.
Scalability potential: Low-to-ultra runtime behavior remains unchanged; value is compile-wall isolation and stable ABI ownership.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost is 0 us. This prevents assembly-boundary drift, not frame-time work.
Decision 27 - Binary Payload Ledger Row
Problem: BINARYPAYLOADINTEGRATIONLEDGER.md documented SHINOBU141's inventory routing payload lane, but did not record SHINOBU230's cross-domain use of shared slot ABI or static proof caveat for battery charger transaction.
Solution: Added SHINOBU230 static boundary row documenting InventorySlotDTO in Core.Contracts, BufferID.ShinobuInventorySlots as charge-bit route, charger DTO sizes, shader-buffer LED presentation route, and unrelated HectonScannerProjectionState.cs compile blocker.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving ledger unchanged was rejected because current architecture depends on shared ABI moved out of Inventory Routing implementation scope. Claiming runtime proof was rejected because Unity import/Burst/Play Mode/profiler evidence is still absent.
Scalability potential: Low-to-ultra behavior is unchanged; ledger update keeps future agents from reintroducing sibling runtime coupling or duplicate DTO.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost is 0 us. value is documentation authority and compile-wall preservation.
Decision 28 - Sibling World Import Prune

Decision 33 - Vault Lock Coverage For Link Mutation And Mock Hydration

Decision 34 - Conservation Transaction Order And Active Hum AUP
Problem: previous transaction debited CSR power potential first, then attempted inventory ConditionFlags CAS, then used bounded best-effort refund if that CAS failed. That is not hard conservation proof. short-lived report draft also overstated replacement as unconditional Interlocked.Exchange primary write. Hum routing also emitted from linkAups0 regardless of which charger drew energy.
Solution: Kept slot ReservedLock as inventory ownership fence. locked inventory ConditionFlags CAS now lands before CSR power-node CAS. If power CAS loses, inventory charge is rolled back with Interlocked.Exchange while same slot lock is still held. There is no power refund loop and no post-debit inventory CAS path. Added LastActiveLink at offset 32 in ChargerAtomicCountersDTO; lanes record link that actually drew energy, aggregation preserves it, and hum signal AUP reads that link.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping bounded AddPotential rollback loop was rejected because bounded retries can still destroy energy under contention. Treating Exchange as primary inventory write was rejected because it would silently overwrite changed charge word; CAS is proof, Exchange is only locked rollback after failed CSR CAS. Computing active centroid was rejected for now because it needs extra summed AUP state; last active link is deterministic and stays within 64-byte counter line.
Scalability potential: Low tier keeps identical gameplay truth with fewer cadence ticks. Middle/high/ultra can add richer hum or shader presentation later without changing SOA/CSR transaction route.
Hardware Impact: Successful transfer keeps one inventory CAS and one CSR CAS, but removes bounded power-refund helper and its retry path. LastActiveLink reuses padding inside existing 64-byte counter DTO, so false-sharing protection remains intact.

Charger-to-tool swap reinserts battery into charger if tool insert fails.

Decision 51 - Visual Buffer Prewarm And Cold Facade Allocation Annotation
Problem: LED Dear Lie path correctly used double-buffered GraphicsBuffer upload and dirty hashes, but buffer pair was still first-created from VisualSyncTick. That puts first-use GPU allocation on presentation phase, exactly where shader/driver stutter is most visible. separate static scan also showed cold managed BatterySlot fallback allocations without canonical COLD ALLOC comments, leaving future auditors false trail even though those objects are facade/editor metadata rather than charge truth.
Solution: PreSimulationTick now calls EnsureGraphicsBuffers() after Vault/default readiness and tuning application, before VISUALSYNC can upload LED state. VisualSyncTick keeps same guard as safety fallback, but normal runtime gets double buffer prewarmed earlier in dispatcher frame. ChargerOOPScanner emits visualBuffersPrewarmedBeforeVisualSync, and shared equipment report records it as true. BatteryCharger now annotates serialized BatterySlot2, legacy fallback array, and per-slot facade object allocations with canonical COLD ALLOC comments.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping lazy first allocation in VISUALSYNC was rejected because it risks visible first-active frame hitch for no gameplay benefit. Deleting BatterySlot facade metadata was rejected because it would break prefab/editor migration and does not affect SOA/Vault charge truth. Moving graphics buffer allocation into static constructor was rejected because Unity graphics resources need runtime lifecycle control and explicit release.
Scalability potential: Low devices avoid first-use visual allocation spike and keep coarse GPU LED state. Middle/high/ultra keep same StructuredBuffer route and can spend saved CPU on richer shader interpretation of visual state; GlobalQualityWeight still scales cadence/presentation only and does not change DTO layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Hot Burst charge kernel remains 0 us changed. First-active LED presentation loses one avoidable GPU allocation on visual phase; buffer cost remains bounded at two structured buffers of DefaultLinkCapacity sizeof(ChargerVisualStateDTO).
Decision 52 - CSV Tuning Parser Fail-Closed Polish
Problem: charger profile CSV parser used allocation-free span parser, but numeric parser accepted partial values because it returned after consuming prefix digits and did not require end-of-field. malformed field like 0.5junk could therefore hydrate as 0.5, and accidental extra column could be ignored. That violates human-readable tuning bridge rule: bad authored data must fail closed, not become silent simulation tuning.
Solution: Replaced ParseFloat with TryParseFiniteFloat. It trims span, requires at least one digit, rejects non-finite intermediate accumulation, rejects trailing characters by requiring index == value.Length, and returns boolean so TryParseLine can reject malformed rows. TryParseLine now also rejects extra columns by checking Trim(line).Length != 0 after expected four numeric fields. ChargerOOPScanner and shared equipment report now expose csvParserRejectsMalformedRows=true.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping permissive partial parsing was rejected because it turns authoring typos into valid tuning. Using float.Parse, string.Split, or managed dictionaries was rejected because Task 17 mandates ReadOnlySpanbyte and zero-GC cold ingestion. Throwing exceptions on malformed rows was rejected because editor/runtime hot reload should skip bad rows deterministically and preserve last valid tuning state.
Scalability potential: Low-tier devices keep same cheap charger cadence and avoid corrupted rate/exponent values that could create spikes. Middle/high/ultra keep designer-authored overkill charge profiles, but only when rows are syntactically valid. GlobalQualityWeight cadence remains continuous and independent of CSV validity.
Hardware Impact: Hot Burst charge kernel cost remains 0 us. Cold/editor CSV ingestion adds few byte comparisons per numeric field and prevents malformed tuning from amplifying grid drain or visual LED cadence.
Decision 53 - Emergency Mock Fallback Authority Fence
Problem: emergency mock charger generator satisfied CI fallback requirement, but it could also hydrate 5,000 mock charger links in normal player runtime if no live links existed when dispatcher first touched domain. Once usingMockInventorySlots became true, TryRegisterChargerLink refused live registration, making mock data sticky and capable of blocking streamed or late-built real chargers.
Solution: Added AllowEmergencyMockNetwork() so mock hydration is confined to UNITYEDITOR | | DEVELOPMENTBUILD. Non-development runtime still creates Vault buffers and tuning state, but does not fabricate charger truth. TryRegisterChargerLink now validates that live Inventory-owned ShinobuInventorySlots buffer exists for authored slot first; if mock network is active, it calls DropMockNetworkForLiveRegistration() to reset mock active counts and allow live link to overwrite window. Scanner/report proof fields now expose emergencyMockEditorOrDevelopmentOnly=true and liveRegistrationDropsMockFallback=true.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping always-on mock hydration was rejected because fallback benchmark must not become runtime authority. Removing mock generator was rejected because Task 05 requires isolated 5,000-link stress data for CI/dev. Clearing or owning shared Inventory slot buffer was rejected because Inventory owns live slot truth; this domain only drops its own mock window.
Scalability potential: Low-tier release builds avoid unnecessary 5,000-link synthetic job when no chargers exist. Editor/development builds still get full 5,000-link pressure test. Middle/high/ultra behavior with live chargers is unchanged: continuous GlobalQualityWeight controls cadence, not authority ownership.
Hardware Impact: Hot Burst charge kernel remains 0 us changed. Release/no-charger boot avoids scheduling one 5,000-link GenerateMockChargerNetworkJob; live registration pays cold scalar reset if it replaces dev mock fallback.
Decision 54 - Binary Payload Ledger Registration
Problem: BatteryChargerLogisticsBufferIds owns local 72300..72310 Vault ID range, but Docs/ARCHITECTURE/BINARYPAYLOADINTEGRATIONLEDGER.md did not register that range or provide SHINOBU230 payload route card. ledger explicitly rejects local numeric (BufferID)N casts without registered range, so source-only proof was incomplete.
Solution: Added 72300..72310 to active BufferID range table and inserted SHINOBU230 payload boundary entry. entry records each buffer ID, Power owner, primary DTO layout anchors, authority route, endian status, rollback/save boundary, and Docs/AgentLogs/DumpSHINOBU230.bin fault route. Reconciled equipment report query against current reports: ... schema and reran targeted source/report guards.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing H8Memory.BufferID enum entries was rejected for this loop because mandate was to register and document existing range without broad core churn; no runtime callsite requires enum-name syntax to resolve Vault handles. Leaving ledger silent was rejected because it violates binary payload integration doctrine. Treating initial root-array JSON query as real missing report row was rejected after schema inspection proved row exists under reports.
Scalability potential: Low-tier devices get no additional runtime work. Middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged: continuous cadence and LED StructuredBuffer presentation remain scaling path. ledger improvement prevents future agents from colliding with or reallocating charger range.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost is 0 us. Documentation/proof cost only. practical gain is preventing BufferID ownership ambiguity that could corrupt Vault payload routing or create compile-wall churn later.
Decision 55 - Scanner-Enforced Ledger Proof
Problem: Loop 38 registered 72300..72310 in binary payload ledger, but scanner/report contract did not verify that registration. That made proof dependent on prose in LOGSHINOBU230.md instead of Task 19 machine-readable equipment report. future edit could remove ledger entry while ChargerOOPScanner still returned PASS.
Solution: Added binaryPayloadLedgerRangeRegistered and binaryPayloadLedgerBoundaryRegistered to ChargerOOPScanner. scanner reads Docs/ARCHITECTURE/BINARYPAYLOADINTEGRATIONLEDGER.md, checks 72300..72310 range, SHINOBU230 boundary heading, 72310 mock inventory slot route, and DumpSHINOBU230.bin, then includes those booleans in verdict. shared equipment report was updated to same schema.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving ledger proof in log text was rejected because Task 19 requires static proof output to EQUIPMENTOPTIMIZATIONREPORT.json. Adding separate Python checker was rejected because this is editor-only scanner-owned proof and no new toolchain dependency is needed. Running Unity or dotnet was rejected because CPU/build gate remains blocked.
Scalability potential: Runtime behavior is unchanged across low/middle/high/ultra tiers. hardening protects Vault range from future collision and keeps charger graph/scalability math tied to documented payload route.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost is 0 us. Editor scanner pays one File.ReadAllText on ledger and handful of ordinal string checks. This is acceptable because scanner is cold proof tool, not gameplay.
Decision 56 - Runtime Assembly Isolation Bridge
Problem: charger logistics runtime and contracts were still under root Hecton8.Core asmdef. Creating naive Power runtime asmdef would have forced Hecton8.Core to reference Power runtime because BatteryCharger.cs directly called BatteryChargerLogisticsRuntime. That is compile-wall failure mode mandate forbids.
Solution: Moved charger logistics runtime/contracts/gizmo into Assets/Project/Scripts/Power/BatteryChargerLogistics/ and added Hecton8.Power.BatteryChargerLogistics.Runtime.asmdef. Added Hecton8.Core.BatteryChargerLogisticsBridge, cold delegate table owned by Core, so Gameplay facade depends only on Core. Power runtime registers its methods into bridge at boot and clears them during reset/shutdown. Added editor asmdef for X-Ray/scanner tools and scanner/report fields that gate on asmdef presence, no sibling runtime refs, no direct facade runtime calls, and runtime bridge registration. remaining using Hecton8.Inventory resolves Core-contract InventorySlotDTO ABI marker; there is no asmdef reference to Hecton8.Inventory.Routing.Runtime.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding Hecton8.Power.BatteryChargerLogistics.Runtime to Hecton8.Core.asmdef was rejected because it creates direct Core-to-domain compile wall. Moving entire Power/ folder under new asmdef was rejected because unrelated Power files would be swept into this lane. Expanding GlobalRegistry with new service slot was rejected because it touches massive core registry header for cold facade bridge. Reflection or scene lookup was rejected because read/register accessors must stay pure and allocation-free.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra runtime math is unchanged. split protects iteration time and keeps saved CPU budget available for existing continuous GlobalQualityWeight cadence and shader-buffer LED Dear Lie. No gameplay truth owner, DTO layout, save identity, or authority route changed.
Hardware Impact: Hot Burst charge kernel cost remains 0 us changed. Cold facade calls now go through static delegate bridge; that is outside scheduled charge kernel and only affects interaction/registration/readback paths. real gain is compile-wall isolation and avoiding future whole-Core rebuild cascade for Power-only logistics edits.
Decision 57 - Locked Simulation Tick Authority
Problem: BatteryChargerLogisticsRuntime.ScheduleSimulation accumulated timing.FrameDelta before deciding whether to schedule deterministic charge transaction kernel. That made charge authority dependent on render-frame pacing when dispatcher did not provide fixed lane value, violating rollback rule that critical state changes must be driven by locked simulation tick rather than variable frame time.
Solution: Added SimulationTickDeltaSeconds = 1f / 60f and ResolveSimulationTickDelta(in DispatcherTimingDTO timing). resolver uses finite positive timing.FixedDelta when dispatcher supplies fixed-step bridge, clamped to 1/240..1/5, and otherwise returns locked 60 Hz domain constant. ScheduleSimulation now accumulates that resolved tick value; Burst job still receives single scalar DeltaSeconds, so DTO layout and hot pointer kernel shape do not change. ChargerOOPScanner now proves lockedSimulationTickDeltaUsed=true and frameDeltaBypassedForChargeAuthority=true, and gates shared report verdict on both fields.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping FrameDelta was rejected because it lets render stalls alter authority-side charge transfer and rollback snapshots. Adding new field to DispatcherTimingDTO was rejected as core contract churn outside SHINOBU230 scope and unnecessary because FixedDelta already exists. Moving charger scheduling to fixed dispatcher interface was rejected for this loop because it would expand assembly split blast radius; local resolver gives deterministic authority without changing global dispatcher contracts.
Scalability potential: Low-tier devices now shed charge-kernel frequency through existing continuous GlobalQualityWeight cadence without changing total authority time based on render stalls. Middle/high/ultra tiers still resolve cadence through math.smoothstep and math.lerp(5f, 60f, q), reaching per-frame 60 Hz charge transactions at quality 1.0 while preserving same DTO/save identity and shader-buffer LED Dear Lie.
Hardware Impact: Hot kernel cost is unchanged: one scalar DeltaSeconds is written into job exactly as before. scheduler replaces variable frame-time read with deterministic finite resolver, estimated below 0.01 us per dispatcher tick. practical gain is deterministic rollback behavior and removal of frame-pacing drift from power-grid energy conservation.
Decision 58 - GlobalRegistry Service Bridge Hardening
Problem: Loop 40 isolated Power runtime assembly, but Core facade bridge still used managed delegate table. That protected compile wall but did not match stricter cross-domain route rule, which allows GlobalRegistry service locator, unmanaged function pointers, or typed SignalBus payloads. Unmanaged function pointers are poor fit for these facade methods because target bodies cross managed Unity/runtime boundaries: IDataVault, GlobalRegistry, GraphicsBuffer lifecycle state, and cold authored inventory checks. SignalBus is also wrong for TryRegister/TryRead because facade needs synchronous commit/fail-closed answers before removing or rolling back inventory.
Solution: Replaced delegate table with IBatteryChargerLogisticsService, published by BatteryChargerLogisticsRuntime through GlobalRegistry.RegisterBatteryChargerLogisticsRuntime(this). GlobalRegistry was opened as partial and new service route lives in GlobalRegistry.BatteryChargerLogistics.cs, keeping edit local instead of inserting into huge registry body. BatteryChargerLogisticsBridge now caches registry-published service via BindService and never polls GlobalRegistry from facade reads. runtime implements interface explicitly and unregisters during reset/shutdown. Scanner/report proof now gates on runtimeRegistersGlobalRegistryService, bridgeDelegateTableEradicated, bridgeUsesCachedRegistryService, and globalRegistryBatteryServiceRoute.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping managed delegate bridge was rejected because it is not one of allowed cross-domain routes. Adding unmanaged UnmanagedCallersOnly/function-pointer table was rejected because methods are not pure Burst-compatible math kernels and would cross managed Vault/Unity lifecycle APIs; this would be compile-risk without performance gain. Adding full dense GlobalRegistryServiceSlot enum entry was rejected for this pass because it touches central registry atlas and multiple service-slot proof maps; partial route gives cold service identity without broad core churn. SignalBus was rejected because these facade calls require synchronous return values.
Scalability potential: Low tier keeps same continuous 5..60Hz cadence shedding and no per-frame registry polling. Middle/high/ultra keep same GPU StructuredBuffer LED Dear Lie and hum signal route. Gameplay truth ownership, DTO layout, save identity, and authority route remain unchanged; only cold cross-assembly publication path changed.
Hardware Impact: Hot Burst charge kernel cost remains 0 us changed. Cold facade interactions replace delegate invocation with one cached interface dispatch. Boot/shutdown pay one registry publish/unpublish. measurable gain is architectural: no direct sibling runtime reference and no ad-hoc delegate table left between Core facade and Power runtime.
Decision 59 - Inventory Reservation Fence For Charger Insert
Problem: cold BatteryCharger.InsertBatteryFromInventory facade removed one item from PlayerInventory before charger bridge accepted target slot. old path attempted rollback with TryAddItem, but that was not hard owner-local reservation proof: failed charger commit could depend on later managed reinsert capacity instead of preserving Inventory ownership until Power-owned charger link accepted handoff.
Solution: Replaced remove-first sequence with existing Inventory-owner PlayerInventory.CraftReservation fence. BatteryCharger now reserves one matching battery hash into preallocated PlayerInventory.CraftReservation1 scratch buffer, calls InsertBattery only after reservation success, releases reservation if charger commit fails, and commits inventory reservation only after charger accepted item. If inventory commit then fails, charger slot is removed and development-build rollback fault is emitted. ChargerOOPScanner now proves playerInventoryBridgeHardReservationProof=true, playerInventoryBridgeRemovesBeforeChargerCommit=false, and reservation/commit/release sequence in shared equipment report.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping remove-first path was rejected because rollback is weaker than owner-local reservation. Adding new Inventory API was rejected as cross-domain churn; existing craft-reservation contract already provides bounded owner-local lock. Allocating reservation array during interaction was rejected; facade owns one cold, annotated scratch slot instead.
Scalability potential: Low-tier runtime cost is unchanged in Burst charge kernel and remains 0 us hot-path. Middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged: continuous GlobalQualityWeight controls charge cadence, and LED Dear Lie remains GPU-buffer driven. change strengthens cold human interaction seam without changing DTO layout, save identity, or power authority route.
Hardware Impact: Hot kernel cost remains 0 us changed. Cold interaction adds one reservation check and one reservation commit on successful inventory-to-charger transfer. gain is conservation proof at managed facade boundary: Inventory remains source owner until charger bridge accepts slot, removing prior rollback-capacity dependency.
Decision 60 - Dead Rollback Helper Eradication
Problem: Loop 43 replaced remove-first inventory insertion with Inventory-owned reservation fence, but BatteryCharger.cs still contained unused TryReturnItemToInventory helper. Even without callsites, that dead helper preserved old rollback-capacity route in source and could mislead future maintenance or scanner authors into restoring weaker pattern.
Solution: Deleted TryReturnItemToInventory from managed facade. Re-ran targeted source scan against BatteryCharger.cs; there are now zero hits for TryReturnItemToInventory, playerInventory.RemoveOneItem(, or direct grid RemoveItemAt( in charger facade. shared equipment report row already proves replacement route: reserve before charger commit, release on charger failure, and commit only after charger acceptance.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving dead helper was rejected because source-level fossils invite regression. Broadening scanner rules to ignore helper was rejected because code should be simpler than exception. Editing PlayerInventory was rejected because its existing craft-reservation API already provides required owner-local fence.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra behavior is unchanged. This is cold facade cleanup; Burst charge graph, continuous GlobalQualityWeight cadence, GPU LED Dear Lie, telemetry ring, and Vault DTO layout are untouched.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost remains 0 us changed. practical gain is reduced maintenance risk at Inventory-to-Power handoff and one fewer managed method for future compile/import churn.
Decision 61 - Registry-Owned Bridge Reset
Problem: GlobalRegistry service route removed managed delegate table, but BatteryChargerLogisticsBridge.Clear() was still public unconditional clear. Normal shutdown called it after matched registry unregister. In reload/teardown interleaving, old runtime instance could clear newer service binding after CompareExchange correctly refused to unregister it.
Solution: Deleted public bridge clear method. Added GlobalRegistry.ResetBatteryChargerLogisticsRuntimeForDomainReload() for SubsystemRegistration window, using Interlocked.Exchange to clear registry slot and then cached bridge. Normal runtime shutdown now calls only GlobalRegistry.UnregisterBatteryChargerLogisticsRuntime(this), which clears bridge only when previous slot matches shutting-down instance. Updated scanner/report and binary payload ledger to prove direct clear route is gone.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping unconditional BatteryChargerLogisticsBridge.Clear() was rejected because it can violate owner-local service identity. Making bridge clear compare against expected service was rejected because Power runtime should not directly own Core bridge mutation; registry is owner of route. Leaving this as rationale-only convention was rejected because scanner/report proof already gates compile-wall route.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra charge math is unchanged. change affects only cold boot/shutdown service identity; continuous cadence, Vault handles, DTO layout, shader LED Dear Lie, and telemetry ring remain identical.
Hardware Impact: Hot path cost remains 0 us changed. Boot/domain-reset pays one Interlocked.Exchange; shutdown pays existing CompareExchange. gain is preventing stale runtime teardown from clearing live registry-published service.
Decision 62 - Cadence Cap Remainder Preservation
Problem: ScheduleSimulation correctly used locked simulation tick delta and continuous GlobalQualityWeight cadence, but safety cap integrationDt = min(accumulator, 1s) then zeroed authorityAccumulator. long hitch over one second would therefore discard elapsed authority time and violate requirement that cadence shedding must preserve mathematical time-to-full.
Solution: Keep one-second per-job cap, but subtract only executed slice: authorityAccumulator = max(0, authorityAccumulator - integrationDt). This bounds worst-case per-job transfer after hitch while carrying remaining elapsed authority time into later dispatcher frames. Added scanner/report proof field cadenceCapPreservesAccumulatorRemainder=true.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing cap was rejected because multi-second hitch could create single large transfer spike and fault cascade. Keeping zeroing was rejected because it loses gameplay-economy time. Running catch-up jobs in same-frame loop was rejected because it would violate dispatcher-owned completion windows and risk frame spikes.
Scalability potential: Low-tier devices can run at 5Hz end of continuous cadence without losing charge time during stalls. Middle/high/ultra still approach 60Hz through smoothstep/lerp. cap affects per-job chunk size only; it does not change truth ownership, DTO layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: Hot scheduling cost adds one scalar subtraction and math.max when job is actually scheduled. Estimated below 0.01 us per scheduled charge pass. gain is deterministic economic conservation under long frame stalls without same-frame catch-up loops.
Decision 63 - Coalesced Skipped-Cadence Telemetry
Problem: Low-quality cadence shedding previously called RecordSkippedCadenceFrame on every scheduler frame below execution period and wrote full ChargerTelemetryEntry row each time. At 5 Hz charge cadence under 60 Hz dispatcher, that could replace roughly 55 of 60 black-box rows per second with skip-only records, reducing forensic density for actual charge transactions, atomic failures, NaN flags, and power draw.
Solution: Converted skipped cadence recording to in-runtime scalar counter. RecordSkippedCadenceFrame now increments skippedCadenceFrames and does not write telemetry ring. next executed WriteTelemetryFrame ORs TelemetryFlagSkippedCadence, writes coalesced count into ChargerTelemetryEntry.SkippedCadenceFrames at offset 60, then clears counter after row is emitted. ChargerTelemetryEntry stays exactly 64 bytes; offset-60 tail lane was renamed from anonymous Reserved0 to meaningful counter and layout audit now checks that field.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping one row per skipped frame was rejected because black-box history should prioritize executed charge state and faults. Adding second skip-only Vault ring was rejected as unnecessary memory and ownership surface. Dropping skipped-cadence telemetry entirely was rejected because cadence shedding still needs forensic proof. Reusing DeltaSeconds for skip count was rejected because it would corrupt integration-time semantics.
Scalability potential: Low-tier devices still reduce charge work continuously through GlobalQualityWeight cadence, but 300-frame ring now preserves real charge rows while carrying skipped-frame count. Middle/high/ultra paths are unchanged because fewer frames are skipped as cadence approaches 60 Hz. DTO size, BufferID identity, save identity, and authority route remain unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Each skipped scheduler frame now pays one saturated scalar increment instead of one 64-byte NativeArray write plus cursor update. Exact runtime microseconds remain pending Unity profiler proof; static cost reduction is small per frame but materially improves forensic signal quality under thermal throttling.
Decision 64 - Editor Tuning DTO Coherence
Problem: editor/runtime tuning bridge wrote QualityOverride and flags before recomputing GlobalQualityWeight and CadenceHz, but recompute path read old tuning row. designer changing quality override could therefore leave Vault tuning row internally stale for one scheduler pass: override fields said one thing, cadence fields still reflected previous row.
Solution: Added one cold helper, ApplyPendingTuningValues(ref ChargerTuningDTO dto), used by direct editor tuning, pre-simulation tuning, and default tuning. helper writes max charge rate, exponent, override, flags, resolved continuous GlobalQualityWeight, battery capacity, and CadenceHz in one DTO update. resolved quality comes from ResolvePendingQualityWeight(), which consumes pending override immediately when it is finite and non-negative, otherwise falls back to HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving one-frame stale row was rejected because Task 16 requires real-time editor control without recompilation. Recomputing cadence in X-Ray UI only was rejected because Vault row is authority consumed by scheduler. Adding second editor-only mirror field was rejected because it would create shadow tuning state.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra tuning now changes actual continuous cadence immediately through same helper. This does not introduce binary hardware switches and does not change DTO layout, save identity, BufferID identity, or charge authority route. First-20 route impact: habitat power feedback becomes tunable in Play Mode without stale cadence proof.
Hardware Impact: Hot Burst kernel cost remains 0 us changed. Cold tuning writes now perform one direct quality resolver and one cadence calculation when editor or pre-simulation owner updates single tuning DTO. practical gain is removing one-pass mismatch between visible designer controls and scheduler cadence.
Decision 65 - Generation-Handle Slot Fence Proof
Problem: runtime had already moved cold inventory slot writes to VaultGenerationHandleInventorySlotDTO plus TryAcquireWriteLock, but ChargerOOPScanner still proved coldSlotWriteLocksBeforeResolve by searching for removed legacy TryLockBuffer(BufferID.ShinobuInventorySlots) and direct TryGetBuffer(...) route. That created false evidence surface: rerunning scanner would not be proving current descriptor write fence, while JSON report still carried stale true value.
Solution: Added coldSlotWriteUsesGenerationHandleFence to scanner and report. scanner now requires exact TryAcquireInventorySlotsWrite(...) callsite, descriptor borrow through TryBorrowInventorySlotHandle(...), writer fence vault.TryAcquireWriteLock(in handle, SystemID.Power, out slots), and authoritative slot write after acquired view. old coldSlotWriteLocksBeforeResolve field is now backed by this descriptor-route proof.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping old token proof was rejected because it described route that no longer exists. Removing field was rejected because downstream audit history already consumes coldSlotWriteLocksBeforeResolve. loose search for any TryAcquireWriteLock was rejected because it could pass on unrelated Vault lane and would not prove inventory owner fence.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra runtime behavior is unchanged. patch affects only editor/static evidence. actual cold facade slot write already uses owner-local inventory descriptor locking; continuous charger cadence, DTO layout, save identity, BufferID identity, and GPU LED Dear Lie are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Hot path cost remains 0 us changed. Static proof cost is editor-only O(source bytes). gain is audit integrity: scanner now verifies generation-handle write fence actually used by runtime instead of preserving stale legacy evidence.
Decision 66 - Runtime Admission And Scanner Truth
Problem: report carried false PASS despite two facts scanner already knew were outside SHINOBU ownership: concrete facade residual imports and Inventory Routing whole-slot writers on BufferID.ShinobuInventorySlots. runtime also consumed authorityAccumulator before job admission, so failed lock or buffer resolve could erase charge authority without executing job. DTO write paths still allowed NaN via math.max, and telemetry named schedule-to-finalize wall-time value BurstMicroseconds.
Solution: Changed SHINOBU230 report verdict to PARTIALBLOCKEDBYCROSSDOMAINOWNER and preserved two owner-boundary findings. Moved accumulator subtraction after buffer resolution and linkCount 0, while clearing local accumulator when no active links exist so future inserted battery cannot receive idle back-credit. Added finite sanitizers for charger AUP, charge rate, efficiency scalar, max charge rate, efficiency exponent, and quality override before DTO writes. Renamed telemetry field to FenceElapsedMicroseconds@28, renamed threshold to FaultDumpFenceElapsedThresholdMicroseconds, updated layout audit, X-Ray label, scanner gates, and ledger. fault dump route is now explicitly documented as blocking fault-only exception for NaN or fence-elapsed breach.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping PASS verdict was rejected because machine-readable proof must not hide cross-domain blockers. Subtracting authority before buffer admission was rejected because it silently loses deterministic charge time on contention. Adding catch-up loop was rejected because it would create same-frame job pressure and violate dispatcher-owned completion windows. Keeping BurstMicroseconds was rejected because it mislabels wall time and corrupts profiler interpretation. Sending fault dumps through new background managed queue was rejected for this loop because route is crash/fault-only and synchronous exception is now documented instead of being used in healthy frames.
Scalability potential: Low-tier devices still shed work continuously through math.smoothstep and math.lerp(5f,60f,q). Below 0.3, fewer charge batches are admitted, but authority time is consumed only when real batch exists and DTO identity is unchanged. Middle/high/ultra keep same 60 Hz upper cadence, GPU LED StructuredBuffer Dear Lie, and acoustic signal route. No binary quality switch was added.
Hardware Impact: Hot Burst charge kernel cost remains 0 us changed. admitted scheduler path keeps one scalar subtraction; failed lock/resolve paths no longer lose authority. Finite guards are cold registration/tuning path only. practical gain is NaN prevention, conservation under contention, and honest telemetry naming without extra Vault buffers or cache-line growth.
Decision 67 - Owned Surface Mandate Sweep
Problem: After admission and telemetry patch, next risk was not known failing line but mandate drift: hidden .Complete(), Pack=1, private native allocation, LINQ/foreach, frame delta, unmanaged property use, or sibling runtime references could have entered SHINOBU230 surface while patches accumulated across loops.
Solution: Ran scoped owned-file grep over battery charger logistics runtime/contracts/editor bridge/facade files instead of whole-repo scan. owned surface has no Pack=1, hidden .Complete(), private native collection allocation, foreach, LINQ, UnityEngine.Random, Time.deltaTime, or hot-path auto-property pattern hits. Re-checked Burst jobs: all three jobs use CompileSynchronously=true, FloatMode.Deterministic, FloatPrecision.Standard; distinct arrays/raw pointers carry NoAlias. Re-checked asmdefs: runtime references Core/Core.Contracts/Core.Memory and Unity packages only, not sibling Gameplay/Construction/Inventory/World/Generators runtime assemblies. Continuous quality remains math.smoothstep plus math.lerp(5f,60f,q).
Rejected Alternatives: broad repo grep was rejected as primary proof because this worktree is shared and many hits belong to other agents/domains. Adding direct references to cross-domain owners was rejected because it would solve scanner findings by breaking compile wall. Running rebuild was rejected because CPU was at 100% and external scanner projection source/meta are still absent.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra behavior remains same as Loop 50: continuous cadence scales work, DTO identity does not change, and GPU LED Dear Lie is still visual path. sweep did not add work; it proved no hidden hot-path regression entered owned surface.
Hardware Impact: Runtime delta is 0 us. value is risk reduction: no new GC patterns, no hidden job fences, no alignment hazards, and no new sibling assembly route on owned files.
Source lines scanned 821; unique retained 408.

Rationale_SHINOBU_231.md
RationaleSHINOBU231
Date: 2026-05-20
Status: PENDING VERIFICATION
Agent: SHINOBU231
Problem: Upgrade stat evaluation request crosses equipment, vehicles, inventory, DataVault, visual sync, and telemetry. Direct concrete dependencies on unfinished agents would create compile walls.
Solution: Start with owner-local unmanaged DTOs/jobs and adapters that can be wired to Vault buffers later. Use GlobalDataVault only where existing interfaces are found; otherwise expose unmanaged kernels without inventing global surface.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct GlobalRegistry polling for PlayerInventory or vehicle components in evaluation loop. This violates hot-path global authority law and creates branchy concrete coupling.
Scalability potential: Low uses same deterministic bitwise truth at minimum cost; Middle runs full gameplay truth at normal cadence; High/Ultra spend saved time in VISUALSYNC through shader flags/glow/extrusion, not heavier simulation.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 gain depends on existing branch/OOP debt. Expected static target is eliminating virtual calls and string/list checks from stat loops; measured proof absent.
Problem: Upgrade mask layout requires ARM64-safe 64-bit reads.
Solution: Define UpgradeMaskDTO as StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit, Size = 16) with EntityHashID offset 0, EquipmentHashID offset 4, ActiveUpgradesMask offset 8.
Rejected Alternatives: Default sequential layout or StructLayout(Pack=1). Sequential may drift under future edits; Pack=1 is banned for runtime DTOs with 8-byte fields.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all use same deterministic truth; presentation richness is decoupled through visual bits.
Hardware Impact: Prevents ARM64 misaligned ulong load traps and cache penalties; estimated prevention value is structural, not claimed measured microsecond delta.
Problem: Complex upgrades such as depth modules do not stack linearly.
Solution: Cold-build flat LUTs for narrow bit groups and read them O(1) in hot job. Use bit extraction and shifts to form LUT indices.
Rejected Alternatives: Sequential if/else priority chains and polymorphic ApplyModifier(ref stats) methods. Both create branch/dispatch cost and hardcoded behavior spread.
Scalability potential: Low uses same LUT; Ultra can add visual flag richness without changing survival truth.
Hardware Impact: Replaces unpredictable branches with linear memory reads; expected low-end gain is branch predictor stability and better Burst vectorization. Measured proof absent.

Rejected Alternatives: Casting absolute coordinates to float before subtracting origin. This loses precision at long range and breaks 50km sampling.

Hardware Impact: Prevents precision bugs rather than raw CPU savings. Low-end cost is bounded by branchless mask gate.

Route Card: SHINOBU231UPGRADEMATRIXVAULT
Owner: SHINOBU231 / TOOLUPGRADEMATRIXCOMPILER.
Phase: PRESIMULATION sync, SIMULATION evaluate/publish, POSTSIMULATION telemetry, VISUALSYNC visual flags.
Buffers: 71380 UpgradeMasks, 71381 BaseStats, 71382 CompiledStats, 71383 Lut, 71384 Rules, 71385 TelemetryRing, 71386 TelemetryCursor, 71387 InventorySlots, 71388 ItemMap, 71389 VisualStates, 71410 ToolModuleRules.
Disposition: YELLOW until Unity compile, Burst Inspector, scheduler wiring, and profiler timing prove route live.
Problem: EvaluateUpgradeMasksJob used AupPrecisionMath.DowncastLocalDelta, which performs branch guards inside shared helper. AUP order was correct, but hot job proof was not strictly branchless.
Solution: Keep AupPrecisionMath.LocalDeltaDouble for mandatory double-domain subtraction, then perform float cast locally and select float3.zero with math.select when either double or float lanes are non-finite.
Rejected Alternatives: Calling general AUP helper from per-entity stat compiler. helper is valid in other domains, but its if guards weaken no-branch proof for this matrix kernel.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all keep identical survival truth; visual richness remains only quality-scaled lane.
Hardware Impact: Low-end i3/MX350 saves small branch cost and removes predictor noise from 10k-row evaluation. Estimate: 1-3 us/10k rows; Unity profiler proof pending.
Problem: VISUALSYNC was represented as raw uint flag buffer, which could not carry continuous quality, shader extrusion, or glow intensity without additional state.
Solution: Replace Vault visual lane with UpgradeVisualStateDTO64 and add PublishUpgradeVisualStateJob. job writes mask hash, entity/equipment IDs, visual flags, GlobalQualityWeight, smooth intensity, extrusion scale, and glow scalar.
Rejected Alternatives: Runtime mesh instantiation, GameObject fin/armor toggles, or raw uint only. These either spike CPU or force later systems to invent shadow quality state.
Scalability potential: Low = flags plus near-zero smooth intensity; Middle = moderate glow/extrusion; High = full shader-driven visual overkill; Ultra = same CPU route with richer shader interpretation.
Hardware Impact: Avoids millisecond-scale managed mesh/object churn. Per-entity write is 64 bytes and false-sharing resistant.
Problem: BuildUpgradeLUTJob.ApplyRule still contained switch lane dispatcher inside Burst math job.
Solution: Replace switch with twelve lane delta masks and straight-line multiplier/additive updates.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cold switch because it is not per-frame. That is acceptable for runtime cost, but weak for strict matrix compiler audit.
Scalability potential: All tiers use same precomputed LUT. Saved cold-boot cycles are minor; main value is deterministic branchless rule baking.
Hardware Impact: Cold boot only; removes branch table risk when generating matrices on weak devices.
Problem: Submarine transport stat resolvers still used branchy if ((mask & bit) != 0) chains for thrust, turn speed, depth, and integrity.
Solution: Convert installed item hashes with math.select into VehicleUpgradeBits, then resolve each stat using bit-extracted 0/1 scalars and multiplier/additive math.
Rejected Alternatives: Depending directly on Tools namespace from transport file. local bit helper avoids cross-domain compile-wall coupling while preserving same 64-bit mask pattern.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all resolve same vehicle truth; later visual response can read UpgradeVisualStateDTO without changing transport physics.
Hardware Impact: Removes branch predictor work from repeated transport stat queries. Estimate: 2-8 us/transport stat refresh depending call rate; compile/profiler proof pending.
Problem: Tool runtime DTOs used sequential layout, and only explicit tool stat compile route was managed ToolModuleData cold loop.
Solution: Convert ToolState, ToolRuntimeProfile, and ToolRuntimeStats to explicit field offsets with unchanged sizes, and add CompileToolRuntimeStatsJob so LUT-compiled vectors can be projected into ToolRuntimeStats in Burst.
Rejected Alternatives: Changing hot array element sizes to 64 bytes without integration mandate. That would break existing ModularEquipmentEngine size assertions and inflate memory bandwidth.
Scalability potential: Low uses same 40-byte stat rows; Middle/High/Ultra increase visual/state richness through separate buffers, not by bloating tool stats.
Hardware Impact: ARM64 layout becomes auditable; Burst route avoids managed multiplier loops once dispatcher wiring lands. Estimate: 4-12 us/fleet pass when wired.

Problem: New tool rule DTOs need explicit ARM64 layout proof.

Rejected Alternatives: Sequential DTO layout or packing tool multipliers into loosely related arrays. Sequential layout risks future drift; parallel arrays complicate ownership and alias proof.

Rationale_SHINOBU_232.md
RationaleSHINOBU232
Status: LOOP 43 TELEMETRYFLAGSEMANTICS - STATIC VERIFIED / BUILD GUARD BLOCKED
Current Supersession Ledger
Decision 52 supersedes Decision 34 for Burst float mode: caustic pointer kernels are deterministic, not Fast.
Decision 55 supersedes Decision 33/54 for legacy caustics service accessors: ICausticsService is identity-only.
Decision 56 supersedes Decision 4/33/54 for weather and wave inputs: SHINOBU reads Core IWeatherService.GetRuntimeSnapshot() plus optional ShinobuOceanSurfaceSwell, not Atmosphere DTO rows.
Decision 57 supersedes old weather/wave telemetry flag names: FlagWeatherSnapshotBound and FlagWaveInputBound are current; no WeatherVaultBound or WaveVaultBound flag name remains in source.
Decision 0 - Scope Boundary
Problem: Caustic lighting task spans rendering, voxel SDF visibility, ocean phase, and quality scaling while 20+ agents may edit neighboring systems.
Solution: Keep implementation in first-party rendering domain and use existing registry/vault/shader interfaces when present; otherwise provide owner-local fallback state without hard dependencies on unfinished agents.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct coupling to Celestial/Ocean/Voxel concrete classes because batch protocol forbids invented dependencies.
Scalability potential: Low uses one cheap monochrome Voronoi layer and shallow depth cutoff; Middle adds smoother panning; High adds dual-layer chroma; Ultra spends saved projector passes on richer distortion.
Hardware Impact: MX350/i3 avoids projector geometry re-render and light cookie passes; expected saving is from removed extra passes, not CPU claims until Unity profiling exists.
Decision 1 - Task Count
Problem: Initial regex undercounted tasks because task lines are text labels, not XML task tags.
Solution: Treat Task 01 through Task 20 in extracted XML as authoritative count.
Rejected Alternatives: Counting XML phase tags or self-reflection questions as tasks.
Scalability potential: Correct loop scheduling prevents skipped quality tiers and verification.
Hardware Impact: No runtime impact.
Decision 2 - Legacy Projector/RT Cut
Problem: Existing AnalyticalCausticsService could allocate 512 RenderTexture and dispatch compute caustic map, preserving expensive projector/cookie era through texture indirection.
Solution: Bootstrap now prefers AbyssalDeferredCausticsRuntime and legacy service no-ops RenderTexture creation, compute dispatch, and texture publication. active path is fullscreen RenderGraph pass reading camera color and depth handles.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping 512 caustic map as intermediate because it preserves CPU/GPU sync risk and VRAM churn.
Scalability potential: Low skips old map entirely and culls by depth; Middle keeps one procedural layer; High/Ultra spend saved pass on second Voronoi and chroma.
Hardware Impact: MX350/i3 avoids one caustic map allocation path and any geometry/projector-style redraw. Exact profiler value pending Unity run; engineering estimate is 220 us/frame risk removed.
Decision 3 - 64B Vault DTO and Constant Buffer
Problem: Shader globals as many SetGlobalVector/Float calls create API lookup overhead and make ARM64 constant layout fragile.
Solution: CausticsParametersDTO is explicit 64 bytes: ProjectionVectorAndScale at 0, NoiseAnimationSpeed at 16, IntensityAndDepthFalloff at 32, QualityAndColor at 48. Runtime writes Vault NativeArray memory through UnsafeUtility.AsRef and uploads through double-buffered GraphicsBuffer.Target.Constant using LockBufferForWrite and UnsafeUtility.MemCpy.
Rejected Alternatives: Managed properties, MaterialPropertyBlock, or ad hoc Shader.SetGlobalFloat fields because they create copies and dictionary/API churn.
